definition_zh: 古生物学家；从事化石发掘与研究者；博物馆古生物部门的研究或策展人员
definition_en: a person who studies ancient life through fossils, whether in the field, a museum or a laboratory
core_image: 野外营地里，研究者蹲在碎石堆前，用镊子夹起一颗牙齿化石放进编号袋
scene: 野外营地里，一位研究者蹲在碎石堆中，用镊子夹起一颗牙齿化石放进编号袋。 The paleontologist brushed sand from a tooth before it could crack.
sceneCN: 这里 paleontologist 指「从事古生物研究的专业人员」（第 1 个义项：以化石研究远古生命的学者）；句意为这位古生物学家在一颗牙齿开裂之前把沙刷掉。图中可辨识物件：碎石堆、镊子、牙齿化石、编号袋、记录本。

pos.zh: 古生物学家；古生物研究者；古生物部门的研究或策展人员

collocations.zh: 古生物学家用的地质锤

senses.title: A specialist in ancient life
senses.titleCN: 研究远古生命的专业学者
senses.definition: a scientist who studies extinct organisms and their environments through fossil evidence
senses.definitionCN: 通过化石证据研究已灭绝生物及其环境的科学家
senses.example: The paleontologist compared the jaw with three museum specimens.
senses.exampleCN: 这位古生物学家把这件下颌与三件馆藏标本作了比较。
senses.why: the agent suffix -ist marks the person, while the discipline noun marks the field, so the pair is strictly complementary.
senses.whyCN: 施事后缀 -ist 标出人，学科名词标出领域，两者严格互补。

senses.title: A field collector
senses.definition: a person who finds, excavates and records fossils at outcrops and quarries
senses.definitionCN: 在露头与采石场寻找、发掘并记录化石的人
senses.example: The paleontologist spent six weeks mapping the quarry before digging.
senses.exampleCN: 这位古生物学家在动土前花了六周测绘采坑。
senses.why: fieldwork is a distinct role within the profession, and the same title covers the person holding the trowel.
senses.whyCN: 野外工作是这一行中独立的角色，同一个头衔也指拿着小铲的人。

senses.title: A museum curator or researcher
senses.titleCN: 博物馆的古生物研究或策展人员
senses.definition: a specialist employed by a museum to care for, study and display fossil collections
senses.definitionCN: 受雇于博物馆，负责保管、研究与展示化石藏品的人员
senses.example: The paleontologist rehoused the type specimens in acid-free trays.
senses.exampleCN: 这位古生物学家把模式标本改放到无酸托盘里。
senses.why: institutions use the title for curatorial work, which is research plus stewardship rather than excavation.
senses.whyCN: 机构用这个头衔指策展工作，即研究加上保管，而非发掘。

senses.title: A university researcher
senses.definition: an academic who teaches the subject and runs a research programme on fossil material
senses.definitionCN: 教授该学科并就化石材料主持研究项目的学者
senses.example: The paleontologist supervised two doctoral students on the project.
senses.exampleCN: 这位古生物学家在该项目上指导两名博士生。
senses.why: the title attaches to a post as much as to a person, so it appears in staffing lists and grant applications.
senses.whyCN: 这个头衔既属于人也属于职位，因此出现在人员名单与经费申请中。

senses.title: A consultant on stratigraphy
senses.titleCN: 为地层工作提供咨询的专家
senses.definition: a specialist called in to identify fossils so that a rock unit can be dated or correlated
senses.definitionCN: 被请来鉴定化石，以便给岩层定年或对比的专家
senses.example: The paleontologist identified the graptolites that fixed the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 这位古生物学家鉴定了确定该阶的笔石。
senses.why: industry and survey work employ the title for a service role, where the fossil is evidence rather than an object of wonder.
senses.whyCN: 工业与地质调查用这个头衔指服务性角色，此时化石是证据而非观赏对象。

senses.title: An amateur specialist
senses.definition: an informed non-professional who collects and studies fossils seriously outside paid employment
senses.definitionCN: 在职业之外认真采集与研究化石的非专业者
senses.example: An amateur paleontologist found the site while walking a new road cut.
senses.exampleCN: 一位业余古生物研究者在查看新开的公路切面时发现了这个地点。
senses.why: the qualification here is knowledge and practice, not salary, which is why the same noun serves both worlds.
senses.whyCN: 这里的资格是知识与实践，而非薪俸，因此同一名词服务于两个世界。

senses.title: A science communicator
senses.titleCN: 从事科普的古生物学者
senses.definition: a specialist who explains fossil research to the public through writing, media or museum tours
senses.definitionCN: 通过写作、媒体或博物馆导览向公众解释化石研究的专家
senses.example: As a paleontologist, she writes as carefully for children as for journals.
senses.exampleCN: 作为古生物学家，她为儿童写作和为期刊写作一样用心。
senses.why: public-facing work has become part of the role, so the title now covers speaking as well as studying.
senses.whyCN: 面向公众的工作已成为角色的一部分，因此这个头衔也涵盖讲述，而不仅是研究。

senses.title: A named branch specialist
senses.titleCN: 某一分支的古生物学家
senses.definition: a specialist identified by the group studied, as in vertebrate paleontologist or palynologist
senses.definitionCN: 以所研究类群来限定的专家，如脊椎动物古生物学家或孢粉学家
senses.example: The vertebrate paleontologist joined the excavation for one season.
senses.exampleCN: 这位脊椎动物古生物学家参加了一季的发掘。
senses.why: branch names combine with the person noun, so the title scales from the whole field down to a single group.
senses.whyCN: 分支名与人物名词组合，使头衔可以从整个领域细到单一类群。

intro.en: Paleontologist is paleontology plus the agent suffix -ist, from Greek -istēs. The discipline name was coined in the early nineteenth century; the personal noun followed immediately. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: paleontologist 是 paleontology 加施事后缀 -ist（源自希腊 -istēs）。学科名于十九世纪初造出，人物名词紧随其后。年代均为约数。

items.en: Paleontology joins palaios 'old', onta 'beings' and -logia 'study'; the discipline name was assembled in the early nineteenth century.
items.cn: paleontology 由 palaios「古老」、onta「存在者」与 -logia「研究」组合；学科名于十九世纪初拼成。

items.en: -ist comes from Greek -istēs, a suffix of persons who practise or adhere to something, as in botanist and geologist.
items.cn: -ist 来自希腊 -istēs，指从事或信奉某事的人，如 botanist 与 geologist。

items.en: Once the field had a name, its practitioner was formed by adding -ist, and both spellings palaeo- and paleo- carry the pair.
items.cn: 领域一有名称，从业者便通过加 -ist 构成，palaeo- 与 paleo- 两种拼写都带这一对词。

items.en: As museums and universities created posts in the nineteenth century, the title became an office as well as a description.
items.cn: 随着博物馆与大学在十九世纪设立岗位，这个头衔既成描述也成职位。

items.en: Twentieth-century practice extended the title to amateurs and communicators who publish serious work without a salary.
items.cn: 二十世纪的实践把这个头衔扩展到无薪却发表严肃工作的业余者与科普者。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dating only): the suffix and stems are secure, but the earliest use of the personal noun is dated approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：后缀与词干确定，但人物名词的最早使用只能约略定年。

note.en: Group one separates the person noun from the field and from look-alike titles; group two separates it from neighbouring professions.
note.cn: 第一组把人物名词与学科名及形近头衔分开；第二组区分它与相邻职业。

entries.definition: The discipline; the person noun differs only by the agent suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 学科；人物名词只差一个施事后缀。

entries.definition: The same profession written with ae, standard in British usage.
entries.definitionCN: 同一职业，用 ae 拼写，通行于英国。

entries.definition: A specialist in ancient humans only; the wider title covers all extinct life.
entries.definitionCN: 只研究远古人类的专家；较宽的头衔涵盖一切已灭绝生命。

entries.definition: A specialist in fossil plants; the wider title does not require plants.
entries.definitionCN: 研究化石植物的专家；较宽的头衔并不限于植物。

entries.definition: A specialist in past human societies through material traces; the two trades overlap at sites but differ in object.
entries.definitionCN: 通过物质遗存研究过去人类社会的专家；两者在遗址上交叉，但对象不同。

entries.definition: A specialist in rocks and earth history; fossils are one kind of evidence among many.
entries.definitionCN: 研究岩石与地球历史的专家；化石只是众多证据之一。

entries.definition: Someone who gathers fossils, often without publishing; the title implies study, not just acquisition.
entries.definitionCN: 采集化石的人，常常并不发表；后者含研究之意，不只是收集。

entries.definition: A person responsible for a collection; a paleontologist may be one, but curation is the duty, not the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 负责藏品的人；古生物学家可以担任，但策展是职责，而非学科。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: paleontology + -ist: the person who practises the study of ancient beings.
normal.cn: paleontology + -ist：从事远古存在者研究的人。

normal.en: The title pairs with the field noun exactly: paleontology/paleontologist.
normal.cn: 这个头衔与学科名词严格配对：paleontology/paleontologist。

normal.en: British spelling doubles the vowel: palaeontologist.
normal.cn: 英式拼写多一个元音：palaeontologist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: field paleontologist, museum paleontologist, vertebrate paleontologist.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：野外古生物学家、博物馆古生物学家、脊椎动物古生物学家。

normal.en: Compare archaeologist and geologist: same site, different object.
normal.cn: 比较 archaeologist 与 geologist：同一遗址，不同对象。

abstract.cn: 想象一个人跪在尘土里，拿着刷子和编号袋。

abstract.en: Picture a jaw on a table with three labels around it and a lamp overhead.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上放着一件下颌，周围三个标签，头顶一盏灯。

abstract.en: Picture a child on a museum floor asking a patient expert why the bone is heavy.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子坐在博物馆地上，问一位耐心的专家骨头为什么这么重。

examples.en: The paleontologist published the jaw as a new genus.
examples.cn: 这位古生物学家把这件下颌发表为一个新属。

examples.en: Two paleontologists spent the winter preparing the slab.
examples.cn: 两位古生物学家花了一个冬天修整这块板岩。

examples.en: As a paleontologist, he refused to identify the bone from a photograph.
examples.cn: 作为古生物学家，他拒绝仅凭照片鉴定这块骨头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「paleonto（古生物）+ logist（学者）」——研究古生物的学者 → 古生物学家

root: paleontology（希腊 palaios「古老」+ onta「存在者」+ -logia「研究」）+ 施事后缀 -ist（希腊 -istēs）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses describe one person in different hats: specialist, digger, curator, academic, consultant, amateur, explainer and branch expert.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描写同一个人戴的不同帽子：专家、发掘者、策展人、学者、顾问、业余者、讲述者与分支专家。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone kneeling in dust with a brush, a bag and a label.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人跪在尘土中，身边是刷子、袋子和标签。

branches.en: THE PERSON AT WORK: the title covers both the specialist and the trowel.
branches.cn: 工作中的这个人：头衔兼指专家与拿小铲的人。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL HATS: museum stewardship and academic posts.
branches.cn: 机构中的帽子：博物馆保管与大学教职。

branches.en: SERVICE ROLE: identifying fossils so that rock can be dated.
branches.cn: 服务角色：鉴定化石以便给岩层定年。

branches.en: BEYOND SALARY: amateurs and public explainers practise the same trade.
branches.cn: 薪俸之外：业余者与科普者从事同一行当。

branches.en: NAMED SPECIALITY: the title narrows to a group, as in vertebrate paleontologist.
branches.cn: 命名的专长：头衔可窄到某一类群，如脊椎动物古生物学家。

intro.en: Paleontologist is the field noun plus the Greek agent suffix -ist, so the whole word unpacks as the person of the discipline.
intro.cn: paleontologist 是学科名词加希腊施事后缀 -ist，整词可解作「该学科的人」。

latinIntro.en: Greek palaios, onta and -logia supply the field; -istēs, through -ist, supplies the person. Latin has no part in the word.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 palaios、onta 与 -logia 提供领域义；-istēs 经 -ist 提供人物义。拉丁语不参与此词构成。

definition_zh: v. 把…嵌入；使深留脑中；埋入；栽种；派驻（记者）
definition_en: to fix something firmly into a surrounding mass or deeply in the mind
core_image: 一枚芯片被压进透明树脂里，树脂凝住后芯片悬在正中，四周没有一丝缝隙
scene: 工人把一枚芯片按进尚未凝固的透明树脂，等树脂硬透，芯片就悬在正中，四周没有一丝缝隙。 The chip was embedded in a block of clear resin.
sceneCN: 这里 embed 指「嵌入」（第 1 个义项：牢牢固定于周围材料中，此处用被动）；句意是芯片被嵌在一块透明树脂里。

pos.zh: 把…嵌入；使深留脑中；埋入；派驻

senses.title: To fix in a surrounding mass
senses.definition: to fix something firmly into a surrounding material
senses.definitionCN: （动词）把某物牢牢固定进周围的材料中
senses.example: The chip was embedded in a block of clear resin.
senses.exampleCN: 芯片被嵌在一块透明树脂里。
senses.why: A chip pressed into clear resin that hardens around it without a gap
senses.whyCN: 芯片被压进透明树脂，树脂在它四周硬透，不留一丝缝隙

senses.title: To fix deeply in the mind
senses.definition: to fix an idea or memory deeply in the mind
senses.definitionCN: （动词）把想法或记忆深深固定在脑中
senses.example: The warning was embedded in her mind by a single accident.
senses.exampleCN: 一次事故就把那句警告深深刻进了她心里。
senses.why: A phrase repeated until it lies down in the memory and stays
senses.whyCN: 一句话反复念，直到它在记忆里躺下来不走了

senses.title: To attach a reporter to a unit
senses.definition: to attach a journalist to a military unit for reporting
senses.definitionCN: （动词）把记者编入部队随队采访
senses.example: Two reporters were embedded with the unit for a month.
senses.exampleCN: 两名记者随该部队采访了一个月。
senses.why: A reporter sitting in a truck beside soldiers with a notebook on the knee
senses.whyCN: 记者坐在军车里的士兵旁边，膝上摊着笔记本

intro.en: Embed is em- plus bed, from Old English bedd; to embed is to put a thing into a bed, the soft place that holds it.
intro.cn: embed 由 em- 加 bed 组成，bed 来自古英语 bedd；embed 就是把东西放进一张床里，放进那个托住它的软处。

items.en: Bedd means a resting place, and gives English bed.
items.cn: bedd 意为安卧之处，给出英语 bed。

items.en: Bedde extends to the bottom of a river and the base of a wall.
items.cn: bedde 扩展到河床与墙基。

items.en: Embed appears in the 1590s, meaning to lay a thing in a surrounding bed.
items.cn: embed 出现于 16 世纪 90 年代，意为把东西安放在周围的床层中。

items.en: Embedded becomes common in geology for fossils held in rock.
items.cn: embedded 在地质学中常用，指岩层中包裹的化石。

items.en: Engineering uses embed for fixing a component inside a material.
items.cn: 工程学用 embed 指把元件固定在材料内部。

items.en: Journalists are embedded with military units, and the word enters daily news.
items.cn: 记者被派驻随军，这个词进入日常新闻。

note.en: Embed, bed and bedding share the Germanic root bedd, a resting place; implant and ingrain are the nearest synonyms.
note.cn: embed、bed 与 bedding 共享日耳曼词根 bedd（安卧之处）；implant 与 ingrain 是最接近的同义词。

dict_mnemonic.text: embed ＝ em-（使进入）＋ bed（床；基座，古英语 bedd）＝「放进一张床里托住」。三单 embeds，过去式与过去分词 embedded，现在分词 embedding；名词 embedment 嵌入、埋置，embeddedness 嵌入性；同族 bed 床、河床，bedding 垫层、床上用品。三类用法：嵌入材料 embed in concrete 嵌在混凝土里、embed a chip 嵌入芯片、a fossil embedded in rock 嵌在岩石里的化石；深留脑中 deeply embedded 根深蒂固的、embedded in the mind 深印在心里；派驻记者 embed a journalist 派驻记者、embedded with the unit 随部队采访。栽种也说 embed bulbs in soil 把鳞茎埋进土里。近义 implant 侧重植入体内，ingrain 侧重习惯信念的固化，insert 只是放进去，不一定固定；embed 强调被周围材料牢牢托住。

branches.en: A thought held inside the memory.
branches.cn: 想法被托在记忆内部。

branches.cn: 记者被安放在部队之中。

branches.cn: 两者都被固定住，掉不出来。

branches.en: Both put a thing into a surrounding body.
branches.cn: 两者都把东西放进一个包围它的整体。

intro.cn: embed 由 em- 加 bed 组成；-ment 给出 embedment，-ing 给出 bedding，em- 也给出 embark 与 embargo。

latinIntro.en: The root bed is Germanic, from Old English bedd; only the prefix em- comes from Latin in-, so embed is a mixed English and Latin formation.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 bed 是日耳曼语，来自古英语 bedd；只有前缀 em- 来自拉丁语 in-，所以 embed 是英语与拉丁语的混合构词。

definition_zh: 注释；作注解；评注
definition_en: to add explanatory notes to a text or diagram
core_image: 在书页边缘写下小字：为正文点灯
scene: 图书馆里，研究生在旧书页边写下小字。 Students annotate their textbooks with questions and explanations.
sceneCN: 这里 annotate 是「注释」（第 1 个义项：为文本添加说明性批注）；句意为：学生们在教科书上写下问题和解释作为批注。

pos.zh: 注释；为……作注解
作注解；写批注

derivatives.zh: annotate 的名词形式，义为「注释；批注」
annotate 的过去分词形容词，义为「有注释的」

senses.title: To add explanatory notes to a text
senses.definition: to add notes that explain or comment on a written work
senses.definitionCN: 为书面作品添加解释性或评论性批注
senses.example: The editor annotated the letter with dates and names.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑为信件添加了日期与人名的注释。
senses.why: The Latin notare means to mark, and a note is a mark made beside the text.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 notare 意为「作标记」，note 即写在正文之旁的标记。

senses.title: To supply critical commentary
senses.definition: to add notes that judge or interpret, not merely explain
senses.definitionCN: 添加具评判或阐释性质而非仅说明的批注
senses.example: Scholars annotated the poem with competing interpretations.
senses.exampleCN: 学者们以相互竞争的解读为这首诗作评注。
senses.why: Marks beside a text grow from glosses into arguments.
senses.whyCN: 写在旁边的标记从「释义」成长为「论辩」。

senses.title: To label a diagram or dataset
senses.definition: to add labels or descriptions to images, maps, or data
senses.definitionCN: 为图像、地图或数据添加标签或说明
senses.example: The team annotated the X-rays before the review.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在会诊前为 X 光片加了标注。
senses.why: The page expands to any surface where marks explain content.
senses.whyCN: 「页面」扩展到一切可加注说明的表面。

senses.title: To mark up for a machine (computing)
senses.definition: to tag data with labels for training or analysis
senses.definitionCN: 为训练或分析给数据打标签
senses.example: Volunteers annotated thousands of street photos.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者为数千张街景照片做了标注。
senses.why: The old marginal mark becomes a digital label.
senses.whyCN: 古老的页边标记变成了数字标签。

senses.title: To furnish a text with apparatus
senses.definition: to prepare a scholarly edition with notes, sources, and cross-references
senses.definitionCN: 编订附有注释、出处与互见的学术版本
senses.example: She spent a decade annotating the medieval manuscript.
senses.exampleCN: 她花了十年为这部中世纪手稿作注。
senses.why: Notes accumulate into a whole scholarly apparatus around the old text.
senses.whyCN: 注释累积为围绕古文本的整套学术 apparatus。

senses.title: To annotate on or upon: to comment at large
senses.definition: to comment on or discuss a subject at length (older use)
senses.definitionCN: 对某题作长篇评论（旧式用法）
senses.example: Early writers annotated on the classics at book length.
senses.exampleCN: 早期作家以整本书的篇幅评述经典。
senses.why: When notes are spoken aloud, they become commentary.
senses.whyCN: 当注释被大声说出，便成为评论。

senses.title: To record observations alongside events
senses.definition: to add running notes to a log, timeline, or record
senses.definitionCN: 在日志、时间线或记录旁添加随行批注
senses.example: The pilot annotated the flight log with weather remarks.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员在飞行日志上添加了天气备注。
senses.why: Every official record admits marginal remarks from experience.
senses.whyCN: 一切正式记录都容纳来自经验的页边备注。

senses.title: To annotate oneself: to be marked by traces
senses.definition: to bear marks or traces that need explaining
senses.definitionCN: 带有需要解释的痕迹或标记
senses.example: The map annotated itself with every route the caravan took.
senses.exampleCN: 商队走过的每条路线都在地图上留下了标记。
senses.why: The direction of noting can reverse: the world marks us back.
senses.whyCN: 「作注」的方向可以反转：世界也会反过来标记我们。

intro.en: Annotate is built openly from Latin parts: to note upon, to make a mark against a text.
intro.cn: annotate 由拉丁部件透明构成：在文本之上作标记，即「加注」。

items.en: The root *ǵneh₃- meant to know, the same root that gives know and cognition.
items.cn: 印欧词根 *ǵneh₃- 意为「知道」，与 know、cognition 同根，一般认为。

items.en: Noscere meant to know; notare meant to mark, from nota, a mark or sign.
items.cn: 拉丁语 noscere 意为「知道」；notare 意为「作标记」，出自 nota（标记、符号）。

items.en: Adnotare combined ad (to) and notare, meaning to note down about a thing.
items.cn: 后拉丁语 adnotare 由 ad（对）加 notare 构成，义为「就某事作记录」。

items.en: English adopted annotate in the early seventeenth century for scholarly glossing.
items.cn: 英语于十七世纪初借入 annotate，用于学术注释。

items.en: The verb now spans manuscripts, diagrams, logs, and machine-learning datasets.
items.cn: 如今该动词覆盖手稿、图表、日志与机器学习数据集。

note.en: The groups below separate same-root forms from nearby words of marking and commenting.
note.cn: 以下分「同根词」与「标记、评论近义词」两组。

entries.definitionCN: 注释；批注，annotate 的名词形式，同根

entries.definition: to put into notation, especially music
entries.definitionCN: 以记号记录（尤指乐谱），共享 nota 词根

entries.definition: to indicate or mean
entries.definitionCN: 表示；意指，同出 nota 词根

entries.definition: to add a brief explanatory note
entries.definitionCN: 作简短注释，传统语文学用语

entries.definition: to remark on or discuss
entries.definitionCN: 评论；评述，口语化近义

entries.definition: to attach an explanatory label, especially to images
entries.definitionCN: 为图像加说明文字，偏图片场景

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin nota root and its large English family.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆钩子基于真实的拉丁 nota 词根及其庞大的英语词族。

normal.en: ad (to) + notare (to mark) = to mark against a text: annotate.
normal.cn: ad（对）+ notare（标记）= 在文本旁作标记：即 annotate。

normal.en: Same nota family: note, notation, denote, notion.
normal.cn: 同属 nota 词族：note、notation、denote、notion。

normal.en: An annotated bibliography lists sources with descriptions.
normal.cn: annotated bibliography 指附说明的参考书目。

normal.en: A heavily annotated book is dense with marginal notes.
normal.cn: heavily annotated 的书写满页边批注。

normal.en: In computing, to annotate data means to label it.
normal.cn: 在计算机领域，annotate data 意为给数据打标签。

abstract.en: Picture a pencil hovering over a yellowed margin, about to write.
abstract.cn: 想象一支铅笔悬在发黄的页边，正要落笔。

abstract.en: See sticky flags blooming along the edge of a thick report.
abstract.cn: 想象厚报告的书口开出一片彩色标签。

abstract.en: Feel the satisfaction of a question answered in the very margin where it arose.
abstract.cn: 感受疑问在其出现的那一页边被解答的满足感。

examples.cn: 请在周五研讨课前为选段作注。

examples.en: Her annotated translation became the standard edition.

examples.en: The geologists annotated the aerial photos with fault lines.
examples.cn: 地质学家在航拍照片上标注了断层线。

definition_zh: 农业社会；以土地占有与农耕关系为基础组织的社会
definition_en: a society organized around land ownership and the farming order built on it
core_image: 地契、界石、犁与谷仓构成一幅以土地为骨架的村庄图
scene: 村里的老人指着界石，讲起曾为一条田埂打过官司的往事。 In an agrarian society, land ownership decides a family's standing.
sceneCN: 这里 agrarian society 指「围绕土地占有与农耕关系组织起来的社会」（第 1 个义项：以土地与农耕为基础的社会）；句意为在农业社会里，土地所有权决定一个家庭的地位。图中可辨识物件：地契、界石、犁、谷仓、田埂。

pos.zh: 农业社会（可数）

collocations.phrase: the transition from an agrarian society

derivatives.zh: 土地的 / 土地改革者

senses.title: A society built on land and farming
senses.titleCN: 以土地与农耕为基础的社会
senses.definition: a society in which land is the main source of livelihood, wealth and status
senses.definitionCN: 土地是生计、财富与地位主要来源的社会
senses.example: In an agrarian society, land ownership decides a family's standing.
senses.exampleCN: 在农业社会里，土地所有权决定一个家庭的地位。
senses.why: agrarian names land as property, so the phrase is a society whose order rests on who holds the fields.
senses.whyCN: 土地一词指作为财产的土地，因此这个短语指一个秩序取决于谁持有田地的社会。

senses.title: Its system of land tenure
senses.definition: the rules by which land is held, rented, inherited and worked
senses.definitionCN: 土地被持有、租佃、继承与耕作的规则
senses.example: Tenancy shaped agrarian society more than soil quality did.
senses.exampleCN: 租佃制度对农业社会的塑造甚于土壤质量。
senses.why: the same field can support very different societies depending on who holds it and on what terms.
senses.whyCN: 同一块田依据谁持有、以什么条件持有，可以支撑非常不同的社会。

senses.title: Village and kinship organization
senses.definition: the ordering of life through villages, households and extended kin
senses.definitionCN: 通过村落、家庭与扩展亲族来安排生活
senses.example: Agrarian society settled disputes inside the kin group before going to court.
senses.exampleCN: 农业社会先在亲族内部解决纠纷，再上法庭。
senses.why: farming is carried on by households, so the household and its kin become the working unit of society.
senses.whyCN: 农耕由家庭承担，因此家庭及其亲族成为社会的工作单位。

senses.title: A pre-industrial stage
senses.definition: the stage in development typology that precedes industrial society
senses.definitionCN: 发展类型学中先于工业社会的阶段
senses.example: The typology treats agrarian society as the stage before industry.
senses.exampleCN: 类型学把农业社会视为工业之前的阶段。
senses.why: a social type becomes a stage when it is placed on a single line of development.
senses.whyCN: 当一个社会类型被放到一条发展线上，它就成了阶段。

senses.title: A seasonal labour calendar
senses.titleCN: 按季节安排的劳动历法
senses.definition: a working year paced by ploughing, sowing, weeding and harvest
senses.definitionCN: 按犁地、播种、除草与收割安排的工作年
senses.example: In agrarian society, weddings waited until after the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 在农业社会，婚礼要等到收割之后。
senses.why: when income arrives once a year, every social event is scheduled around the crop.
senses.whyCN: 当收入一年只来一次，一切社交活动都要围绕作物安排。

senses.title: Its class structure
senses.definition: the division between landowners, tenants and landless labourers
senses.definitionCN: 地主、佃农与无地劳工之间的划分
senses.example: Agrarian society was divided between those who held land and those who worked it.
senses.exampleCN: 农业社会分为持有土地者与耕作土地者。
senses.why: land is scarce and inheritable, so tenure hardens into classes that pass from generation to generation.
senses.whyCN: 土地稀缺且可继承，因此占有关系固化为代代相传的阶级。

senses.title: A historical era
senses.definition: the long period before industrialization in a given region
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区工业化之前的漫长时期
senses.example: The archive covers three centuries of agrarian society.
senses.exampleCN: 这批档案涵盖农业社会三个世纪的历史。
senses.why: historians date the era by the moment industry begins to dominate, not by a single event.
senses.whyCN: 历史学者以工业开始占主导的时刻断代，而非以单一事件。

senses.title: A contemporary rural order
senses.definition: a present-day society still organized around small farms and land tenure
senses.definitionCN: 今天仍围绕小农场与土地占有组织的社会
senses.example: Agrarian society persists where land reform stalled.
senses.exampleCN: 在土地改革停滞的地方，农业社会仍然延续。
senses.why: the typology describes a sequence, not an extinction, so the phrase still names living societies.
senses.whyCN: 类型学描述的是序列而非灭绝，因此这个短语仍命名活着的社会。

intro.en: Agrarian comes from Latin agrarius 'of land', from ager 'field'; society comes from Latin societas 'association'. The pairing belongs to modern social thought. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: agrarian 来自拉丁 agrarius「土地的」，其词根为 ager「田地」；society 来自拉丁 societas「结社」。这一配对属于近代社会思想。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ager meant 'field, farmland'. It also gives acre, and its Indo-European source is a reconstruction rather than an attested form.
items.cn: ager 意为「田地、耕地」，也构成 acre；其印欧来源属重构形式，而非有据可查的材料。

items.en: Agrarius 'of land' described laws about public land and the politicians who proposed them, so the legal sense is older than the social one.
items.cn: agrarius「土地的」用于关于公地的法律及提出这些法律的政治人物，因此法律义早于社会义。

items.en: Societas named an association or partnership among socii 'allies'; its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: societas 指 socii「盟友」之间的结社或伙伴关系；其更深来源未得到证明。

items.en: Nineteenth-century social thinkers joined the two words to name the land-based order that industry was replacing.
items.cn: 19 世纪的社会思想家把这两个词连用，命名正被工业取代的、以土地为基础的秩序。

items.en: Development studies later applied the phrase to present-day smallholder regions, where land tenure still orders society.
items.cn: 发展研究后来把这个短语用于当代小农地区，那里的土地占有仍在安排社会。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origins and first date): the pre-Latin root of ager and the origin of socius are reconstructions, and the earliest use of the exact phrase is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：ager 在拉丁语之前的词根与 socius 的来源均属重构形式；这一确切短语的最早使用没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one holds land-based social labels that are nearly interchangeable; group two holds orders defined by other features.
note.cn: 第一组是几乎可以互换的、以土地为基础的社会称谓；第二组是按其他特征定义的社会秩序。

entries.definition: A society defined by what it produces; the two phrases overlap heavily, but this one stresses crops rather than tenure.
entries.definitionCN: 按产出定义的社会；两个短语大量重叠，但这个更强调作物而非土地占有。

entries.definition: A society organized around manufacturing, which replaces the land order.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕制造业组织的社会，它取代土地秩序。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning of land; it can modify reform, law or crisis without naming a whole society.
entries.definitionCN: 意为土地的那个形容词；可修饰改革、法律或危机，不必指整个社会。

entries.definition: The rules of holding land, which are central to agrarian society but are only one of its features.
entries.definitionCN: 持有土地的规则，是农业社会的核心，但只是其特征之一。

entries.definition: A society of small cultivators tied to landlords and markets; it stresses class position rather than the type of economy.
entries.definitionCN: 由小农组成、与地主和市场绑定的社会；强调阶级位置而非经济类型。

entries.definition: A society defined by low density and country living; it may still depend on industry for income.
entries.definitionCN: 以低密度与乡居生活定义的社会；收入仍可能依赖工业。

entries.definition: A society of lords, vassals and serfs bound by obligations; narrower and more political than agrarian society.
entries.definitionCN: 由领主、封臣与农奴按义务联结的社会；比农业社会更窄、更政治化。

entries.definition: Any society before factory industry, including trading and pastoral ones that are not agrarian.
entries.definitionCN: 工厂工业之前的任何社会，包括并非农业的贸易社会与游牧社会。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The adjective means of land, so the phrase is a society ordered by who holds the fields.
normal.cn: 这个形容词意为土地的，因此短语指一个按谁持有田地来排序的社会。

normal.en: Tenure is the hinge: landowners, tenants and labourers.
normal.cn: 土地占有是铰链：地主、佃农与劳工。

normal.en: The village and the kin group are its working units.
normal.cn: 村落与亲族群是它的工作单位。

normal.en: The harvest sets its calendar and its debts.
normal.cn: 收割决定它的历法与债务。

normal.cn: 农业社会与工业社会是一组标准对照。

abstract.en: Picture a boundary stone that decides more than any fence.
abstract.cn: 想象一块界石比任何篱笆都更能决定事情。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger of land that doubles as a list of who may speak.
abstract.cn: 想象一本土地账簿同时是一份谁可以说话的名单。

abstract.en: Picture a village where the harvest is the only clock that matters.
abstract.cn: 想象一座村庄，收割是唯一重要的时钟。

examples.en: Agrarian society gave way slowly to wage labour in the towns.
examples.cn: 农业社会缓慢地让位给城镇里的雇佣劳动。

examples.en: Reformers argued that agrarian society kept half the population illiterate.
examples.cn: 改革者认为农业社会使一半人口不识字。

examples.en: The survey compares agrarian society in three mountain districts.
examples.cn: 这项调查比较了三个山区的农业社会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「土地的（agrarian）+ 社会（society）」——按谁持有田地来排序的社会，就是农业社会

root: 拉丁 ager「田地」→ agrarius「土地的」→ agrarian；拉丁 socius「同伴」→ societas「结社」→ society。两词在 19 世纪社会思想中连用。两词更深来源均属重构或不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one land order: a society living off fields, its tenure rules, its villages and kin, its pre-industrial stage, its harvest calendar, its classes, its historical era and the rural present that continues where reform stalled.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一种土地秩序展开：靠田地为生的社会、它的占有规则、它的村落与亲族、它的前工业阶段、它的收获历法、它的阶级、它的历史时期，以及改革停滞后仍在延续的农村现状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a deed, a boundary stone, a plough and a barn making the frame of one village.
core.cn: 核心意象：地契、界石、犁与谷仓构成一座村庄的骨架。

branches.en: LAND BASE: the base sense, a society whose livelihood, wealth and rank come from land.
branches.cn: 土地基础：基础义，生计、财富与等级都来自土地的社会。

branches.en: TENURE AND CLASSES: the rules of holding land harden into landlords, tenants and labourers.
branches.cn: 占有与阶级：持有土地的规则固化为地主、佃农与劳工。

branches.en: HOUSEHOLD TIME: kin groups work, settle disputes and marry around the harvest.
branches.cn: 家庭时间：亲族群围绕收割劳作、解决纠纷与婚嫁。

branches.en: PLACE IN HISTORY: a pre-industrial stage that becomes a dated era in each region.
branches.cn: 历史中的位置：前工业阶段在各地区成为可断代的时期。

branches.en: PRESENT: where reform stalled, the same order is still lived.
branches.cn: 现在：在改革停滞之处，同一秩序仍被人生活着。

intro.en: The phrase is a land adjective plus a noun of association, and both halves carry productive pieces.
intro.cn: 这个短语由一个土地形容词加一个结社名词构成，两半都带着能产的构词成分。

definition_zh: 矛盾情绪；矛盾心态；既爱又恨；犹豫不决
definition_en: the state of having two opposite feelings or attitudes about the same person, thing or choice
core_image: 一个人同时向同一扇门伸出手和收回手，两只手都停在半空
scene: 她在旧屋门口站了很久，一只手想推门进去，另一只手却把钥匙握得更紧。 Her ambivalence about selling the family house lasted for years.
sceneCN: 这里 ambivalence 指对同一件事同时怀有两种相反情绪（第 1 个义项：矛盾情绪）；句意为她对是否卖掉祖屋的矛盾心态持续了好几年。

pos.zh: 矛盾情绪；矛盾心态；犹豫不决

senses.title: Two opposite feelings at once
senses.titleCN: 同时怀有两种相反情绪
senses.definition: the coexistence of opposite feelings, such as love and resentment, toward one object
senses.definitionCN: 对同一对象同时存在相反情感，例如爱与怨恨
senses.example: She felt ambivalence toward the town that raised her.
senses.exampleCN: 她对养育自己的小镇怀着矛盾情绪。
senses.why: The word names two forces pulling at once: ambi- is 'both', and valentia is 'strength'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名两股同时拉扯的力量：ambi- 是「两者」，valentia 是「力量」。

senses.title: Indecision between options
senses.definition: a state of being unable to choose because both options attract and repel
senses.definitionCN: 因为两个选项都既吸引又排斥而无法选择
senses.example: His ambivalence about the job offer delayed the reply for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这份工作邀请的矛盾心态让回复拖了一周。
senses.why: Choice requires a preference; when two preferences hold equal weight, the scale does not tip.
senses.whyCN: 选择需要偏好；当两种偏好等重时，天平不会倾斜。

senses.title: Attraction and repulsion together
senses.definition: an emotional pull toward something that also causes discomfort or fear
senses.definitionCN: 对某物既被吸引又感到不适或恐惧
senses.example: There is a strange ambivalence in watching a storm from a safe room.
senses.exampleCN: 在安全的房间里看暴风雨，有一种奇怪的既吸引又排斥的感觉。
senses.why: Attraction and fear can hold the same object, which is the two-force structure at its most physical.
senses.whyCN: 吸引力与恐惧可以同时占据同一个对象，这是「两股力量」结构最具体的样子。

senses.title: Conflicting attitudes
senses.definition: the holding of two incompatible opinions or values about the same issue
senses.definitionCN: 对同一问题持有两种不相容的意见或价值
senses.example: Public ambivalence about the new tax shaped the debate.
senses.exampleCN: 公众对新税的冲突态度影响了这场辩论。
senses.why: Two opinions on one issue behave like two weights; when both are heavy, the attitude cannot settle.
senses.whyCN: 对同一问题的两种意见像两个砝码；两者都重时，态度无法稳定。

senses.title: A psychiatric term
senses.definition: in psychiatry, the simultaneous existence of contradictory impulses or feelings
senses.definitionCN: 在精神医学中，指相互矛盾的冲动或情感同时存在
senses.example: The clinician noted ambivalence as a feature of the patient's mood.
senses.exampleCN: 临床医生把矛盾情感记为病人情绪的一个特征。
senses.why: Clinical language names the same two-force conflict, but here it is observed as a symptom rather than a choice.
senses.whyCN: 临床语言命名的是同一种「两股力量」冲突，只是这里它被观察为症状，而不是选择。

senses.title: A public mood
senses.definition: a widespread mixture of approval and unease in a society
senses.definitionCN: 社会中普遍存在的赞同与不安的混合
senses.example: Surveys recorded ambivalence rather than clear support.
senses.exampleCN: 调查记录到的是矛盾心态，而不是明确支持。
senses.why: When many people hold the same mixed feeling, the private structure becomes a public climate.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人持有同一种混合感受时，私人的结构就变成公共的气候。

senses.title: A literary tone
senses.definition: a tone in writing that expresses affection and criticism at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 写作中同时表达亲近与批评的基调
senses.example: The novel's ambivalence toward its hero gives it depth.
senses.exampleCN: 小说对主人公的矛盾态度让它有了深度。
senses.why: A narrator can hold two attitudes without resolving them, and readers feel that suspension as tone.
senses.whyCN: 叙述者可以同时持有两种态度而不作解决，读者把这种悬置感受为基调。

senses.title: Uncertainty of choice
senses.definition: a lingering doubt that prevents a firm commitment
senses.definitionCN: 迟迟不去的疑虑使人无法坚定承诺
senses.example: Her ambivalence kept the engagement in limbo.
senses.exampleCN: 她的犹豫不决让婚约悬而未决。
senses.why: The two forces never settle, so the commitment stays suspended, which is the practical result of the structure.
senses.whyCN: 两股力量始终不落定，因此承诺一直悬着，这就是该结构在实际生活中的结果。

intro.en: Ambivalence is a modern psychiatric coinage built from two Latin pieces meaning 'both' and 'strength'.
intro.cn: ambivalence 是一个现代精神医学新造词，由两个拉丁语零件构成，分别表示「两者」与「力量」。

items.en: English borrowed the term in the early 20c. and soon widened it from clinical writing to ordinary emotional life.
items.cn: 英语在二十世纪初借入该术语，很快把它从临床文本扩展到日常情感生活。

items.en: The Swiss psychiatrist Eugen Bleuler coined Ambivalenz in 1910 to describe contradictory impulses in schizophrenia.
items.cn: 瑞士精神科医生尤金·布洛伊勒于 1910 年造出 Ambivalenz，用来描述精神分裂症中的矛盾冲动。

items.en: The prefix ambi- means 'both, on both sides', as in ambidextrous and ambiguous.
items.cn: 前缀 ambi- 意为「两者、两边」，如 ambidextrous 与 ambiguous。

items.en: Valentia 'strength, power' comes from valere 'to be strong, be worth', which also gives value and valid.
items.cn: valentia「力量、能力」来自 valere「强壮、有价值」，它也产生了 value 与 valid。

items.en: From psychiatry the word spread to politics, criticism and everyday speech, where it usually means mixed feelings rather than illness.
items.cn: 从精神医学出发，这个词扩散到政治、批评与日常语言，通常表示混合情绪，而不是疾病。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the 'both' prefix or the same root; the near-meaning group names forms of doubt and conflict.
note.cn: 形近组共享「两者」前缀或同一词根；近义组列出怀疑与冲突的各种形态。

entries.definition: having mixed or opposite feelings.
entries.definitionCN: 怀有混合或相反情感的。

entries.definition: in a way that shows mixed feelings.
entries.definitionCN: 以表现矛盾情感的方式。

entries.definition: having more than one possible meaning; unclear.
entries.definitionCN: 有不止一种可能含义；不清楚。

entries.definition: able to use both hands equally well.
entries.definitionCN: 双手同样灵巧的。

entries.definition: the inability to make a decision.
entries.definitionCN: 无法作出决定。

entries.definition: a struggle between opposing forces or wishes.
entries.definitionCN: 对立力量或愿望之间的挣扎。

entries.definition: a state of not being sure what to think or do.
entries.definitionCN: 不确定该想什么或做什么的状态。

entries.definition: a feeling of not being convinced.
entries.definitionCN: 未被说服的感觉。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the 'both' prefix and the picture of two hands pulling one door.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想利用「两者」前缀和「两只手拉同一扇门」的画面。

normal.en: ambi means both, valence means strength: two strengths pulling at once.
normal.cn: ambi 意为两者，valence 意为力量：两股力量同时拉扯。

normal.en: Picture two hands on one door handle, one pushing in and one pulling back.
normal.cn: 想象两只手握在同一门把上，一只往里推，一只往回拉。

normal.en: The ending -ence makes it a state, so it is the condition of being pulled two ways.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ence 使它成为状态，即被两边拉扯的处境。

normal.en: Link it with ambiguous: both words begin with 'both'.
normal.cn: 把它和 ambiguous 联系起来：两个词都以「两者」开头。

normal.en: Say it as am-bi-valence, a balance that will not settle.
normal.cn: 读成 am-bi-valence，一架不肯停稳的天平。

abstract.en: A scale with equal weights cannot tip, and that stillness is the word.
abstract.cn: 两边的重量相等的天平不会倾斜，这种静止就是这个单词。

abstract.en: Love and resentment can occupy the same object without cancelling out.
abstract.cn: 爱与怨恨可以占据同一对象而不互相抵消。

abstract.en: Clinical use narrows the word; everyday use widens it back to mixed feelings.
abstract.cn: 临床用法使词义变窄；日常用法又把它扩回混合情绪。

examples.en: She described her ambivalence about leaving the city.
examples.cn: 她描述了自己对离开这座城市的矛盾心情。

examples.en: The novel treats modernity with ambivalence.
examples.cn: 这部小说以矛盾的笔调对待现代性。

examples.en: His ambivalence made the final decision harder.
examples.cn: 他的犹豫不决让最终决定更难作出。

sensesIntro.en: Ambivalence is one structure, two forces on the same object; the senses vary by whether the forces are feelings, opinions, choices or a clinical symptom.
sensesIntro.cn: ambivalence 只有一个结构，即两股力量作用在同一对象上；各义项的差别在于这两股力量是情感、意见、选择还是临床症状。

core.en: TWO FORCES, ONE OBJECT

branches.en: The basic emotional mixture of attraction and resistance.
branches.cn: 吸引与抗拒的基本情绪混合。

branches.en: The choice that cannot be made and the doubt that remains.

branches.en: Attitudes and public moods made of two incompatible halves.
branches.cn: 由两个不相容部分构成的态度与公众情绪。

branches.en: The clinical reading, where the conflict is a symptom.

branches.cn: 同时容纳亲近与批评的文学基调。
