definition_zh: 减轻；缓解；缓和；使缓和
definition_en: to make pain, difficulty or a bad feeling less severe without removing its cause
core_image: 压在人肩上的石袋被一只只手卸下一半，肩线慢慢回正
scene: 换药时最疼，护士引导病人慢慢呼吸，疼痛就退了一些。 The clinic uses guided breathing to alleviate pain during dressing changes.
sceneCN: 这里指让疼痛变轻（第 1 个义项：减轻疼痛或症状）；句意为诊所靠引导呼吸来缓解换药时的疼痛。图中可辨识物件：病床、绷带、被卸下一半的石袋。

pos.zh: 减轻；缓解；缓和

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「减轻；缓解」
由该动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「缓解性的」
由该动词加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「缓解的；缓和剂」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「缓解者；缓解手段」
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「已减轻的」

senses.title: To ease pain
senses.definition: to reduce the intensity of physical pain without curing its cause
senses.definitionCN: 降低身体疼痛的强度，但不消除病因
senses.example: The drug alleviates pain but does not repair the joint.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药能减轻疼痛，却修不好关节。
senses.why: Alleviate comes from a word for light, and pain is treated as a weight that can be made lighter.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出自「轻」义，疼痛被当作一份可以变轻的重量。

senses.title: To ease pressure or strain
senses.definition: to reduce the level of stress, workload or tension that people or systems carry
senses.definitionCN: 降低人或系统所承受的压力、工作量或紧张程度
senses.example: Extra staff alleviated the pressure on the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 增加人手缓解了夜班的压力。
senses.why: Pressure is a load, so making it lighter is the same physical move applied to work.
senses.whyCN: 压力是负荷，让它变轻就是把同一物理动作用到工作上。

senses.title: To reduce poverty or hardship
senses.definition: to lessen the severity of material hardship, usually by policy rather than by cure
senses.definitionCN: 减轻物质困苦的严重程度，通常靠政策而非根治
senses.example: The subsidy alleviated hardship among the poorest households.
senses.exampleCN: 这项补贴缓解了最贫困家庭的困苦。
senses.why: Social policy speaks of lightening a burden that cannot yet be removed.
senses.whyCN: 社会政策谈的是先把卸不掉的负担弄轻。

senses.title: To relieve congestion
senses.definition: to make traffic, queues or demand less dense
senses.definitionCN: 使交通、排队或需求不再那么密集
senses.example: A second entrance alleviated congestion at the main gate.
senses.exampleCN: 增加第二个入口缓解了正门的拥堵。
senses.why: Congestion is pressure concentrated at one point, and the verb spreads or lowers it.
senses.whyCN: 拥堵是集中在一处的压力，这个动词把它摊开或降低。

senses.title: To soothe anxiety
senses.definition: to make fear or worry less intense, often temporarily
senses.definitionCN: 使恐惧或担忧不那么强烈，常常只是暂时
senses.example: A clear explanation alleviated her anxiety about the results.
senses.exampleCN: 清楚的解释缓解了她对结果的焦虑。
senses.why: Emotional weight is lightened much as physical weight is, which is why the same verb serves both.
senses.whyCN: 情绪的重量与身体的重量一样可以被减轻，所以同一个动词两者都管。

senses.title: To soften an impact
senses.definition: to reduce how hard an event, change or policy hits those affected
senses.definitionCN: 降低某个事件、变化或政策对受影响者的打击力度
senses.example: The fund alleviated the impact of the sudden price rise.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔基金缓和了价格骤涨带来的冲击。
senses.why: An impact lands as force, and lightening it is to take part of the blow away.
senses.whyCN: 冲击以力量的形式落下，减轻它就是卸掉一部分打击。

senses.title: To provide relief measures
senses.definition: to supply practical help that makes a difficult situation easier to bear
senses.definitionCN: 提供实际帮助，使困难处境更容易承受
senses.example: The city alleviated the water shortage with temporary deliveries.
senses.exampleCN: 市里用临时送水缓解了缺水。
senses.why: Here the verb shifts from the feeling to the measure that produces the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 这里动词从「感受」转向「产生该感受的措施」。

senses.title: To treat symptoms only
senses.definition: to give symptomatic relief while leaving the underlying condition untreated
senses.definitionCN: 只提供症状层面的缓解，不处理根本病因
senses.example: Hospice care alleviated her symptoms without treating the disease itself.
senses.exampleCN: 临终照护缓解了她的症状，却没有治疗疾病本身。
senses.why: Medicine distinguishes cure from relief, and alleviate belongs firmly to the second.
senses.whyCN: 医学区分「治愈」与「缓解」，这个词稳稳属于后者。

intro.en: Alleviate comes from Latin alleviare, to lighten, from ad, toward, and levare, to raise or lighten, from levis, light in weight. It is not related to the Latin verb for raising or nourishing.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 alleviare「使轻」，由 ad「向」与 levare「举起、减轻」构成，而 levare 出自 levis「轻」；它与拉丁语中表示「举起、养育」的另一个动词无关。

items.en: Levis meant light in weight, and the same root gives levity, elevate and relief through related verbs.
items.cn: 这个词指重量轻；同一词根经相关动词还给出「轻快」「举起」与「缓解」等词。

items.en: Levare meant to lighten or to raise, and the two readings share the picture of something becoming easier to lift.
items.cn: 这个词意为使轻或举起，两种读法共享「东西变得容易举起」的画面。

items.en: The prefix ad- meant toward, and it marks the direction in which the lightening is applied.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 意为「向」，标出减轻作用的方向。

items.en: Alleviare meant to lighten, relieve or comfort, and it was used of pain, grief and burdens.
items.cn: 这个词意为使轻、缓解、安慰，用于疼痛、悲伤与负担。

items.en: It is often confused with allevare, to raise or feed, but the two verbs differ in root and meaning.
items.cn: 它常与表示「举起、喂养」的 allevare 混淆，但两者词根与词义都不同。

items.en: English took the verb directly from Latin in the sixteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语十六世纪直接从拉丁语引入这个动词，确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the light root or looks close; the second group names neighbouring ideas of relief and reduction.
note.cn: 第一组与「alleviate」共享「轻」的词根或只是形近；第二组是与「缓解、减少」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of making something less severe.
entries.definitionCN: 指减轻、缓解这一行为的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective for something that relieves.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指起缓解作用的。

entries.definition: To raise something, from the same light root through a different prefix path.
entries.definitionCN: 指举起、抬高；同出「轻」词根，经不同前缀路径。

entries.definition: Lightness of mood, literally lightness of weight.
entries.definitionCN: 指情绪轻快，字面就是「重量轻」。

entries.definition: The noun for easing a burden, from a related Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指负担的减轻，出自相关的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: To take a burden or pain away, often more completely than alleviate.
entries.definitionCN: 指卸去负担或疼痛，程度常比 alleviate 更彻底。

entries.definition: To make something less painful or difficult, in plain everyday language.
entries.definitionCN: 指使不那么痛苦或困难，是日常说法。

entries.definition: To make something bad less severe, especially damage or risk.
entries.definitionCN: 指使坏事不那么严重，尤指损害或风险。

entries.definition: To calm a feeling or a surface, with a comforting tone.
entries.definitionCN: 指安抚情绪或舒缓表面，带安慰色彩。

entries.definition: To make or become smaller in amount.
entries.definitionCN: 指在数量上减少。

entries.definition: To bring down a size, amount or level, the broad neutral verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指降低大小、数量或水平，是宽泛中性的说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the light root, the false twin allevare, and the medical phrases that keep the word in use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「轻」的词根、容易混淆的近形动词 allevare，以及让这个词保持活力的医学搭配。

normal.en: Levis is light, so alleviate is to put something on a scale and watch the reading drop.
normal.cn: levis 是「轻」，所以这个词就是把东西放上秤，看读数往下走。

normal.en: Elevate and alleviate look alike and are related, but one raises and the other lightens.
normal.cn: elevate 与 alleviate 形近且同源，但一个往上举，一个往轻里减。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with allevare, which meant to raise or feed.
normal.cn: 不要与 allevare 混淆，那个词是「举起、喂养」。

normal.en: Clinics alleviate pain, cities alleviate congestion, and policy alleviates poverty.
normal.cn: 诊所缓解疼痛，城市缓解拥堵，政策缓解贫困。

normal.en: Alleviate treats the symptom; cure treats the cause.
normal.cn: 这个词处理症状，「治愈」处理病因。

abstract.en: To alleviate is to admit you cannot remove the weight, and still take some of it off.
abstract.cn: 减轻，就是承认重量卸不掉，却仍然拿走一部分。

abstract.en: Relief is not cure: the stone is lighter, but it is still on the shoulder.
abstract.cn: 缓解不是治愈：石头变轻了，可还在肩上。

abstract.en: Every soothing act is a small redistribution of weight from the weak to the strong.
abstract.cn: 每一次安抚，都是把重量从弱者身上往强者身上挪一点。

examples.en: Cool compresses alleviate the itching for about an hour.
examples.cn: 冷敷能缓解瘙痒大约一小时。

examples.en: The new lane alleviated congestion on the western approach.
examples.cn: 新车道缓解了西侧入口的拥堵。

examples.en: Cash transfers alleviated hardship but did not end it.
examples.cn: 现金补助缓解了困苦，却没有终结它。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿利维特」——肩上的石袋被卸下一半：减轻、缓解

root: 拉丁语 levis「轻」→ levare「使轻、举起」→ alleviare「使轻、缓解」（ad-「向」）；英语十六世纪直接引入。与表示「举起、养育」的 allevare 无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all lighten something: pain, pressure, poverty, congestion, anxiety, impact, shortage and symptoms.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在给某物减重：疼痛、压力、贫困、拥堵、焦虑、冲击、短缺与症状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: half the stones are lifted off a shoulder, and the shoulder slowly straightens.
core.cn: 核心意象：肩上的石袋被卸下一半，肩线慢慢回正。

branches.en: THE BODY IS LIGHTENED: pain or a symptom loses intensity, though the cause may remain.
branches.cn: 身体变轻：疼痛或症状减弱，病因却可能还在。

branches.en: THE LOAD IS SHARED: stress and workload are lowered for those carrying them.
branches.cn: 负荷被分担：承受者的压力与工作量降下来。

branches.en: THE INWARD WEIGHT: hardship and anxiety become easier to bear.
branches.cn: 内心的重量：困苦与焦虑变得较易承受。

branches.en: THE CROWD IS SPREAD: congestion loses its concentration at one point.
branches.cn: 人群被摊开：拥堵失去那一点上的集中。

branches.en: THE BLOW IS SOFTENED: an impact or a shortage meets a measure that takes part of its force.
branches.cn: 打击被软化：冲击或短缺遇上一项卸去部分力度的措施。

intro.en: Alleviate is a Latin verb built from a light root, and the same root runs through elevate, levity and relief.
intro.cn: 这是一个由「轻」词根构成的拉丁动词，同一词根贯穿 elevate、levity 与 relief。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies levis, levare and alleviare; the deeper origin of the root is reconstructed rather than recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 levis、levare、alleviare；词根更早的来源属重构而非有记录的形式。

items.example: The adjective named what is easy to carry.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词指容易携带的东西。

items.example: The two readings meet in the idea of making something easier to lift.
items.exampleCN: 两种读法在「让东西更容易举起」处汇合。

items.example: Before l it assimilates to al-, as in alleviate.
items.exampleCN: 在 l 前同化为 al-，即 alleviate 的形式。

items.example: The verb was used of pain and grief.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词用于疼痛与悲伤。

items.example: It marks the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 它标明英语动词。

items.example: It forms alleviation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 alleviation。

items.example: It forms alleviative.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 alleviative。

items.example: It forms alleviator.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 alleviator。

items.example: The same root, moved from weight to temperament.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根，从重量移到性情。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「减轻；缓解」
由该动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「缓解性的」
由该动词加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「缓解的；缓和剂」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「缓解者」
由同一「轻」词根加表示「向外」的前缀构成，义为「举起；提升」

definition_zh: 表示；标示；意味着；指代
definition_en: to be a sign of something, or to stand for a particular meaning
core_image: 路牌上画着一辆被斜线划掉的车——它不描写车，只把“此处禁行”标出来
scene: 摊开一张两国交界的地图： The dotted line on the map denotes the border between the two countries.
sceneCN: 这里 denote 是「标示、标出」（第 2 个义项）；地图上的虚线并不描写边界，只是把边界的位置标出来。句意：地图上的虚线标示两国边界。

pos.zh: 表示；标示；意味着；指代
（符号、词语）表示……的意思

senses.title: Mark off: single a thing out by a mark
senses.titleCN: 划界标出：用标记把某物单独圈出来
senses.definition: to mark something off from others, or identify it by a distinguishing mark
senses.definitionCN: 把某物从其他事物中划出来，或用有区别的标记把它认出来
senses.example: On the plan, each plot is denoted by a small numbered square.
senses.exampleCN: 在平面图上，每一块地都用带编号的小方框标出。
senses.why: Latin denotare joins de- 'completely' to notare 'to mark'. The first English sense in the 1590s was 'mark off from others; identify by a mark' — the mark does not describe the thing, it singles it out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 denotare 由 de-“完全”加 notare“做标记”构成。16 世纪 90 年代英语最早的意思是“把某物从别的东西里划出来、用标记认出它”——标记不描写事物，只把它单独点出来。

senses.title: Be the sign of: stand in place of something
senses.titleCN: 标示：作为某物的记号站在那里
senses.definition: to be a sign or symptom of something; to indicate it
senses.definitionCN: 作为某事物的记号或征兆；表明、指示该事物
senses.example: The raised flag denotes that the track is closed.
senses.exampleCN: 升起的旗子表示这条跑道已关闭。
senses.why: Once a mark can single a thing out, the mark can also stand for it. The 1590s record already includes 'be the sign or symptom of', so the physical mark became a sign read by an observer.
senses.whyCN: 一旦一个标记能把事物单独点出来，它也能代替那个事物站在那里。16 世纪 90 年代的记录已含“是……的记号或征兆”，于是手上的标记变成了让观察者去读的符号。

senses.title: Of a word: carry a literal meaning
senses.titleCN: 字面所指：一个词承载的本义
senses.definition: of a word, to have a particular literal meaning or refer to a particular thing
senses.definitionCN: 指词语具有某种字面意义，或指称某一特定事物
senses.example: In British English, 'flat' denotes an apartment, not a tyre.
senses.exampleCN: 在英式英语里，flat 指的是公寓，而不是轮胎。
senses.why: Language took the sign relation and made it verbal: a word is the mark, its literal meaning is what the mark stands for. This is the 'denotation' later contrasted with the feelings a word carries.
senses.whyCN: 语言把“记号—所指”这层关系搬到了词语上：词是标记，字面意义是标记所代表的东西。这就是后来与“言外之感”相对立的“外延、字面意义”。

senses.title: Of a symbol: represent a fixed value
senses.titleCN: 符号代表：固定地代表某个对象
senses.definition: of a symbol, to represent or stand for a particular object or quantity
senses.definitionCN: 指符号代表、指代某一特定对象或数量
senses.example: In the equation, the letter x denotes an unknown number.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个方程里，字母 x 表示一个未知数。
senses.why: Mathematics kept the strictest part of the word: a symbol is appointed to stand for exactly one value. The mark is arbitrary, but the standing-for is fixed by rule.
senses.whyCN: 数学保留了这个词最严格的一面：一个符号被指定代表恰好一个值。记号本身是任意的，但“代表什么”由规则固定下来。

senses.title: Point to indirectly: suggest without saying
senses.titleCN: 暗示：不直说而指向某意
senses.definition: to suggest or imply something indirectly, rather than state it openly
senses.definitionCN: 间接地暗示或意味着某事，而不是公开说出
senses.example: A rising tone may denote doubt rather than a real question.
senses.exampleCN: 升调可能表示怀疑，而不是真正的提问。
senses.why: A sign need not be explicit. Since a mark can be read for what it hints at, denote widened from 'stand for' to 'point toward' — the listener infers what the sign implies.
senses.whyCN: 记号不必明说。既然一个标记可以被读出它暗示的东西，denote 就从“代表”扩大到“指向”——听者去推断记号所隐含的意思。

senses.title: Denotation in semantics: the hard edge of meaning
senses.titleCN: 语义学的外延：意义中坚硬的那条边
senses.definition: in semantics, the direct or literal meaning of an expression, as opposed to its connotation
senses.definitionCN: 语义学中指表达式的直接或字面意义，与内涵、联想义相对
senses.example: The denotation of 'snake' is a reptile; its connotation may be danger.
senses.exampleCN: snake 的外延是一种爬行动物；它的内涵可能是危险。
senses.why: Twentieth-century linguistics split the old verb into two nouns: denotation is what the sign covers, connotation is what it trails behind. The term keeps the word's original 'marking out' image.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪语言学把这个旧动词拆成两个名词：外延是符号所覆盖的范围，内涵是它身后拖着的联想。术语仍保留这个词最初“划出范围”的意象。

senses.title: Of a name: designate a person or office
senses.titleCN: 指称：名称指定某个人或职位
senses.definition: of a name or title, to designate a particular person, group, or office
senses.definitionCN: 指名称或头衔指定某个人、群体或职位
senses.example: 'Chair' denotes the person who runs the meeting, not the furniture.
senses.exampleCN: chair 指的是主持会议的人，而不是那件家具。
senses.why: A title is a mark pinned on a person. The 'mark off' sense survives here: the name does not describe the holder, it identifies which person is meant.
senses.whyCN: 头衔是别在人身上的标记。“划出来”的义项在这里仍然活着：名称不描写持有者，只指明说的是哪一个人。

senses.title: In medicine: be a symptom of
senses.titleCN: 医学上：作为某种病症的指征
senses.definition: of a symptom or test result, to indicate the presence of a particular disease or condition
senses.definitionCN: 指症状或检查结果表明存在某种疾病或状况
senses.example: A persistent cough may denote a lung infection.
senses.exampleCN: 持续咳嗽可能表明肺部感染。
senses.why: Medicine uses the body as a surface of signs. A symptom marks a hidden condition the way a flag marks a closed track; the visible sign denotes what cannot be seen.
senses.whyCN: 医学把身体当作一片符号的表面。症状标示看不见的病情，就像旗子标示关闭的跑道；可见的征兆代表着看不见的东西。

senses.title: In grammar: a form marks a function
senses.titleCN: 语法上：形式标记某一功能
senses.definition: of a grammatical form, to signal a particular function such as tense, number, or case
senses.definitionCN: 指语法形式标示时态、数、格等特定功能
senses.example: In English, the -s ending denotes plural number on nouns.
senses.exampleCN: 在英语里，-s 词尾表示名词的复数。
senses.why: Grammarians treat inflection as a mark on a stem. The suffix is the visible mark; plural is the function it denotes, so the 1590s 'mark' sense is applied to the smallest pieces of language.
senses.whyCN: 语法学家把屈折变化看作词干上的标记。后缀是看得见的记号，复数是它所表示的功能——16 世纪 90 年代那个“标记”义就这样用到了语言最小的部件上。

intro.en: Denote comes from Latin denotare, 'mark out, designate', built from de- 'completely' and notare 'to mark'. It reached English through French dénoter in the 1590s, and later became a technical term in logic and semantics.
intro.cn: denote 来自拉丁语 denotare“标出、指定”，由 de-“完全”与 notare“做标记”构成。它经法语 dénoter 于 16 世纪 90 年代进入英语，后来成为逻辑学和语义学的术语。

items.en: Denotare meant 'to mark out, point out, designate'. It is a transparent compound of de- 'completely' and notare 'to mark', from nota 'a mark, sign, note'.
items.cn: denotare 意为“标出、指出、指定”，是 de-“完全”与 notare“做标记”的透明复合词，而 notare 来自 nota“标记、符号、记号”。

items.en: French dénoter carried the Latin sense 'to denote, mark out' and supplied the form English borrowed.
items.cn: 法语 dénoter 承袭拉丁语“标示、标出”的意思，并提供了英语借入的词形。

items.en: The first English records give 'mark off from others; identify by a mark; be the sign or symptom of'. The mark and the thing it stands for arrive together.
items.cn: 英语最早记录为“把某物从其他事物中划出；用标记辨认；是……的记号或征兆”。标记与它所代表的事物是一起出现的。

items.en: The verb settled into the general sense 'be a sign of, indicate'. Objects, words, and symptoms could all denote what they pointed to.
items.cn: 这个动词稳定在泛指的“是……的记号、表明”上。物件、词语、症状都可以 denote 它们所指向的东西。

items.en: Logic and linguistics turned denote into a technical word: denotation is the literal range of a term, while connotation is the feeling it drags along. The spelling and the mark image have not changed.
items.cn: 逻辑学和语言学把 denote 变成术语：denotation 是词语的字面范围，connotation 是它拖着的感受。拼写与“标记”的意象都没有变。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: to move someone to a lower rank or position. It shares the de- opening and the stress pattern of denote.
entries.definitionCN: 使降级、降职。与 denote 同样以 de- 开头、重音位置相同。

entries.definition: to give one's time or energy wholly to something. It differs from denote by a single consonant.
entries.definitionCN: 把时间或精力完全献给某事。与 denote 只差一个辅音。

entries.definition: to publicly declare someone or something wrong or evil. It begins with the same deno- string but ends in a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 公开谴责、告发。开头同样是 deno-，但词根不同。

entries.definition: to have a particular sense or refer to a particular thing. It is the plain everyday match for denote in its word sense.
entries.definitionCN: 意思是；指的是。对应 denote 表“词语字面意义”的义项，是最日常的说法。

entries.definition: to be a sign of something, or to make a meaning known. It is close to denote but often implies communication.
entries.definitionCN: 表示；意味着；象征。与 denote 接近，但更强调传达出意思。

entries.definition: to show or point to something, often indirectly. It matches the 'be a sign of' sense without the technical weight.
entries.definitionCN: 表明；指示。对应“是……的记号”义，但没有术语色彩。

entries.definition: to stand for something or act on its behalf. It matches denote in the symbol-and-name senses.
entries.definitionCN: 代表；象征。对应 denote 的符号义和名称指称义。

entries.definition: to be an abbreviation or symbol of something. It is the spoken paraphrase of what a mark denotes.
entries.definitionCN: 代表；是……的缩写或符号。是“一个标记 denote 什么”的口语说法。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: the Latin notare family behind note and notify, the con- prefix inside connote, and the everyday habit of reading marks as signs.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：note、notify 背后拉丁语 notare 词族，connote 里的 con- 前缀，以及人把标记读成符号的日常习惯。

normal.en: de- means 'completely' and notare means 'to mark': to denote is to mark a thing fully, so that the mark can stand for it.
normal.cn: de- 是“完全”，notare 是“做标记”：denote 就是把标记完整地打在事物上，好让这个标记能代替它。

normal.en: note, notable, notify and denote all sit on Latin nota 'mark'. A note is a mark you make so the thing can be found again.
normal.cn: note、notable、notify、denote 都站在拉丁语 nota“标记”上。note 是你做的标记，为的是以后还能找到那件事。

normal.en: connote = con- 'with' + notare 'mark': connotation is the extra mark a word carries along with its plain denotation.
normal.cn: connote = con-“一起”+ notare“标记”：connotation 就是一个词在字面外延之外顺带带着的额外标记。

normal.en: In a dictionary, the denotation is the first line; the connotation is what the usage note whispers after it.
normal.cn: 词典里，denotation 是第一行释义；connotation 是后面用法说明悄悄补充的那层意味。

normal.en: Mathematicians say x denotes a number: the letter is a mark appointed to stand in the number's place.
normal.cn: 数学家说 x denotes 一个数：字母是被指派站在那个数位置上的标记。

abstract.en: A sign is a finger pointing at the moon: denote gives the pointing, not the moonlight.
abstract.cn: 符号是指向月亮的手指：denote 给出的是那根手指，而不是月光。

abstract.en: Denotation is the hard edge of a word's meaning; connotation is the soft shadow it casts.
abstract.cn: 外延是词义坚硬的那条边，内涵是它投下的柔软影子。

abstract.en: To denote is to draw a line around a thing and say: this mark, and no other, stands here.
abstract.cn: denote 就是绕着事物画一条线，然后说：站在这里的，是这个标记，不是别的。

examples.en: In this chart, the red bars denote last year's sales.
examples.cn: 在这张图里，红色柱条表示去年的销售额。

examples.en: For many people, a wedding ring denotes commitment rather than wealth.
examples.cn: 对许多人来说，婚戒表示的是承诺，而不是财富。

examples.en: The symbol @ denotes 'at' in an email address.
examples.cn: 符号 @ 在电子邮件地址中表示“at”。

dict_mnemonic.text: “点 note”——de（完全）+ note（标记），把标记完全点到事物上，就是标示、表示

root: 源自拉丁语 denotare“标出、指定”，由 de-“完全”+ notare“做标记”构成，notare 又来自 nota“标记”；经法语 dénoter 于 16 世纪 90 年代进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of denote, from a mark that singles a thing out to the semantic term for literal meaning. Each step keeps the same move: a visible mark is placed where something else should be read.
sensesIntro.cn: denote 的九个义项，从把事物单独划出的标记，一直到语义学里指“字面意义”的术语。每一步都保持同一个动作：把一个看得见的标记放在本该读出别的东西的位置上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark laid on a thing so that the mark can stand for it.
core.cn: 核心意象：把一个标记打在事物上，好让这个标记代替它。

branches.en: THE MARK AND THE SIGN: first the mark identifies a thing, then the same mark is read as its sign.
branches.cn: 标记与符号：先是用标记认出事物，接着同一个标记被读成事物的符号。

branches.en: WORDS AND NAMES: a word marks a literal meaning, and a title marks which person is meant.
branches.cn: 词与名称：词标出字面意义，头衔标出说的是哪个人。

branches.en: FORMAL MARKS: a mathematical symbol stands for a fixed value, and a grammatical ending marks a function.
branches.cn: 形式标记：数学符号代表固定数值，语法词尾标示功能。

branches.en: READING BEYOND THE MARK: a tone hints at doubt, and a symptom points to a hidden disease.
branches.cn: 读出标记之外：语调暗示怀疑，症状指向看不见的疾病。

branches.en: THE TECHNICAL EDGE: denotation names the literal range of a term, set against its connotation.
branches.cn: 术语的边界：外延命名词语的字面范围，与内涵相对。

intro.en: Denote is a Latin loan built on the stem not- 'mark': note, notable, notify and annotate share it, while de-, con- and ad- change the direction of the marking.
intro.cn: denote 是建立在词干 not-“标记”上的拉丁借词：note、notable、notify、annotate 共用这个词干，而 de-、con-、ad- 改变标记的方向。

latinIntro.en: Latin nota 'mark, sign' produces notare 'to mark', then denotare 'mark out', annotare 'write down beside', and connote 'mark along with'. The family is about marks, not about knowledge.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nota“标记、符号”生出 notare“做标记”，再生成 denotare“标出”、annotare“在旁边写下”、connotare“连带着标记”。这个词族讲的是标记，不是知识。

items.meaning: to mark out; be a sign of
items.meaningCN: 标示；表示（de- 完全 + notare 标记）
items.example: The crest denotes the city's founding family.
items.exampleCN: 这个纹章标示这座城市的创建家族。

items.meaning: the literal meaning or range of a term
items.meaningCN: 字面意义；外延（-ation 构成名词）
items.example: Definitions focus on denotation, not on tone.
items.exampleCN: 释义关注的是字面意义，而不是语气。

items.meaningCN: 指示的；字面意义的（-ative 构成形容词）
items.example: Scientific writing tends to be denotative.
items.exampleCN: 科学写作倾向于使用字面意义。

items.meaning: a short written record; to notice
items.meaningCN: 笔记；注意到（直接来自 nota 标记）
items.example: She noted the exact time of the call.
items.exampleCN: 她记下了那通电话的确切时间。

items.meaningCN: 值得注意的；显著的（-able 值得）
items.example: The town is notable for its stone bridge.
items.exampleCN: 这座小镇因石桥而闻名。

items.example: Please notify us of any change of address.
items.exampleCN: 地址如有变动，请通知我们。

items.meaning: to add notes beside a text
items.meaningCN: 给……作注释（ad- 朝向 + notare 标记）
items.example: Students annotate the poem in the margins.
items.exampleCN: 学生们在页边给这首诗作注释。

items.meaning: a note added to a text
items.meaningCN: 注释；评注（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: The annotation explains an old idiom.
items.exampleCN: 这条注释解释了一个古老的习语。

items.meaning: to carry an extra suggested meaning
items.meaningCN: 意味着；含言外之意（con- 一起 + notare 标记）
items.example: The word 'home' connotes warmth and safety.
items.exampleCN: home 这个词含有温暖和安全的意味。

latinEntries.meaning: to mark, note, make a note of
to mark out, point out, designate

definition_zh: 因果关系；因果作用；引起；归因
definition_en: the relationship between a cause and its effect, or the act of causing something
core_image: 一排多米诺骨牌：第一张倒下，第二张跟着倒下，那条传递下去的连接就是因果
scene: 研讨课上，老师把两张图表并排投影：一张显示相关，一张显示因果。他说： Correlation is not causation.
sceneCN: 这里指第 1 个义项。这里 causation 是「因果关系」（第 1、7 个义项：因果关联与统计中的因果判断）；句意：相关不等于因果。图中可辨识物件：两张折线图、投影仪、粉笔、讲台。

pos.zh: 因果关系；因果作用；引起

forms.label: 复数（多种因果作用，较少用）

senses.title: The relation between cause and effect
senses.definition: the relation in which one event or state brings about another
senses.definitionCN: 一个事件或状态引起另一个事件或状态的关系
senses.example: The study examines the causation of migration.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究考察移民的因果关系。
senses.why: Causation names the link itself, not the cause and not the effect. The word is the bridge between two events, which is why it is so often paired with chain.
senses.whyCN: causation 命名的是连接本身，而不是原因或结果。这个词是两个事件之间的桥，因此常与 chain 搭配。

senses.title: The act of causing something
senses.definition: the action by which something is produced or brought about
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物产生或被造成的行为
senses.example: The report traces the causation of the accident to a faulty valve.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把事故的起因追溯到一个故障阀门。
senses.why: Here the noun names an activity rather than a relation. Someone or something did the causing, and the word points to that doing.
senses.whyCN: 这里名词命名的是一个活动，而不是一种关系。某人或某物做了“引起”这件事，这个词指向那个作为。

senses.title: Causation as a philosophical principle
senses.titleCN: 作为哲学原理的因果律
senses.definition: the principle that every event has a cause, or that like causes produce like effects
senses.definitionCN: 每个事件都有原因、或相同原因产生相同结果的原则
senses.example: Hume asked whether we can ever observe causation itself.
senses.exampleCN: 休谟追问我们是否真能观察到因果作用本身。
senses.why: Philosophy turned the relation into a principle. What is at stake is not this or that cause, but whether the link is necessary or merely customary.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把这种关系变成一条原理。争论的不是某一个原因，而是这条连接是必然的，还是仅仅是习惯性的。

senses.title: Legal causation
senses.definition: in law, the link between a person's act and a result for which they may be held responsible
senses.definitionCN: 法律中某人的行为与其可能须负责的结果之间的连接
senses.example: The court found no legal causation between the warning and the injury.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认定该警告与伤害之间不存在法律因果关系。
senses.why: Law narrows causation to what is fair to attribute. Not every physical link creates liability; the chain must be close enough to count.
senses.whyCN: 法律把因果收窄到“公平地归责”的范围。并非每条物理连接都产生责任，链条必须足够近才算数。

senses.title: Attributing an outcome to a source
senses.titleCN: 把结果归因于某个来源
senses.definition: the assignment of an observed result to a particular cause or set of causes
senses.definitionCN: 把观察到的结果指派给某个原因或一组原因
senses.example: Attribution of causation requires more than a single case.
senses.exampleCN: 因果归因需要的不只是一个案例。
senses.why: This is causation as a judgement we make, not a fact we see. The word covers the mental move from 'this happened' to 'that made it happen'.
senses.whyCN: 这是作为判断的因果，而不是被看见的事实。这个词覆盖了从“这件事发生了”到“那件事造成了它”的心智移动。

senses.title: A chain or mechanism of causes
senses.definition: a series of linked causes through which an effect is produced
senses.definitionCN: 产生某一结果的一连串相互连接的原因
senses.example: Historians reconstructed the chain of causation behind the famine.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家重建了那场饥荒背后的因果链。
senses.why: Complex outcomes rarely have one cause. The word then refers to the whole mechanism, the set of links that together produce the result.
senses.whyCN: 复杂结果很少只有一个原因。此时这个词指整个机制，也就是共同产生结果的那一组连接。

senses.title: The origins of a disease
senses.definition: in medicine and epidemiology, the factors that bring about a disease
senses.definitionCN: 医学与流行病学中导致疾病的各种因素
senses.example: Researchers still debate the causation of the syndrome.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者仍在争论这种综合征的成因。
senses.why: Medicine uses the word when it needs to separate what brings a condition about from what merely accompanies it. Cause and correlation must be told apart.
senses.whyCN: 医学在需要区分“造成某种状况”与“仅仅伴随它”时使用这个词。原因与相关必须被分开。

senses.title: Causal explanation in social science
senses.titleCN: 社会科学中的因果解释
senses.definition: in social research, the attempt to explain social outcomes by identifying their causes
senses.definitionCN: 社会研究中通过确认原因来解释社会结果的尝试
senses.example: The paper argues for multiple causation in urban poverty.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文主张城市贫困存在多因性。
senses.why: Social phenomena have many causes at once, so the word shifts from a single link to a field of interacting factors. The plural causations becomes thinkable.
senses.whyCN: 社会现象同时有许多原因，于是这个词从单一连接转向一组相互作用因素。复数形式 causations 也就变得可想了。

senses.title: Causation versus correlation
senses.definition: the relation that statistical association alone cannot establish
senses.definitionCN: 仅凭统计关联无法确立的那种关系
senses.example: The slogan 'correlation is not causation' warns against hasty inference.
senses.exampleCN: “相关不等于因果”这句口号警告人们不要草率推断。
senses.why: Statistics gave the word its sharpest modern contrast. Two variables can move together without one causing the other, and causation is the name of what is still missing.
senses.whyCN: 统计学给了这个词最尖锐的现代对照。两个变量可以一起变动而互不为因，causation 正是那个仍然缺失的东西的名字。

intro.en: Causation looks like a plain derivative of cause, but it entered English through a Latin noun with a different job. Latin causatio meant 'a pleading, an excuse', and the modern sense 'cause and effect relation' is an English development. This semantic shift is the main thing to notice.
intro.cn: causation 看起来只是 cause 的平实派生词，实际上它是经一个功能不同的拉丁名词进入英语的。拉丁语 causatio 意为“申辩、借口”，而现代“因果关系”义是英语自身的发展。这个语义偏移是此处最该注意的地方。

items.en: Causa meant 'cause, reason, motive', and also 'a judicial case'. English cause and the whole causal family descend from it, not from the unrelated casus 'a fall'.
items.cn: causa 意为“原因、理由、动机”，也指“司法案件”。英语 cause 与整个因果词族都出自它，而不是出自无关的 casus“落下”。

items.en: Causari meant 'to plead, to bring a case, to give as an excuse'. It came from causa in its legal sense, so the verb was about arguing, not about producing effects.
items.cn: causari 意为“申辩、提起诉讼、作为借口提出”。它来自法律义的 causa，因此这个动词讲的是争论，而不是产生结果。

items.en: Causatio, the noun of causari, meant 'a pleading, an excuse, a pretext'. It did not mean the relation between cause and effect, which is the sense English later gave the word.
items.cn: causatio 是 causari 的名词，意为“申辩、借口、托词”。它并不表示因与果的关系，后者是英语后来赋予这个词的意思。

items.en: English adopted causation in the 16th century. Early uses already concerned causing, but the abstract 'cause and effect' sense grew in philosophical writing rather than in law.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪采用 causation。早期用法已涉及“引起”，但抽象的“因与果”义是在哲学写作而非法律中成长起来的。

items.en: Hume and other philosophers made causation a central problem: is the link between events observed, or only inferred from habit? The word became a technical term of epistemology.
items.cn: 休谟等哲学家把因果问题推到中心：事件之间的连接是被观察到的，还是仅由习惯推断出来的？这个词成了认识论的术语。

items.en: Statistics, medicine and law each gave causation a narrower test. The slogan 'correlation is not causation' and the phrase chain of causation belong to the 20th century's effort to separate association from production.
items.cn: 统计学、医学与法律各自给了因果一套更窄的检验。“相关不等于因果”与“因果链”这两个说法，属于 20 世纪把“伴随”与“产生”分开的努力。

note.en: The three words cause, causal and causality sit very close to causation and are often confused. The first group sorts them by part of speech; the second group sorts the neighbouring ideas.
note.cn: cause、causal、causality 与 causation 距离很近，常被混淆。第一组按词性分开，第二组按相邻概念分开。

entries.definition: the principle or property of being causal. Causation is a relation between events; causality is the general capacity or law behind such relations.
entries.definitionCN: 具有因果性的原理或属性。causation 是事件之间的关系，causality 是这种关系背后的普遍能力或规律。

entries.definition: relating to a cause. It is the adjective that modifies links, factors and explanations.
entries.definitionCN: 与原因有关的。它是修饰连接、因素与解释的形容词。

entries.definition: the thing that produces an effect, or to produce one. Cause names one end of the relation; causation names the relation.
entries.definitionCN: 产生结果的事物，或产生结果。cause 命名关系的一端，causation 命名关系本身。

entries.definition: a mutual variation of two quantities. It is precisely what causation is often wrongly inferred from.
entries.definitionCN: 两个量之间的相互变化。它正是人们常错误推断出因果的那个东西。

entries.definition: the act of assigning a result to a source. It is the judgement side of causation.
entries.definitionCN: 把结果指派给某个来源的行为。它是因果的判断面。

entries.definition: the process by which something is fixed or decided. It can imply a stronger, more necessary link than causation.
entries.definitionCN: 某物被固定或决定的过程。它可以暗示比 causation 更强、更必然的连接。

entries.definition: the act of bringing something into existence. It stresses the first moment, not the whole causal link.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物开始存在的行为。它强调最初一刻，而不是整条因果连接。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the difference between cause, causation and causality visible, and attach the word to its standard phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩让 cause、causation、causality 的区别保持可见，并把词系到标准搭配上。

normal.en: See the build: cause + -ation, the noun of the process or relation.
normal.cn: 看见构成：cause 加 -ation，表示过程或关系的名词。

normal.en: Say the slogan: correlation is not causation. It fixes the word in its most useful contrast.
normal.cn: 念那句口号：相关不等于因果。它把这个词钉在最常用的对照里。

normal.en: Picture dominoes for chain of causation.
normal.cn: 用多米诺骨牌记 chain of causation。

normal.en: Keep the trio straight: cause is the thing, causal is the adjective, causation is the link.
normal.cn: 把三件套分清：cause 是事物，causal 是形容词，causation 是连接。

normal.en: In law, ask whether the link is close enough to count.
normal.cn: 在法律中，问这条连接是否近到足以算数。

abstract.en: Hold one line between two dots: the line is causation, the dots are cause and effect.
abstract.cn: 抓住两点之间的一条线：线是 causation，两端是原因与结果。

abstract.en: Sort the senses by discipline: philosophy, law, medicine, social science, statistics, everyday attribution.
abstract.cn: 按学科分组义项：哲学、法律、医学、社会科学、统计学、日常归因。

abstract.en: Remember the historical twist: the Latin noun meant 'excuse', not 'cause-effect link'.
abstract.cn: 记住历史转折：这个拉丁名词意为“借口”，不是“因果连接”。

examples.en: The researchers could not establish causation from the survey alone.
examples.cn: 研究者仅凭这项调查无法确立因果关系。

examples.en: Legal causation limits who can be held responsible for a harm.
examples.cn: 法律因果关系限定了谁可以为某项损害负责。

examples.en: Multiple causation is common in complex social problems.
examples.cn: 复杂社会问题中多因性很常见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“考贼神”：像“考”察案子的“贼”，要把“神”秘的因果链查清——causation 就是因果关系。

root: 拉丁语 causa“原因、理由、诉讼案件”，派生 causari“申辩”与 causatio“申辩、借口”；英语以 cause 加 -ation 构成 causation，并把词义从“申辩”转为“因果关系”。注意它与 casus“落下”无关。

sensesIntro.en: Causation is about a link rather than a thing. Cause names one end, effect names the other, and causation names the connection between them, together with all the questions that connection raises: is it necessary, is it close enough, is it observed or inferred, and is it one link or a whole chain?
sensesIntro.cn: causation 讲的是连接，而不是事物。cause 命名一端，effect 命名另一端，causation 命名它们之间的连接，以及这条连接引出的全部问题：它是否必然、是否足够近、是被观察还是被推断、是一条链还是一整张网。

core.en: The link that carries one event into another: cause at one end, effect at the other.
core.cn: 把一件事带成另一件事的连接：一端是原因，另一端是结果。

branches.en: THE LINK: the relation itself, the act of producing, and whole chains.
branches.cn: 连接：关系本身、产生行为，以及整条链。

branches.en: THE PRINCIPLE: causation as a law of how events work.
branches.cn: 原理：作为事件运行法则的因果。

branches.en: THE LEGAL TEST: a link close enough for responsibility.
branches.cn: 法律检验：近到足以产生责任的连接。

branches.en: THE JUDGEMENT: attributing outcomes, and explaining social ones.
branches.cn: 判断：归因结果，并解释社会结果。

branches.en: THE EVIDENCE: disease origins and the contrast with mere correlation.
branches.cn: 证据：疾病成因，以及与被单纯相关的对照。

intro.en: Causation is cause plus -ation, and the family keeps the Latin base causa across nouns, adjectives and verbs. The list shows how the same base yields cause, causal, causality and causative.
intro.cn: causation 是 cause 加 -ation，整个词族在名词、形容词、动词中保留拉丁词基 causa。清单展示同一词基如何生出 cause、causal、causality、causative。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries include the noun of cause, the verb of pleading, and the noun of pleading. The last two are essential because they explain why English causation looks like a legal word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目包括“原因”名词、“申辩”动词与“申辩”名词。后两者很关键，因为它们解释了为什么英语 causation 看起来像一个法律词。

items.meaning: the cause-effect relation; the act of causing
items.example: Causation is hard to prove from correlation.
items.exampleCN: 仅凭相关很难证明因果。

items.meaning: the source of an effect; a purpose or case
items.example: The cause of the fire was electrical.
items.exampleCN: 火灾的起因是电路问题。

items.example: There is a causal link between the two events.
items.exampleCN: 两个事件之间存在因果联系。

items.meaning: the principle or property of being causal
items.example: The argument questions causality itself.
items.exampleCN: 这一论证质疑因果性本身。

items.meaning: producing an effect; in grammar, expressing cause
items.example: The verb is used in a causative construction.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词用于使役结构。

items.meaning: in terms of cause and effect
items.example: The two factors are causally connected.
items.exampleCN: 这两个因素有因果联系。

items.example: They feared a causeless panic.
items.exampleCN: 他们担心一场无缘由的恐慌。

items.example: He left because the room was too hot.
items.exampleCN: 他离开是因为房间太热。

items.example: The causal chain runs from policy to outcome.
items.exampleCN: 因果链从政策延伸到结果。

items.meaning: a condition that contributes to an outcome
items.example: Smoking is a causal factor in the disease.
items.exampleCN: 吸烟是这种疾病的一个致因因素。

latinEntries.meaning: to plead, to give as an excuse
a pleading, an excuse, a pretext

definition_zh: 营养生长的；无性繁殖的；植物状态的；自主神经的（旧称）
definition_en: relating to growth and nutrition rather than reproduction; in medicine, lacking conscious activity; in older anatomy, involuntary
core_image: 一株植物只顾长根长叶，不开花也不结果，全部力气都花在「把身体做大」上
scene: 这株植物不靠种子，而靠地下横走的茎不断冒出新的植株；园艺上把这种繁殖方式与开花结果相区分。 The plant spreads by vegetative shoots rather than by seed.
sceneCN: 这里 vegetative 指「营养生长的、以根茎叶的伸长来繁殖的」（第 3 个义项：不经有性过程的营养繁殖）；句意为这株植物靠营养枝而非种子蔓延。

pos.zh: 营养生长的；无性繁殖的
（医学）植物状态的；无意识活动的
（旧称）自主神经的；不随意的

senses.title: Growing rather than reproducing
senses.titleCN: 只管长身体，不进入繁殖
senses.definition: concerned with growth and nutrition rather than with flowering or reproduction
senses.definitionCN: 与生长、营养有关，而非与开花繁殖有关
senses.example: Pruning shifts the tree from vegetative growth to fruit production.
senses.exampleCN: 修剪让这棵树从营养生长转向结果。
senses.why: Vegetative labels the part of a plant's life that builds the body; reproduction is the other part, and the two compete for the same energy.
senses.whyCN: vegetative 标出植物生命中「造身体」的那一半；繁殖是另一半，两者争夺同一份能量。

senses.title: A state without conscious activity
senses.titleCN: 只剩身体机能、没有意识的状态
senses.definition: a medical condition in which a person shows no conscious activity
senses.definitionCN: 人没有意识活动、只余身体机能的医学状态
senses.example: He remained in a vegetative state for months.
senses.exampleCN: 他在植物状态中躺了几个月。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the plant image: a body that breathes and digests but does not think is alive the way a plant is alive.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了植物的意象：会呼吸、会消化却不思考的身体，像植物那样活着。

senses.title: Reproduction by shoots, not seed
senses.titleCN: 用根茎叶直接长出新株的繁殖方式
senses.definition: reproduction by roots, stems or leaves rather than by seed
senses.definitionCN: 以根、茎、叶而非种子产生新个体的繁殖方式
senses.example: The plant spreads by vegetative shoots rather than by seed.
senses.exampleCN: 这株植物靠营养枝而非种子蔓延。
senses.why: Because a shoot carries the parent's full genetic make-up, botanists call this growth-as-reproduction, hence vegetative.
senses.whyCN: 因为一条枝带着母株的完整遗传信息，植物学家把这种「生长即繁殖」称为营养繁殖。

senses.title: The non-reproductive phase
senses.titleCN: 一生中尚未开花的阶段
senses.definition: the period of a plant's life before flowering begins
senses.definitionCN: 植物开花之前的那段生活史
senses.example: Long days shorten the vegetative phase in some cereals.
senses.exampleCN: 长日照缩短了某些谷物的营养生长期。
senses.why: Once a plant is timed by seasons, its life splits into a building phase and a breeding phase, and the first keeps the old name.
senses.whyCN: 一旦植物受季节支配，一生就分成「建造期」与「繁殖期」，前者沿用旧名。

senses.title: Propagation by cuttings
senses.titleCN: 用切下的枝叶根繁育新株
senses.definition: multiplication of plants from cuttings, division or grafting
senses.definitionCN: 用插条、分株或嫁接来增殖植株
senses.example: Gardeners use vegetative propagation for identical apples.
senses.exampleCN: 园艺师用营养繁殖得到一模一样的苹果。
senses.why: Horticulture needs copies, not offspring; a vegetative method copies the parent exactly, which is why the word is prized there.
senses.whyCN: 园艺要的是复制品而非后代；营养繁殖能精确复制母株，这正是这个词在园艺里受重视的原因。

senses.title: Dormant or resting plant tissue
senses.titleCN: 处于休眠、只维持生命的状态
senses.definition: of tissue, alive but resting and showing only basic maintenance
senses.definitionCN: 组织活着却休眠、只做基本维持
senses.example: A vegetative bud waits under the bark until spring.
senses.exampleCN: 一个营养芽在树皮下等到春天。
senses.why: When growth pauses without dying, the word describes the low setting of life rather than its absence.
senses.whyCN: 当生长停住却没死，这个词描述的是生命的低档运转，而不是生命的缺席。

senses.title: Of involuntary nerve function
senses.titleCN: 指不随意的神经活动（旧术语）
senses.definition: relating to the involuntary nervous system, an older medical usage
senses.definitionCN: 与不随意神经系统有关，属旧式医学用法
senses.example: Older texts call it the vegetative nervous system.
senses.exampleCN: 旧文献称其为自主神经系统。
senses.why: The older label treats digestion and circulation as the body's plant-like housekeeping, running without a decision.
senses.whyCN: 这个旧称把消化与循环看成身体「像植物一样的家务」，无需谁来做决定。

senses.title: Bare, monotonous, merely existing
senses.titleCN: 形容生活只剩吃喝睡、毫无波澜
senses.definition: describing a life or place that only maintains itself, with no interest or event
senses.definitionCN: 形容生活或地方只维持自身，没有兴致也没有事件
senses.example: The town felt vegetative, all routine and no occasion.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇显得沉闷，全是例行公事，没有一件值得说的事。
senses.why: The figurative use borrows the plant state: functions continue, but nothing is initiated, and the tone is mildly disparaging.
senses.whyCN: 比喻用法借的是植物状态：机能继续，却没有任何主动的开端，语气略带贬义。

intro.en: Vegetative comes from Medieval Latin vegetativus 'giving life, growing', from vegetare 'to enliven'. The medical and botanical uses split in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: vegetative 来自中世纪拉丁 vegetativus「赋予生命、促使生长」，源于 vegetare「使有生气」。医学与植物学的用法在 19 世纪分开。

items.en: Vegetare 'to enliven, animate' is the base verb, itself from vegetus 'lively'.
items.cn: vegetare「使有生气、使活动」是基础动词，再往前是 vegetus「有活力的」。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed vegetativus for the power that makes a body grow and stay alive.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁构出 vegetativus，指使身体生长并维持生命的力。

items.en: English took the adjective in the fourteenth century in the sense of 'giving life', applied to nourishment and warmth.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入这个形容词，义为「赋予生命的」，用于营养与温热。

items.en: From the eighteenth century botanists used it for growth opposed to reproduction, and the phrase vegetative reproduction followed.
items.cn: 18 世纪起，植物学家用它指与繁殖相对的生长，「营养繁殖」一语随后出现。

items.en: Nineteenth-century medicine applied it to patients who breathe but do not respond, and to the nerves that work without conscious control.
items.cn: 19 世纪医学把它用于会呼吸却无反应的病人，也用于不随意控制的神经。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates and root): the exact first English citation for each specialised sense is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of vegere remains unsettled, so any root form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与词根）：各专门义的确切首见书证并无定论；vegere 在拉丁语之前的来源亦未确定，凡给出的词根形式都是重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds adjectives and nouns that look alike but diverge in sense or root; group two holds words for unconscious or inactive states.
note.cn: 第一组是外形相近而词义或词根有别的形容词与名词；第二组指无意识或不活动的状态。

entries.definition: The mass noun for plant cover; the adjective describes the growing, non-reproductive side of plants.
entries.definitionCN: 指植物覆盖的集合名词；形容词则描述植物生长而非繁殖的一面。

entries.definition: Means 'of plants' in general, with no technical split between growth and reproduction.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指「植物的」，不含生长与繁殖的技术区分。

entries.definition: A person who eats no meat, built on vegetable from the same Latin stem but far from botany.
entries.definitionCN: 指不吃肉的人，由同出该拉丁词干的 vegetable 构成，与植物学已相距很远。

entries.definition: From vita 'life'; it means necessary for life, not plant-like growth.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 vita「生命」，意为维持生命所必需，不指植物式生长。

entries.definition: The general word for lacking awareness; vegetative is the narrower clinical stage.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指失去意识；vegetative 是更窄的临床分度。

entries.definition: Means unable to act or move, often of matter; it lacks the 'still alive' part.
entries.definitionCN: 指不能活动，多用于物质，缺了「仍然活着」这一层。

entries.definition: A resting state that will resume; vegetative tissue may also be dormant, but vegetative stresses maintenance.
entries.definitionCN: 指会恢复的休眠；营养组织也可能休眠，但 vegetative 强调维持。

entries.definition: A literal description with no Latin flavour; vegetative is the technical term for the same contrast.
entries.definitionCN: 字面描述，不带拉丁色彩；vegetative 是表达同一对照的术语。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations are the real Latin family and the real collocations of botany and medicine.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想是真实的拉丁词族，以及植物学与医学中的真实搭配。

normal.en: vegetare 'to enliven' + -ive: having the power to make grow.
normal.cn: vegetare「使有生气」+ -ive：具有使之生长的力。

normal.en: The family: vegetation, vegetate, vegetatively, vegetated.
normal.cn: 同族：vegetation、vegetate、vegetatively、vegetated。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: vegetative growth, vegetative reproduction, vegetative state.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：营养生长、营养繁殖、植物状态。

normal.en: Botany pairs it with reproductive: one builds the body, the other makes the seed.
normal.cn: 植物学把它与 reproductive 对举：一个造身体，一个结种子。

normal.en: Medicine reuses the plant image for a body that breathes but does not respond.
normal.cn: 医学把这套植物意象再用到会呼吸却无反应的身体上。

abstract.en: Picture a body lying still while its heartbeat keeps its own routine.
abstract.cn: 想象一具静止的身体，心跳照自己的常规走着。

abstract.en: Picture a tree that keeps widening but never bears fruit.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵不断长粗却从不结果的树。

abstract.en: Picture a machine set to idle, running but producing nothing.
abstract.cn: 想象一台调到怠速的机器，转着却不出活。

examples.en: Cut back the vegetative growth so the plant can flower.
examples.cn: 剪掉营养生长，让植物得以开花。

examples.en: The patient moved from a coma into a vegetative state.
examples.cn: 病人从昏迷进入植物状态。

examples.en: Strawberries propagate vegetatively by runners.
examples.cn: 草莓靠匍匐茎进行营养繁殖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「蔬菜（veget）+ 活着（ative）」——只会长身子、不开花 → 营养生长的；植物状态的

root: 中世纪拉丁 vegetativus「赋予生命、促使生长」，来自 vegetare「使有生气」；再往前为 vegetus「有活力的」，vegere 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all come from one contrast: growth and maintenance on one side, reproduction and conscious action on the other, until the word finally means merely existing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都来自同一个对照：一边是生长与维持，另一边是繁殖与有意识行动；最后这个词引申为「只是存在着」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plant spending everything on roots and leaves, never on flower or seed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一株植物把所有力气花在根和叶上，从不用在花与种子上。

branches.en: TWO SIDES: the adjective marks the growing half, then the half that stays alive without awareness.
branches.cn: 两面：形容词先标出「生长」的一半，再标出「活着却无意识」的一半。

branches.en: NO SEED: growth itself becomes a way of multiplying, and a phase before flowering.
branches.cn: 不结种：生长本身成了增殖方式，也成了开花前的阶段。

branches.en: GARDEN USE: cuttings copy a parent, while dormant tissue only waits.
branches.cn: 园艺用法：插条复制母株，休眠组织只是等待。

branches.en: OLD ANATOMY: housekeeping nerves run like plant functions, without decision.
branches.cn: 旧解剖学：家务式的神经像植物机能那样运转，无需决定。

branches.en: FIGURE: a life that maintains itself and initiates nothing.
branches.cn: 比喻：只维持自身、不发起任何事的生活。

intro.en: The adjective is a Latin participle stem plus -ive; the same stem builds the whole vegetation family.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是拉丁分词词干加 -ive；同一词干构成整个 vegetation 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin vegetare 'to enliven' yields vegetativus; -ivus marks a tendency or capacity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vegetare「使有生气」给出 vegetativus；-ivus 表示倾向或能力。

items.example: The stem is about life, not about plants alone.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干说的是生命，不只说植物。

items.example: Rain vegetates the slope.
items.exampleCN: 雨水使山坡有了生气。

items.meaning: tending to, having the power to
items.example: It names a capacity rather than an act.
items.exampleCN: 它命名的是能力，不是动作。

items.example: The word entered English from this form.
items.exampleCN: 英语正是从这个形式借入。

items.example: Vegetative shoots spread.
items.exampleCN: 营养枝蔓延。

items.example: The plant spreads vegetatively.
items.exampleCN: 这株植物以营养方式蔓延。

items.example: Moss vegetates on the wall.
items.exampleCN: 苔藓在墙上生长。

items.example: Vegetation covers the bank.
items.exampleCN: 植被覆盖河岸。

items.example: A vegetated strip filtered the runoff.
items.exampleCN: 一条长满植物的带子过滤了径流。

definition_zh: n. 集中化；中央集权化（英式拼写）
definition_en: the act of bringing power, control or activity under one centre; the British spelling
core_image: 所有箭头都从四面八方汇向一个点
scene: 政府把审批权收归一个部门，完成了彻底的集中化。 The government moved all approvals into one department, a complete centralisation.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：centralisation 指集中化；句意是政府把审批权收归一个部门。

pos.zh: 集中化；中央集权化

senses.title: Bringing things to one centre
senses.definition: the act of gathering control, records or services into a single place
senses.definitionCN: 把控制权、档案或服务集中到一处
senses.example: Centralisation of records cut waiting times.
senses.exampleCN: 档案集中使等候时间缩短。
senses.why: The word is built from centre plus the suffix of process.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 centre 加上表示过程的词缀构成。

senses.title: Political central power
senses.definition: the transfer of political authority from regions to a national centre
senses.definitionCN: 把政治权威从地方转移到国家中心
senses.example: The reform deepened centralisation in the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革加深了首都的中央集权。
senses.why: The political sense follows the general one of moving control inward.
senses.whyCN: 政治含义沿用把控制权向内收拢的一般含义。

intro.en: Centralisation builds on Latin centrum, a centre, through central and the verb centralise.
intro.cn: centralisation 经 central 与动词 centralise，建立在拉丁语 centrum（中心）之上。

items.en: Kentron names the sharp point of a compass.
items.cn: 希腊语 kentron 指圆规的尖点。

items.en: Centrum names the middle point of a circle.
items.cn: 拉丁语 centrum 指圆的中心。

items.en: English central means of the middle.
items.cn: 十七世纪 central 意为居中的。

items.en: The verb means to bring to one centre.
items.cn: 十九世纪动词意为集中到一处。

items.en: Centralisation names state control from a capital.
items.cn: 十九世纪指由国家首都统一控制。

items.en: The noun covers any gathering of control.
items.cn: 现代泛指任何控制权的集中。

note.en: The look-alike group swaps spelling or ending; the near-meaning group names concentration and its opposite.
note.cn: 形近组替换拼写或词尾；近义组列出集中及其反面。

entries.definition: The American spelling of the word.
entries.definitionCN: 美式拼写。

entries.definition: To bring under one centre.
entries.definitionCN: 使集中。

entries.definition: The state of being central.
entries.definitionCN: 中心性。

entries.definition: The act of bringing things together.
entries.definitionCN: 集中。

entries.definition: The joining of parts into one.
entries.definitionCN: 合并巩固。

entries.definition: Control held by a central body.
entries.definitionCN: 中央集权制。

normalIntro.en: Every arrow bends toward one point at the middle.
normalIntro.cn: 所有箭头都弯向中央的一点。

normal.en: Centrum means a centre.
normal.cn: centrum 意为中心。

normal.en: Central means of the middle.
normal.cn: central 意为居中的。

normal.en: Centralise means to gather inward.
normal.cn: centralise 意为向内收拢。

normal.en: The noun names the process.
normal.cn: 名词指这个过程。

normal.en: Its opposite adds de- to the front.
normal.cn: 反义词在前面加 de-。

abstract.en: A city pulling the threads of a country.
abstract.cn: 一座城牵动全国的线。

abstract.en: Power folding into one hand.
abstract.cn: 权力折进一只手。

abstract.en: A wheel with a single hub.
abstract.cn: 只有一个轮毂的轮子。

examples.en: Centralisation of buying saved the group money.
examples.cn: 集中采购为集团省了钱。

examples.en: Critics feared the centralisation of policing.
examples.cn: 批评者担心警务权被集中。

examples.en: The report traced a slow centralisation of power.
examples.cn: 报告追溯了权力缓慢集中的过程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「森戳来贼身」——森林里把东西都戳到中央来，一身集中在一点。

root: 希腊语 kentron（尖点）→ 拉丁语 centrum → central → centralise → centralisation

sensesIntro.en: The everyday sense gathers records and services; the political sense gathers authority.
sensesIntro.cn: 日常含义收拢档案与服务，政治含义收拢权威。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many arrows all bending toward a single hub
core.cn: 核心意象：许多箭头一齐弯向同一个轮毂

branches.en: Boxes of files carried to one basement.
branches.cn: 一箱箱档案搬进同一个地下室。

branches.en: One switchboard for a whole region.
branches.cn: 覆盖全区的同一台总机。

branches.en: A capital drafting rules for every province.
branches.cn: 首都为各省起草规则。

branches.en: A mayor waiting for a ministry reply.
branches.cn: 市长等着部里的答复。

branches.en: Scattered threads pulled into one knot.
branches.cn: 散线被拉成一个结。

definition_zh: 多普勒效应；波源与观测者相对运动引起接收频率变化的现象
definition_en: the change in the observed frequency of a wave caused by relative motion between the source and the observer
core_image: 一辆鸣笛的车从身边驶过，靠近时音调升高，远去时音调降低
scene: 十字路口，救护车鸣着笛驶近又远去，站在路边的人听到音调先升后降。 A passing siren is a familiar example of the Doppler effect.
sceneCN: 这里指「因波源与观测者相对运动而使接收频率改变的现象」（第 1 个义项：靠近时频率升高、远离时降低）；句意为驶过鸣笛声的音调变化就是多普勒效应的常见例子。图中可辨识物件：救护车、鸣笛、路边行人、车道。

senses.title: Frequency change from relative motion
senses.titleCN: 相对运动引起的频率变化
senses.definition: the general principle that relative motion between source and observer changes the observed frequency of a wave
senses.definitionCN: 波源与观测者相对运动改变所观测到的波频率的一般原理
senses.example: A passing siren is a familiar example of the Doppler effect.
senses.exampleCN: 驶过的鸣笛声是多普勒效应的常见例子。
senses.why: Doppler names the physicist who described the principle, and effect names the phenomenon he explained.
senses.whyCN: Doppler 指描述这一原理的物理学家，effect 指他所解释的现象。

senses.title: Acoustic Doppler effect
senses.definition: the rise and fall of pitch heard when a sound source passes by
senses.definitionCN: 声源驶过时听到的音调先升后降
senses.example: The Doppler effect makes the train horn drop in pitch as it leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 多普勒效应使火车鸣笛在离去时音调下降。
senses.why: sound was the first case Doppler studied, so the acoustic use is the oldest working sense.
senses.whyCN: 声音是多普勒最早研究的情形，因此声学用法是最早的实用义项。

senses.title: Optical Doppler effect
senses.definition: the shift of spectral lines caused by the motion of a light source
senses.definitionCN: 光源运动造成的谱线位移
senses.example: The optical Doppler effect turns motion into a measurable colour shift.
senses.exampleCN: 光学多普勒效应把运动变成可测量的颜色位移。
senses.why: light obeys the same relative-motion rule as sound, but the result is read as wavelength rather than pitch.
senses.whyCN: 光遵守与声音相同的相对运动规则，只是结果读作波长而非音调。

senses.title: Doppler radar speed measurement
senses.definition: the use of reflected radio waves to measure the speed of an object
senses.definitionCN: 利用反射回来的无线电波测量物体速度
senses.example: The Doppler effect lets a radar gun read the speed of a car.
senses.exampleCN: 多普勒效应让测速雷达读出汽车的速度。
senses.why: a moving target returns a shifted echo, so the principle becomes an instrument.
senses.whyCN: 运动目标返回带位移的回波，于是原理变成了仪器。

senses.title: The frequency shift itself
senses.definition: the difference between the emitted and the received frequency
senses.definitionCN: 发出频率与接收频率之间的差
senses.example: The Doppler effect here amounts to a few kilohertz.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的多普勒效应相当于几千赫兹的频移。
senses.why: metonymy turns the principle into the amount it produces, which is what instruments record.
senses.whyCN: 借代把原理转指它所产生的那份量，而仪器记录的正是这份量。

senses.title: Medical Doppler ultrasound
senses.definition: the use of Doppler ultrasound to detect the direction and speed of blood flow
senses.definitionCN: 用多普勒超声检测血流的方向与速度
senses.example: The Doppler effect lets the scanner show blood moving through a valve.
senses.exampleCN: 多普勒效应让扫描仪显示血液流过瓣膜。
senses.why: moving blood reflects sound with a shift, so the principle became a bedside diagnostic.
senses.whyCN: 流动的血液反射声音时带有位移，于是原理成了床旁诊断手段。

senses.title: Weather Doppler radar
senses.definition: the use of Doppler radar to map the motion of rain and wind inside storms
senses.definitionCN: 用多普勒雷达绘制风暴内雨滴与风的运动
senses.example: Weather services rely on the Doppler effect to see rotation inside a storm.
senses.exampleCN: 气象部门依靠多普勒效应观察风暴内部的旋转。
senses.why: the same echo shift that measures a car also measures falling rain, scaled up to a whole storm.
senses.whyCN: 测量汽车的同一回波位移也能测量落雨，只是尺度放大到整个风暴。

senses.title: Figurative perceptual bias
senses.titleCN: 借喻：相对运动造成的感知偏差
senses.definition: a borrowed use for any distortion produced by the relative movement of observer and event
senses.definitionCN: 借指观察者与事件相对运动所造成的一切失真
senses.example: Memory has its own Doppler effect: the faster life moves, the more the past changes pitch.
senses.exampleCN: 记忆有自己的多普勒效应：生活越快，过去音调变得越多。
senses.why: the principle makes perception depend on the observer's motion, and that idea transfers readily to human experience.
senses.whyCN: 这一原理使感知取决于观察者的运动，这一观念很容易迁移到人的经验中。

intro.en: Doppler effect is an eponym: the surname Doppler plus the Latin-derived noun effect. The principle was published in 1842. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: Doppler effect 是冠名词：姓氏 Doppler 加拉丁来源的名词 effect。这一原理于 1842 年发表。年代均为约数。

items.en: Effect descends from Latin effectus, the past participle of efficere 'to bring about', built on ex- 'out' plus facere 'to do, make'.
items.cn: effect 来自拉丁 effectus，即 efficere「促成」的过去分词，由 ex-「出」加 facere「做、造」构成。

items.en: Effectus meant 'a doing, a result', and English effect kept both the sense of result and the sense of bringing something about.
items.cn: effectus 意为「做成、结果」，英语 effect 同时保留了「结果」与「促成」两层意思。

items.en: Christian Doppler, an Austrian physicist, published the principle in 1842, first for sound and then for light.
items.cn: 奥地利物理学家克里斯蒂安·多普勒于 1842 年发表这一原理，先论声音，再论光。

items.en: Experiments with moving sound sources and with starlight confirmed the effect within the following decades.
items.cn: 随后数十年间，用运动声源与星光的实验证实了这一效应。

items.en: Radar, ultrasound and astronomy turned the eponym into a family of instruments and techniques.
items.cn: 雷达、超声与天文学把这个冠名词变成了一整套仪器与技术。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the surname Doppler has a regional Germanic origin whose exact form is uncertain, and the pre-Latin origin of facere is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：姓氏 Doppler 有地区性的日耳曼语来源，确切形式不确定；facere 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds the related technical labels that are often used interchangeably; group two holds the everyday words for the same experience.
note.cn: 第一组是常被互换使用的相关技术标签；第二组是描述同一经验的日常词。

entries.definition: The frequency difference itself; the Doppler effect is the principle, and the shift is its numerical result.
entries.definitionCN: 频率差本身；多普勒效应是原理，频移是其数值结果。

entries.definition: A radar that applies the effect; the name belongs to the device, not to the physics.
entries.definitionCN: 应用这一效应的雷达；名称属于设备，而非物理原理。

entries.definition: The long-wavelength half of the optical Doppler effect, also produced by cosmic expansion.
entries.definitionCN: 光学多普勒效应的长波一半，也可由宇宙膨胀产生。

entries.definition: Any result or outcome; only the eponym fixes it to relative motion and waves.
entries.definitionCN: 任何结果或后果；只有加上冠名才限定为相对运动与波。

entries.definition: The everyday description of the acoustic case; it says nothing about the underlying wave physics.
entries.definitionCN: 对声学情形的日常描述；不涉及背后的波动原理。

entries.definition: The neutral technical name for any change in observed frequency, whatever its cause.
entries.definitionCN: 任何观测频率变化的中性技术名称，不论成因。

entries.definition: Motion of source and observer with respect to each other; it is the condition, not the effect.
entries.definitionCN: 波源与观测者相对彼此的运动；它是条件，而非效应。

entries.definition: Crests arriving closer together, which raises the observed frequency.
entries.definitionCN: 波峰来得更密，从而提高观测频率。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real physics, real instruments and real eponym usage, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的物理、真实的仪器与真实的冠名用法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Approach raises pitch; recession lowers it.
normal.cn: 靠近时音调升高；远离时音调降低。

normal.en: The effect is named after Christian Doppler, who published it in 1842.
normal.cn: 这一效应以 1842 年发表它的克里斯蒂安·多普勒命名。

normal.en: Radar guns, weather radar and medical ultrasound all run on it.
normal.cn: 测速雷达、气象雷达与医用超声都靠它工作。

normal.en: In light the effect is read as redshift or blueshift.
normal.cn: 在光中，这一效应读作红移或蓝移。

normal.en: The effect is the principle; the shift is the number.
normal.cn: 效应是原理；频移是数值。

abstract.en: Picture a runner passing a ringing bell and hearing it fall silent behind.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者经过一只响铃，听见铃声在身后低落。

abstract.en: Picture two trains passing, each hearing the other's horn change key.
abstract.cn: 想象两列火车交会，彼此听见对方的汽笛变了调。

abstract.en: Picture a memory that changes tone depending on how fast you revisit it.
abstract.cn: 想象一段记忆，因你回访的快慢而改变色调。

examples.en: The Doppler effect explains why the siren drops in pitch as the ambulance passes.
examples.cn: 多普勒效应解释了救护车驶过时警笛音调为何下降。

examples.en: Astronomers use the Doppler effect to measure the rotation of galaxies.
examples.cn: 天文学家利用多普勒效应测量星系的旋转。

examples.en: Doppler ultrasound detects the direction of blood flow through a valve.
examples.cn: 多普勒超声检测血液流过瓣膜的方向。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「Doppler（物理学家多普勒）+ effect（效应）」——他描述的运动改变音调现象 → 多普勒效应

root: 姓氏 Doppler（奥地利物理学家，1842 年发表该原理）+ 拉丁 effectus「结果」，后者来自 efficere「促成」= ex-「出」+ facere「做、造」；facere 更深来源不确定，Doppler 姓氏的日耳曼语来源形式存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one principle: relative motion changes frequency, heard as pitch, seen as colour, used by radar, measured as a shift, applied to blood, applied to storms and finally borrowed for perception.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一条原理：相对运动改变频率，听成音调、看成颜色、用于雷达、量成频移、用于血流、用于风暴，最后借用于感知。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a siren passing a listener, its pitch rising as it comes and falling as it goes.
core.cn: 核心意象：警笛经过听者，来时音调升高，去时音调降低。

branches.en: PRINCIPLE AND AMOUNT: the rule and the number it yields.
branches.cn: 原理与数值：规则本身，以及它给出的数。

branches.en: SOUND: the oldest and most familiar case.
branches.cn: 声音：最古老也最熟悉的情形。

branches.en: LIGHT AND STORMS: wavelength shifts and radar echoes share one rule.
branches.cn: 光与风暴：波长位移与雷达回波共用一条规则。

branches.en: INSTRUMENTS: speed guns and ultrasound turn the rule into a reading.
branches.cn: 仪器：测速枪与超声把规则变成读数。

branches.en: PERCEPTION: what is observed depends on how the observer moves.
branches.cn: 感知：观测到什么，取决于观测者怎样运动。

intro.en: The term joins a surname to a Latin-derived noun, so only the second half has a morphological family.
intro.cn: 这个术语把姓氏与一个拉丁来源的名词连接起来，因此只有后半有形态词族。

latinIntro.en: Effectus and efficere come from ex- plus facere; the same root builds effect, effective, efficient and factory.
latinIntro.cn: effectus 与 efficere 来自 ex- 加 facere；同一词根还构成 effect、effective、efficient 与 factory。

items.meaning: the physicist who described the principle
items.meaningCN: 描述这一原理的物理学家
items.example: Doppler published the principle in 1842.
items.exampleCN: 多普勒于 1842 年发表这一原理。

items.meaning: a result produced by a cause
items.example: The effect was easy to hear.
items.exampleCN: 这一效应很容易听见。

items.example: The Latin verb underlies the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词支撑整个词族。

items.example: The method proved effective.
items.exampleCN: 这个方法被证明有效。

items.meaning: in a way that produces a result
items.example: The two cases are effectively the same.
items.exampleCN: 这两种情形实际上是同一回事。

items.example: They tested the effectiveness of the coating.
items.exampleCN: 他们测试了涂层的有效性。

items.example: The Doppler shift was a few kilohertz.
items.exampleCN: 多普勒频移是几千赫兹。

items.example: Doppler radar tracked the storm.
items.exampleCN: 多普勒雷达追踪了风暴。

items.meaning: a place where things are made
items.example: The root facere also hides in factory.
items.exampleCN: 词根 facere 也藏在 factory 里。

definition_zh: 岩体；岩石构造（地表上可辨认形状或层序的一块岩石）
definition_en: a recognizable mass, shape, or layered body of rock, especially one seen at the earth's surface
core_image: 荒漠中一座被风削成拱门的独立岩体
scene: 沙漠公路旁，风把砂岩削成一座孤立的拱门，游客在拱下拍照： Wind and sand had carved the rock formation into a freestanding arch.
sceneCN: 这里 rock formation 指「一块形状可辨认的独立岩体」（第 1 个义项：地表上可辨认形状的一块岩体）；句意为风与沙把这处岩体雕成一座独立的拱门。

pos.zh: 岩体；岩石构造（可数，复数为 rock formations）

derivatives.zh: 多岩石的；像岩石般坚硬的

senses.title: A recognizable mass of rock
senses.titleCN: 形状可辨认的一块岩体
senses.definition: a body of rock with a shape or outline distinct enough to be seen and named as one thing
senses.definitionCN: 形状或轮廓足够分明、可被视为一个整体并加以命名的一块岩石
senses.example: Wind and sand had carved the rock formation into a freestanding arch.
senses.exampleCN: 风与沙把这处岩体雕成一座独立的拱门。
senses.why: Formation here does not mean the process but the shaped result: a mass whose outline has become recognizable.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 formation 不指过程，而指塑形后的结果：轮廓已变得可辨认的一块岩体。

senses.title: A conspicuous feature in a landscape
senses.titleCN: 地貌中突出的岩体景观
senses.definition: a rock mass that stands out as a landmark against the surrounding land
senses.definitionCN: 在周围地形中作为地标突出的岩体
senses.example: The rock formation dominated the valley for miles around.
senses.exampleCN: 这处岩体在数英里内俯瞰整个山谷。
senses.why: What makes it a formation rather than rubble is contrast: it resists erosion and therefore rises above its surroundings.
senses.whyCN: 使它成为岩体而非碎石的，是对比：它抗蚀而高出周围地面。

senses.title: A layered sequence of rock
senses.definition: a stack of visible layers that records successive episodes of deposition
senses.definitionCN: 记录一次次沉积事件的可见层状叠置体
senses.example: The rock formation shows a hundred thin bands of shale.
senses.exampleCN: 这处岩体显出一百条薄薄的页岩层带。
senses.why: The word formation keeps its Latin sense of shaping, and layers are the visible trace of that shaping.
senses.whyCN: formation 保留了拉丁语「塑形」之义，而层理正是这一塑形过程的可见痕迹。

senses.title: The process of rock being made
senses.definition: the natural process by which sediment, lava, or magma becomes solid rock
senses.definitionCN: 沉积物、熔岩或岩浆变为坚固岩石的自然过程
senses.example: The rock formation process began with ash falling into a lake.
senses.exampleCN: 岩石形成过程始于火山灰落入湖中。
senses.why: English allows both readings, so context alone decides whether the phrase names the thing or the making of it.
senses.whyCN: 英语容许两种读法，因此只能靠上下文判断短语指成品还是指制造过程。

senses.title: A mapped rock unit
senses.definition: a body of rock drawn and labelled on a geological map for study
senses.definitionCN: 为研究而在地质图上绘出并标注的岩体
senses.example: Each rock formation on the map has its own colour.
senses.exampleCN: 图上的每一处岩体都有自己的颜色。
senses.why: Survey geologists reduce a three-dimensional body to a coloured shape, and the phrase follows the map.
senses.whyCN: 测量地质学家把三维岩体压缩为彩色图形，这个短语也随之上了地图。

senses.title: An erosional remnant
senses.definition: an isolated pillar, arch, or knob left standing after the softer rock around it has worn away
senses.definitionCN: 周围较软岩石被蚀去后孤立残留的石柱、拱门或石丘
senses.example: The isolated rock formation is all that remains of a former plateau.
senses.exampleCN: 这处孤立岩体是昔日高原仅存的部分。
senses.why: Erosion removes the weak and leaves the strong, so a formation can be read as a negative image of what has been lost.
senses.whyCN: 侵蚀带走软弱部分、留下坚硬部分，因此岩体可读作「已失去之物」的反像。

senses.title: A climbing or visitor attraction
senses.definition: a rock mass used for climbing, photography, or tourism because of its shape
senses.definitionCN: 因其形状而被用于攀岩、摄影或旅游的岩体
senses.example: Climbers travel to the rock formation for its long crack.
senses.exampleCN: 攀岩者为那条长裂缝专程来到这处岩体。
senses.why: Once a shape becomes famous, the phrase shifts from geology to recreation without changing its referent.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某形状出了名，这个短语就从地质学转向休闲用途，而所指对象并未改变。

senses.title: Abstract: a structure slowly assembled
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：缓慢拼合而成的结构
senses.definition: any structure that appears solid but was assembled piece by piece over time
senses.definitionCN: 任何看似坚固、实则由时间中逐块拼合而成的结构
senses.example: The organization grew like a rock formation, one layer of rules at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 这个组织像岩体一样生长，一次添一层规则。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the key contrast: hard and permanent on the outside, gradual and layered in its history.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻保留了关键对比：外表坚硬恒久，历史却渐进且分层。

intro.en: Rock formation joins a word of uncertain origin to a Latin-derived noun. The geological use is nineteenth-century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: rock formation 把一个来源不确定的词与一个拉丁语来源的名词组合起来。地质用法形成于 19 世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Source uncertain: rock appears in Middle English, probably through Old North French roque from Vulgar Latin rocca. The deeper origin of rocca is unknown, so any further root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：rock 见于中古英语，可能经古北部法语 roque 来自通俗拉丁语 rocca。rocca 的更深来源不明，凡再往上推的词根均属重构形式。

items.en: Formation rests on Latin forma 'shape' and formare 'to shape'. Forma itself is of uncertain origin; a Greek connection has been suggested but not demonstrated.
items.cn: formation 依托拉丁语 forma「形状」与 formare「塑形」。forma 本身来源不确定；与希腊语的关联只是提出过，未获证明。

items.en: Formatio named a shaping or a shape in Latin, and English took the noun through Old French formation.
items.cn: formatio 在拉丁语中指塑形或形状，英语经古法语 formation 借入这个名词。

items.en: In the eighteenth century naturalists described 'rocks' and their 'formations' separately, the first as material and the second as arrangement.
items.cn: 18 世纪博物学家把「岩石」与「其构造」分开描述，前者指材料，后者指排列。

items.en: By the nineteenth century rock formation was common in survey reports for a conspicuous mass, while geological formation served as the formal stratigraphic label.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，rock formation 在测量报告中常指显眼的岩体，而 geological formation 则用作正式地层标签。

items.en: The tourist sense is twentieth-century and its first recorded use is not pinned down, so the date is uncertain.
items.cn: 旅游义产生于 20 世纪，其最早书证尚未确定，因此年代存疑。

note.en: Group one holds labels from geology and tourism that are often confused with the phrase; group two holds ordinary words for rock masses.
note.cn: 第一组是常与该短语混淆的地质与旅游标签；第二组是普通岩石体的日常用词。

entries.definition: The formal stratigraphic term for a named body of rock; rock formation is looser and often visual.
entries.definitionCN: 命名岩体的正式地层术语；rock formation 更宽松，常偏重视觉形状。

entries.definition: The visible part of bedrock at the surface; it may be small and need not form a landmark.
entries.definitionCN: 基岩在地表的可见部分，可以很小，也不必形成地标。

entries.definition: A body of rock treated as one item on a map, whether or not it has a dramatic shape.
entries.definitionCN: 在地图上作为一个项目处理的岩体，不论其形状是否醒目。

entries.definition: The solid rock beneath soil and loose material; it is a position in the stack, not a shape.
entries.definitionCN: 土壤与松散物之下的坚固岩石；它指层序中的位置，而非形状。

entries.definition: One large detached block of rock; a formation is still attached and usually much larger.
entries.definitionCN: 一块脱离母岩的大石；岩体仍与原岩相连，且通常大得多。

entries.definition: A steep rock face, especially at a coast; it describes the surface, not the whole body.
entries.definitionCN: 陡峭岩面，尤指海岸处；它描述表面，而非整个岩体。

entries.definition: A single massive stone or a structure cut from one; a formation may consist of many layers.
entries.definitionCN: 单块巨石或由单石凿成的构筑物；岩体可由许多层组成。

entries.definition: Any natural shape of the land surface, including valleys and dunes, not only rock.
entries.definitionCN: 地表任何自然形状，包括谷地与沙丘，不限于岩石。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real geological labels and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实语素、真实地质标签与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Rock is the material; formation is the shape. The phrase names a shape made of material.
normal.cn: rock 是材料，formation 是形状；短语指由材料构成的形状。

normal.en: Compare geological formation: there the stress is on stratigraphic classification, here on the visible mass.
normal.cn: 与 geological formation 比较：后者强调地层分类，这里强调可见岩体。

normal.en: Famous examples are named shapes: Delicate Arch, Old Harry Rocks, the Pillars of Hercules.
normal.cn: 著名例子都是命名的形状：精致拱门、老哈里岩、海格力斯之柱。

normal.en: A formation can be an arch, a pillar, a wall, or a stack of layers; all are outlines.
normal.cn: 岩体可以是拱门、石柱、岩壁或层叠体，共同点都是轮廓。

normal.en: The phrase takes a plural for a group: a cluster of rock formations.
normal.cn: 指一组时用复数：a cluster of rock formations。

abstract.en: Picture a sandcastle that survives the tide because one tower was packed harder than the rest.
abstract.cn: 想象一座沙堡，因为一座塔拍得比别处更实，退潮后仍立着。

abstract.en: Picture a wall built one stone per year, still standing after a lifetime.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵墙每年只添一块石，一辈子后仍然立着。

abstract.en: Picture a reputation that looks like one solid block but was layered by many small acts.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名声看似整块实心，实由许多小事层层堆成。

examples.en: Wind and sand had carved the rock formation into a freestanding arch.
examples.cn: 风与沙把这处岩体雕成一座独立的拱门。

examples.en: The ranger warned visitors not to climb the fragile rock formation.
examples.cn: 巡护员提醒游客不要攀爬这处易损岩体。

examples.en: Each rock formation on the map is coloured by its age.
examples.cn: 地图上每一处岩体都按年代着色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rock（岩石）+ formation（形成物）」——岩石被自然做成的一个有形的东西 → 岩体、岩石构造

root: rock 来源不确定，可能经古北部法语 roque 来自通俗拉丁语 rocca，rocca 更深来源不明；formation 来自拉丁语 formatio「形成」，源自 forma「形状」与 formare「塑形」，forma 亦来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a visible mass to its making, its mapping, its erosion, its fame, and finally to any slowly assembled structure.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从可见岩体出发，依次涉及它的形成、测绘、侵蚀、名声，最后落到一切缓慢拼合的结构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single mass of rock whose outline can be recognized from a distance.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块从远处就能认出轮廓的岩体。

branches.en: SHAPE AND CONTRAST: an outline becomes a landmark only because it differs from what surrounds it.
branches.cn: 形状与对比：轮廓之所以成为地标，只因它与周围不同。

branches.en: STACK AND PROCESS: the visible layers and the making that produced them are two readings of one phrase.
branches.cn: 层叠与过程：可见层理与造成它的过程，是同一短语的两种读法。

branches.en: MAP LABEL: survey geology turns the mass into a coloured shape with a name.
branches.cn: 地图标签：测量地质学把岩体变成有名字的彩色图形。

branches.en: REMNANT: erosion leaves the hard part standing as a negative record of what vanished.
branches.cn: 残体：侵蚀留下坚硬部分，作为消失之物的反向记录。

branches.en: PUBLIC AND METAPHOR: a famous shape becomes a destination, and any slow-built structure can borrow the image.
branches.cn: 公众与比喻：著名形状成为目的地，任何缓慢建成的结构都可借用这一意象。

intro.en: The phrase is an English noun plus a Latin-derived noun, so each half can be read on its own.
intro.cn: 这个短语是英语名词加拉丁语来源名词，两半都可单独读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin forma and formatio stand behind formation; rock itself has no settled Latin source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 forma 与 formatio 支撑 formation；rock 本身没有确定的拉丁语来源。

items.structure: Middle English rock, probably from Old North French roque
items.example: The rock split along a straight crack.
items.exampleCN: 岩石沿一条直裂缝裂开。

items.meaning: full of rocks or as hard as rock
items.example: The rocky slope slowed the climbers.
items.exampleCN: 多石的坡面拖慢了攀登者。

items.example: The drill reached bedrock at ten metres.
items.exampleCN: 钻头在十米处触及基岩。

items.meaning: the act or result of shaping
items.example: The formation of the arch took ages of wind.
items.exampleCN: 拱门的形成历经漫长风蚀。

items.example: The layers form a stepped wall.
items.exampleCN: 这些层构成一堵阶梯状的墙。

items.example: The formative stage of the arch was slow.
items.exampleCN: 这座拱门的形成阶段很缓慢。

items.meaning: a natural shape of the land
items.example: The arch is a striking landform.
items.exampleCN: 这座拱门是醒目的地貌。

items.example: An outcrop showed where the layer began.
items.exampleCN: 一处露头显示该层从哪里开始。

definition_zh: 艺术作品；（书刊、广告中的）插图与图稿；美术品
definition_en: a work of art, especially a painting, drawing or sculpture, or the illustrations and graphic material prepared for publication
core_image: 一块被反复修改的表面，最后以固定的形状离开工作室，进入别人的眼睛
scene: 印刷厂里，编辑把封面图的文件放大，逐条检查线条。 The editor enlarged the artwork to check every line before the press run.
sceneCN: 这里 artwork 指「交给印刷厂的成稿图稿」（第 4 个义项：可供制版复制的图形材料）；句意为编辑把封面图稿放大，在开印前逐条检查线条。

pos.zh: 艺术作品（可数）；插图、图稿（不可数或可数）；美术品

collocations.zh: 封面图稿；封面艺术设计

derivatives.zh: artwork + -ed（分词形容词）→ 经过图稿加工的；从「成品」转到「加工状态」
artwork + -er（人）→ 图稿制作员；从「成品」转到「制作成品的人」
artwork + -ing（动作）→ 图稿制作；从「物件」转到「工序」

senses.title: A single work of art
senses.definition: a painting, drawing, sculpture or similar piece made as art
senses.definitionCN: 作为艺术品创作的绘画、素描、雕塑或类似作品
senses.example: The museum bought the artwork at auction.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆在拍卖会上买下了这件艺术作品。
senses.why: Artwork is simply art plus work, so the compound names a made thing belonging to the category of art: one countable object.
senses.whyCN: artwork 就是 art 加 work，复合词命名一件属于艺术类别的制成品：一个可数的物件。

senses.title: An artist's output as a whole
senses.titleCN: 某位艺术家的全部作品
senses.definition: the collected pieces made by one artist, treated as a body of work
senses.definitionCN: 某位艺术家创作的全部作品，作为一个整体来看
senses.example: The retrospective gathered artwork from forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这场回顾展汇集了四十年的作品。
senses.why: The uncountable use drops the count and keeps the material: the same word now names the whole body rather than one piece.
senses.whyCN: 不可数用法取消了计数，只保留「作品实体」：同一个词现在指整个作品群，而不是单件。

senses.title: Illustrations in a publication
senses.definition: the pictures and drawings prepared to accompany printed text
senses.definitionCN: 为配合印刷文字而准备的图画与插图
senses.example: The novel's artwork was drawn by a single illustrator.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说的插图全部由一位插画师绘制。
senses.why: Publishing borrowed the word because illustrations are art made to work inside a page: the aesthetic object becomes part of a printed job.
senses.whyCN: 出版业借用这个词，因为插图是「在页面里工作的艺术」：审美对象成了印刷品的一部分。

senses.title: Print-ready graphic material
senses.definition: the finished graphic material supplied to a printer for reproduction
senses.definitionCN: 交给印刷厂用于复制的完成图形材料
senses.example: The editor enlarged the artwork to check every line before the press run.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑把封面图稿放大，在开印前逐条检查线条。
senses.why: In the print trade the word narrows to what the press needs: not the idea but the camera-ready surface from which copies are made.
senses.whyCN: 在印刷业中，这个词收窄为印刷机所需之物：不是构思，而是用来复制的那块可制版表面。

senses.title: A digital image or file
senses.definition: an image or layered file made and stored on a computer
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机上制作并保存的图像或分层文件
senses.example: Keep the layered artwork so the type can be changed later.
senses.exampleCN: 保留分层图稿，以便日后修改文字。
senses.why: When production moved to screens, artwork named the editable file rather than the physical surface; the material changed, the function did not.
senses.whyCN: 当制作转移到屏幕上，artwork 指的可编辑文件而非实体表面；材料变了，功能没变。

senses.title: Decoration on a product or package
senses.titleCN: 产品与包装上的装饰图案
senses.definition: the designed pictures or patterns printed on an object or its packaging
senses.definitionCN: 印在物件或其包装上的设计图案
senses.example: The biscuit tin's artwork copies a Victorian print.
senses.exampleCN: 饼干盒上的图案模仿了一幅维多利亚时期的版画。
senses.why: Commercial design applies the print sense to packaging: the image still exists to be reproduced, but now it sells the object beneath it.
senses.whyCN: 商业设计把印刷义用到包装上：图像仍为复制而存在，只是现在用来推销它下面的商品。

senses.title: Visual design for a screen work
senses.titleCN: 影视、游戏等作品的视觉设计
senses.definition: the visual design of a film, game or performance, including concept pieces
senses.definitionCN: 电影、游戏或演出中的视觉设计，包括概念图
senses.example: The game's artwork borrows from woodblock prints.
senses.exampleCN: 这款游戏的视觉设计借鉴了木版画。
senses.why: The word follows images into new media: concept drawings and textures are artworks made to serve a larger screened work.
senses.whyCN: 这个词跟着图像进入新媒介：概念图与贴图都是为更大的屏幕作品服务的图稿。

senses.title: The original object, not a copy
