senses.definition: the physical piece made by the artist, as opposed to a reproduction
senses.definitionCN: 艺术家亲手制作的实体作品，区别于复制品
senses.example: Collectors pay for the artwork itself, not the poster.
senses.exampleCN: 收藏者付钱买的是原作本身，而不是海报。
senses.why: Because artwork names the made object, museums and dealers use it to insist on the original surface rather than its image.
senses.whyCN: 因为 artwork 命名的是被制作出来的物件，博物馆与画商便用它强调原初表面，而非其图像复制。

intro.en: Artwork is an English compound of art and work, recorded from 1847 and possibly modelled on German Kunstwerk; both parts are old, but the compound is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: artwork 是 art 与 work 的英语复合词，1847 年有记录，可能以德语 Kunstwerk 为模板；两部分都很古老，复合词却是现代产物。年代均为约数。

items.en: Art goes back through Old French to Latin ars, artis 'skill, craft', whose deeper root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: art 经古法语上溯拉丁 ars、artis「技艺、手艺」，其更早词根属重构。

items.en: Work descends from Old English weorc 'deed, something made', from Proto-Germanic *werka- and the root *werg- 'to do'.
items.cn: work 来自古英语 weorc「行为、制成之物」，上溯原始日耳曼语 *werka- 与词根 *werg-「做」。

items.en: German Kunstwerk 'work of art' joins Kunst 'art' and Werk 'work'; the English compound may have followed this model, though the model is not certain.
items.cn: 德语 Kunstwerk「艺术作品」由 Kunst「艺术」与 Werk「作品」合成；英语复合词可能沿此模板，但模板本身并不确定。

items.en: Art-work is recorded in 1847 in the sense 'artistic work; paintings, drawings and similar pieces'.
items.cn: art-work 于 1847 年有记录，意为「艺术性的作品；绘画、素描一类」。

items.en: In twentieth-century printing, artwork narrowed to the finished graphic material from which copies are reproduced.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪的印刷业，artwork 收窄为可供复制成品的图形材料。

items.en: From the late twentieth century the word also names editable image files, extending the old print sense to screens.
items.cn: 从 20 世纪后期起，这个词也指可编辑的图像文件，把旧的印刷义延伸到屏幕。

note.en: Group one separates artwork from art- words that look close but name very different things; group two separates it from words for pictures and designs in other trades.
note.cn: 第一组把 artwork 与看似接近、实则所指完全不同的 art- 词分开；第二组把它与其他行当中表示图画与设计的词分开。

entries.definition: The two-word spelling usually means 'work done in or for art', a task or labour, not a countable piece.
entries.definitionCN: 分写形式通常指「为艺术所做的工作」，是一种劳动或事务，而非可数作品。

entries.definition: An object made by human hands, especially one of archaeological interest; its value lies in evidence, not beauty.
entries.definitionCN: 人手制作的物件，尤指有考古意义的器物；其价值在于证据性，而非美。

entries.definition: A clever made device or a cunning trick; it shares the art- stem but carries deception, not display.
entries.definitionCN: 精巧的装置或狡黠的计谋；同出 art- 词干，却带欺骗而非展示之意。

entries.definition: Skilful in a calculating way; it describes a manner, while artwork names a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 以算计的方式机巧；描述一种方式，而 artwork 命名一个物件。

entries.definition: A picture made to explain or decorate a text; it is a functional category, while artwork can stand alone.
entries.definitionCN: 为解释或装饰文字而作的图画；是功能类别，而 artwork 可以独立存在。

entries.definition: A visual element in design or printing, often commercial; artwork is the broader term that may include fine pieces.
entries.definitionCN: 设计或印刷中的视觉元素，常指商业图形；artwork 更广，可包含纯艺术作品。

entries.definition: A casual word for one work in a gallery or studio; artwork is the explicit term used in catalogues and contracts.
entries.definitionCN: 画廊或工作室中对单件作品的随口说法；artwork 是图录与合同中的明确用语。

entries.definition: The arrangement or plan behind an object; artwork stresses the finished visual surface rather than the planning.
entries.definitionCN: 物件背后的安排或方案；artwork 强调完成的视觉表面，而非计划过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: art + work: a made thing in the category of art.
normal.cn: art + work：艺术类别中的一件制成品。

normal.en: The compound is recorded from 1847 and may follow German Kunstwerk, literally 'art-work'.
normal.cn: 这个复合词 1847 年有记录，可能仿照德语 Kunstwerk，字面就是「艺术-作品」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: original artwork, cover artwork, send artwork to the printer.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：原作、封面图稿、把图稿交给印刷厂。

normal.en: The family runs art, work, artwork, artworks and the trade verb artworking.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 art、work、artwork、artworks 以及行业动词 artworking。

normal.en: A printer asks for 'the artwork' when it needs the file, not the framed picture.
normal.cn: 印刷厂要「the artwork」时，要的是文件，不是装框的画。

abstract.en: Picture a surface that keeps the marks of every decision made on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块保留着每一次修改痕迹的表面。

abstract.en: Picture an object that leaves the studio and begins a life in other people's eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象一件物品离开工作室，开始在别人的目光里过日子。

abstract.en: Picture a file and a framed canvas answering to the same name.
abstract.cn: 想象一个文件与一幅装框画布回应着同一个名字。

examples.en: The auction catalogue lists every artwork with its provenance.
examples.cn: 拍卖图录列出每件作品及其来源。

examples.en: The magazine's artwork was finished two weeks before the issue closed.
examples.cn: 杂志的图稿在截稿前两周就完成了。

examples.en: She keeps the original artwork in a flat file, away from light.
examples.cn: 她把原作平放在抽屉柜里，避开光线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「art（艺术）+ work（作品）」——艺术做出来的活儿 → 艺术作品

root: art 来自拉丁 ars（属格 artis）「技艺」；work 来自古英语 weorc「所做之事、制成品」，上溯原始日耳曼语 *werka-。二者在 1847 年合为 artwork，可能仿德语 Kunstwerk。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the object from the gallery wall to the printed page, the packaging and the screen, and finally back to the original surface that copies cannot replace.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让这件物品从画廊墙面走到印刷页、包装与屏幕，最后回到复制品无法替代的原作表面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surface is revised again and again until it leaves the studio as a fixed shape and enters other people's eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块表面被反复修改，直到以固定形状离开工作室，进入别人的眼睛。

branches.en: THE OBJECT AND THE ORIGINAL: one countable piece, and the insistence that it is not a copy.
branches.cn: 物件与原作：一件可数作品，以及对「它不是复制品」的坚持。

branches.en: THE OEUVRE: the same word without a count gathers a whole life's making.
branches.cn: 作品群：去掉计数后，同一个词收拢一生的创作。

branches.en: THE PRINTED PAGE: illustration first, then the material handed to the press.
branches.cn: 印刷页：先是插图，再是交给印刷机的材料。

branches.en: THE FILE: the editable image inherits the print function on a screen.
branches.cn: 文件：可编辑图像在屏幕上继承了印刷功能。

branches.en: COMMERCIAL SURFACES: packaging and screen works put the image to work.
branches.cn: 商业表面：包装与屏幕作品让图像去干活。

intro.en: Artwork is a transparent English compound, so both halves can be read separately, and each half has its own family.
intro.cn: artwork 是一个透明的英语复合词，两半都能单独读，而且各自都有自己的词族。

latinIntro.en: Only the first half has a Latin ancestor, ars; the second half is native Germanic, and the compound itself is modern English.
latinIntro.cn: 只有前半有拉丁祖先 ars；后半是日耳曼本族词，复合词本身则是现代英语的产物。

items.example: Art supplies the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: art 提供这个复合词的前半。

items.example: Work supplies the second half.
items.exampleCN: work 提供后半。

items.example: The gallery hung the artwork badly.
items.exampleCN: 画廊把这件作品挂得很糟。

items.example: The crate held six artworks.
items.exampleCN: 箱子里装了六件作品。

items.example: The artworker fixed the spacing before printing.
items.exampleCN: 图稿制作员在印刷前调整了字距。

items.example: Artworking took longer than the design.
items.exampleCN: 图稿制作比设计本身更耗时。

items.example: The phrase is older than the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语比复合词更古老。

items.example: The dig catalogued every artefact.
items.exampleCN: 发掘记录了每一件器物。

items.example: The artisan signed the table.
items.exampleCN: 工匠在桌上签了名。

definition_zh: 艺术运动；艺术流派
definition_en: an organised trend in which a group of artists share aims and change how art is made
core_image: 一群艺术家在同一份宣言上签名，随后各自用不同材料表达同一种主张
scene: 十九世纪的画家们联合办展，发表宣言，反对学院派的规矩。 A group of painters held their own exhibition and published a manifesto, founding an artistic movement.
sceneCN: 这里指「一群艺术家共同主张所形成的运动」（第 1 个义项：有共同目标的艺术运动）；句意为这群画家自办展览并发表宣言，开创了一个艺术运动。可辨识物件：画布、宣言纸、签名、展厅。

pos.zh: 艺术运动；艺术流派
（某一时期的）艺术潮流

collocations.phrase: the artistic movements of the twentieth century

derivatives.zh: 艺术家（由基础词根加表示「从事者」的后缀构成，语义收窄为职业）
艺术的；有艺术性的（由表示艺术家的词加表示「与……有关的」后缀构成，语义偏移为性质描述）
艺术才能；艺术性（由表示艺术家的词加表示「技艺或集合」的后缀构成，语义偏移为能力）
艺术运动（由表示艺术的词与表示「运动」的词缩略复合，省去形容词形式，语义不变而更常用于史论）

senses.title: A trend with shared aims
senses.titleCN: 有共同目标的艺术运动
senses.definition: an organised trend in which many artists pursue the same aims at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 许多艺术家在同一时期追求相同目标而形成的组织化潮流
senses.example: A group of painters founded an artistic movement in the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 一群画家在首都发起了一场艺术运动。
senses.why: The phrase joins the adjective for art to the noun for motion. A movement is not one work but many works moving in one direction.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把表示艺术的形容词接到表示运动的名词上。运动不是一件作品，而是许多作品朝同一方向移动。

senses.title: A manifesto group
senses.titleCN: 以宣言集结的艺术家团体
senses.definition: a group of artists bound by a published statement of principles
senses.definitionCN: 由一份公开的原则声明联结起来的艺术家群体
senses.example: The artistic movement began with a single manifesto.
senses.exampleCN: 这场艺术运动始于一份宣言。
senses.why: Modern movements needed a public text to declare what they rejected. The manifesto turns separate artists into a named body.
senses.whyCN: 现代艺术运动需要一份公开文本，宣告自己拒绝什么。宣言把分散的艺术家变成一个有名号的团体。

senses.title: A period style named later
senses.titleCN: 后来被命名的时期风格
senses.definition: a style of a period that critics and historians name after the fact
senses.definitionCN: 由评论家与历史学家在事后命名的某一时期风格
senses.example: The artistic movement was named by a hostile critic.
senses.exampleCN: 这场艺术运动是由一位敌意评论家命名的。
senses.why: Many movements did not choose their names. Critics supplied a label, and the label later became a period category.
senses.whyCN: 许多运动的名字并非自己选定。评论家提供了标签，标签后来成为时期分类。

senses.title: An avant-garde challenge
senses.definition: a movement that deliberately breaks with accepted rules and institutions
senses.definitionCN: 有意与既定规则和机构决裂的运动
senses.example: The artistic movement rejected the academy's rules.
senses.exampleCN: 这场艺术运动拒绝了学院的规矩。
senses.why: Avant-garde movements define themselves by what they oppose, so conflict with institutions is part of the sense.
senses.whyCN: 前卫运动以自己反对的东西来定义自身，因此与机构的冲突是这个义项的一部分。

senses.title: A single-medium movement
senses.definition: a movement confined to one art, such as painting, sculpture or photography
senses.definitionCN: 局限于一种艺术门类内的运动，如绘画、雕塑或摄影
senses.example: Photography had its own artistic movement in the same decade.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影在同一个十年里也有自己的艺术运动。
senses.why: Each medium has its own technical problems, so movements often form inside one discipline before spreading.
senses.whyCN: 每种媒介都有自己的技术难题，因此运动常先在某一门类内部形成，再向外扩散。

senses.title: A movement across media
senses.definition: a movement that links painting, literature, music and design under one programme
senses.definitionCN: 在一套纲领下把绘画、文学、音乐与设计联结起来的运动
senses.example: The artistic movement reached poetry and music as well.
senses.exampleCN: 这场艺术运动也波及诗歌与音乐。
senses.why: When a movement has a shared theory rather than a shared technique, it can travel from canvas to page to stage.
senses.whyCN: 当一场运动共享的是理论而非技法，它就能从画布走到书页，再走到舞台。

senses.title: A national or regional movement
senses.definition: a movement tied to the identity or politics of a particular country or region
senses.definitionCN: 与某一国家或地区的身份认同或政治相绑定的运动
senses.example: The artistic movement became part of the independence struggle.
senses.exampleCN: 这场艺术运动成为独立斗争的一部分。
senses.why: Art can carry a nation's claim to its own language and history, so a movement may be organised around place as much as style.
senses.whyCN: 艺术可以承载一个民族对自身语言与历史的主张，因此运动也可能围绕地方而非风格来组织。

senses.title: A reaction against another movement
senses.titleCN: 针对另一场运动的反动
senses.definition: a movement formed chiefly in opposition to an earlier or rival movement
senses.definitionCN: 主要为反对更早或敌对运动而形成的新运动
senses.example: The next artistic movement answered the first one directly.
senses.exampleCN: 下一场艺术运动直接回应了前一场。
senses.why: Movements come in pairs: one sets a rule, the next breaks it. The phrase can therefore name a reaction as easily as an origin.
senses.whyCN: 运动常成对出现：一场立规矩，下一场破规矩。因此这个短语既能命名源头，也能命名反动。

intro.en: Artistic movement joins an adjective built from art with a noun built from a Latin verb meaning 'to move'. Both halves are old borrowings, while the phrase itself is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: artistic movement 把由 art 构成的形容词与一个来自拉丁动词「移动」的名词并在一起。两半都是古老借词，短语本身却是现代的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin ars 'skill, craft' gives art. Its deeper origin is source uncertain, and any older root proposed for it is a reconstructed form.
items.cn: 拉丁 ars「技艺、手艺」给出 art。其更深来源属「来源不确定」，为其提出的更早词根都是重构形式。

items.en: Artist came through French from Latin artista, itself from ars. English added -ic to make artistic in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: artist 经法语来自拉丁 artista，而 artista 又出自 ars。英语在十八世纪加上表示「与……有关的」后缀，构成 artistic。

items.en: Latin movere 'to move' produced motus 'a moving' and movimentum, the source of movement.
items.cn: 拉丁 movere「移动」产生 motus「运动」与 movimentum，后者是 movement 的来源。

items.en: Old French movement carried the noun into English, where it first meant physical motion and later a collective campaign.
items.cn: 古法语 movement 把这个名词带进英语，最初指物理运动，后来指集体行动。

items.en: Artistic movement became a standard term in the nineteenth century, when critics began grouping artists by shared programmes rather than by individual careers.
items.cn: artistic movement 在十九世纪成为标准术语；当时评论家开始按共同纲领、而非个人生涯给艺术家分组。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origins of ars and movere are both unresolved, so older forms offered for either are reconstructed forms rather than recorded words.
items.cn: 来源不确定：ars 与 movere 在拉丁语之前的来源都没有定论，因此为两者提出的更早形式都属于重构形式，而非有记录的真实词形。

note.en: Group one holds forms built from the same words with a different scope; group two holds historical terms for grouped art activity.
note.cn: 第一组是由同样几个词构成、范围不同的形式；第二组是表示群体艺术活动的史学术语。

entries.definition: the usual shorter term in art history; it drops the adjective but keeps the same meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 艺术史中常用的较短说法；省去形容词，意思不变。

entries.definition: relating to art or to artists; alone it describes a quality, not an organised group.
entries.definitionCN: 与艺术或艺术家有关的；单独使用时描述一种性质，而非组织化群体。

entries.definition: the skill of an artist; it names personal ability, while a movement is collective.
entries.definitionCN: 艺术家的技艺；它指个人能力，而运动是集体的。

entries.definition: physical motion, or any organised campaign; the full phrase narrows it to art.
entries.definitionCN: 物理运动，或任何组织化行动；完整短语把它收窄到艺术。

entries.definition: a group of artists sharing a style or teaching; it often implies a master and followers rather than a public programme.
entries.definitionCN: 共享风格或师承的艺术家群体；常暗示师徒关系，而非公开纲领。

entries.definition: the recurring visual features of works; a movement may have a style, but style alone does not imply organisation.
entries.definitionCN: 作品中反复出现的视觉特征；运动可以有一种风格，但风格本身不意味组织。

entries.definition: the advanced group that claims to lead; it stresses rejection of tradition more than the phrase artistic movement does.
entries.definitionCN: 自称走在前列的先进群体；比 artistic movement 更强调拒绝传统。

entries.definition: a general direction of change; it can be unplanned, while a movement implies shared intent.
entries.definitionCN: 变化的大方向；可以是无计划的，而运动暗示共同意图。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Artistic is artist plus -ic, so the phrase literally means the art-related movement.
normal.cn: artistic 是在 artist 之后加表示「与……有关的」后缀而成，因此这个短语字面上就是「与艺术有关的运动」。

normal.en: Movement goes back to a Latin verb for moving, which is why a trend can be pictured as many works walking one way.
normal.cn: movement 上溯到拉丁语表示「移动」的动词，所以一场潮流可以想象成许多作品朝同一方向行走。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark its stages: found, lead, join, and later study a movement.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出它的阶段：创立、领导、加入，后来是研究一场运动。

normal.en: Art movement is the shorter term used most often in textbooks.
normal.cn: art movement 是教科书中最常用的较短说法。

normal.en: Many movements were named by critics, which is why the label sometimes sounds hostile.
normal.cn: 许多运动由评论家命名，这也是标签有时带敌意的原因。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd walking in one direction without a leader visible at the front.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人朝同一方向走，最前面却看不见领队。

abstract.en: Picture a signature page where every name is written in a different hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一页签名，每个名字都出自不同的手。

abstract.en: Picture a rule being written down so that the next generation can break it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条规矩被写下来，好让下一代去打破它。

examples.en: Impressionism began as an artistic movement with its own exhibitions.
examples.cn: 印象派最初是一场自办展览的艺术运动。

examples.en: The artistic movement spread from painting into poetry and music.
examples.cn: 这场艺术运动从绘画蔓延到诗歌与音乐。

examples.en: Later critics treated the artistic movement as a single period style.
examples.cn: 后来的评论家把这场艺术运动当作一个统一的时期风格。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「艺术的运动」—— 一群艺术家朝同一个方向一起走 → 艺术运动、艺术流派

root: 由 artistic 与 movement 组合：artistic 源于拉丁 ars「技艺」经 artist 加表示「与……有关的」后缀；movement 经古法语上溯至拉丁 movere「移动」及其派生 movimentum。两者的更早来源均不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a collective drift: a shared aim, a manifesto, a later label, an avant-garde break, one medium, many media, a nation, and finally a reaction against the movement before it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一次集体转向展开：共同目标、宣言、事后标签、前卫决裂、单一媒介、跨媒介、国族，最后是对前一场运动的反动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many artists walking one way, each carrying a different tool.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多艺术家朝同一方向走，每人手里拿着不同的工具。

branches.en: ORIGIN: a shared aim becomes public when a group writes it down.
branches.cn: 起点：共同目标在群体把它写下来时成为公开纲领。

branches.en: AFTERLIFE: critics turn the group into a period style with a name.
branches.cn: 身后：评论家把这个群体变成一个有名号的时期风格。

branches.en: OPPOSITION: the movement defines itself by what it refuses.
branches.cn: 对抗：运动以自己拒绝的东西来定义自身。

branches.en: MEDIA: one discipline or several can carry the same programme.
branches.cn: 媒介：一门或数门艺术都能承载同一套纲领。

branches.en: PLACE AND REACTION: a national cause and a counter-movement show that art moves with politics and with its rivals.
branches.cn: 地方与反动：民族事业与反向运动说明艺术会随政治与对手一起移动。

intro.en: The phrase is built from art and motion, and both halves bring productive families into English.
intro.cn: 这个短语由「艺术」与「运动」构成，两半都为英语带来能产的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ars gives art, artist, artistic and artisan; Latin movere gives move, movement, motion and motive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ars 给出 art、artist、artistic 与 artisan；拉丁 movere 给出 move、movement、motion 与 motive。

items.example: Ars is the root of art.
items.exampleCN: ars 是 art 的词根。

items.example: Art changed meaning over centuries.
items.exampleCN: art 的含义在几个世纪中发生变化。

items.example: Artist means one who works in art.
items.exampleCN: artist 指从事艺术的人。

items.example: The artist joined the group.
items.exampleCN: 这位艺术家加入了那个群体。

items.example: Artistic means relating to art.
items.exampleCN: artistic 意为与艺术有关的。

items.example: The artistic aims were new.
items.exampleCN: 这些艺术目标很新。

items.structure: movere, movi, motum (Latin verb, second conjugation)
items.example: Movere gives movement and motion.
items.exampleCN: movere 给出 movement 与 motion。

items.structure: Old French movement, from Latin movimentum
items.example: The movement grew quickly.
items.exampleCN: 这场运动发展得很快。

items.example: The artistic movement had a manifesto.
items.exampleCN: 这场艺术运动有一份宣言。

items.example: Art movement is the textbook term.
items.exampleCN: art movement 是教科书的说法。

definition_zh: 衰老；老化；（细胞的）衰老状态；老年期
definition_en: the process or state of growing old, especially the biological decline of cells and organisms
core_image: 一片由绿转黄的银杏叶，叶脉清晰，叶柄旁放着一枚放大镜
scene: 公园的银杏林里，叶子由绿转黄，管理员蹲下捡起一片开始褪色的叶子夹进标本册。 Autumn senescence turns the whole grove gold before the leaves drop.
sceneCN: 这里指植物与叶片的衰老（第 4 个义项：叶片在脱落前发生的有序衰退）；句意为秋天的衰老过程让整片林子转黄，之后叶子才落下。图中可辨识物件：银杏叶、叶脉、标本册、放大镜。

pos.zh: 名词：不可数，指衰老的过程或状态；生物学中特指细胞停止分裂的状态

derivatives.zh: 由动词加表示「正在……的」词尾构成，义为「衰老的；老化的」
去掉名词词尾得到的动词，义为「变老；开始衰老」
同一词根经另一形容词路径形成的名词，义为「衰老；老态」
同一词根的形容词，义为「年老的；老年性的」
由表示「免疫」的成分加本词构成，义为「免疫衰老」
由本词加表示「溶解、清除」的成分构成，指清除衰老细胞的药物

senses.title: Cellular senescence
senses.definition: a stable state in which a cell stops dividing but remains alive and secretes signalling molecules
senses.definitionCN: 细胞停止分裂却仍然存活、并分泌信号分子的稳定状态
senses.example: Cellular senescence is marked by a permanent exit from the cell cycle.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞衰老的标志是永久退出细胞周期。
senses.why: The word names a controlled programme, not passive wear, which is why biology adopted it for cells that refuse to divide.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是一套受控程序而非被动磨损，因此生物学用它指拒绝分裂的细胞。

senses.title: Organismal ageing
senses.definition: the gradual loss of function that living things undergo as they grow older
senses.definitionCN: 生物随年龄增长而逐渐丧失功能的过程
senses.example: Senescence in the whole organism brings a steady loss of reserve capacity.
senses.exampleCN: 整个机体的衰老带来储备能力的逐步丧失。
senses.why: At the level of the body the word covers every system at once, from skin to kidney.
senses.whyCN: 在身体层面，这个词同时涵盖从皮肤到肾脏的每一个系统。

senses.title: Replicative senescence
senses.definition: the permanent arrest that cells enter after a fixed number of divisions, known as the Hayflick limit
senses.definitionCN: 细胞在完成固定次数分裂后进入的永久停滞，即海弗利克极限
senses.example: Replicative senescence was shown by growing fibroblasts until they stopped dividing.
senses.exampleCN: 复制性衰老是通过培养成纤维细胞直到其停止分裂而得到证明的。
senses.why: Counting divisions gave ageing a measurable clock, and the word became the name of that clock's end.
senses.whyCN: 计数分裂次数为衰老提供了可测量的钟表，这个词就成了那只钟走到尽头的名称。

senses.title: Plant and leaf senescence
senses.definition: the ordered breakdown of a leaf or whole plant before it sheds parts or dies back
senses.definitionCN: 叶片或整株植物在脱落或枯死之前发生的有序分解
senses.example: Autumn senescence turns the whole grove gold before the leaves drop.
senses.exampleCN: 秋天的衰老过程让整片林子转黄，随后叶子才落下。
senses.why: In plants the process is scheduled and nutrient-recycling, so the word carries no sense of failure.
senses.whyCN: 在植物身上这一过程是有计划的养分回收，因此这个词不含「衰败」的贬义。

senses.title: Demographic senescence
senses.definition: the rising share of elderly people within a population
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体中老年人所占比例不断上升
senses.example: Demographic senescence has reshaped the country's labour market.
senses.exampleCN: 人口老龄化重塑了该国的劳动力市场。
senses.why: Demography borrowed the biological noun to describe what happens when a whole population grows older.
senses.whyCN: 人口学借用这个生物学名词，描述整个人口变老时发生的事。

senses.title: Senescence in disease
senses.definition: the accumulation of senescent cells that drive inflammation and chronic disease
senses.definitionCN: 衰老细胞的堆积推动炎症与慢性疾病
senses.example: Senescence in the tissue is now treated as a target for new drugs.
senses.exampleCN: 组织中的衰老现象如今被视为新药的靶点。
senses.why: Once senescent cells were linked to illness, the word moved from description to a medical target.
senses.whyCN: 当衰老细胞与疾病建立联系后，这个词便从描述变成了医学靶点。

senses.title: Old age as a stage
senses.definition: the later part of life, described in formal or literary writing
senses.definitionCN: 人生的后期阶段，多用于正式或文学性表达
senses.example: The essay describes senescence as a season rather than a single hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章把老年期描述成一个季节，而不是一个时辰。
senses.why: Before biology claimed the word, it simply meant the state of being old, and that literary sense survives.
senses.whyCN: 在生物学占用这个词之前，它只表示年老的状态，这一文学义至今仍在。

senses.title: Institutional senescence
senses.definition: the loss of adaptability in an organisation that has stopped renewing itself
senses.definitionCN: 组织停止自我更新后失去适应能力
senses.example: Institutional senescence set in once the same committee approved everything.
senses.exampleCN: 自从同一个委员会审批所有事项，机构的老化就开始了。
senses.why: Organisations age in a recognisable way, so the biological noun is applied to them by analogy.
senses.whyCN: 组织会以可辨识的方式变老，因此人们用类比把这个生物学名词用到了它们身上。

senses.title: Immunosenescence
senses.definition: the age-related decline in the immune system's ability to respond to new threats
senses.definitionCN: 免疫系统随年龄增长而对新威胁反应减弱
senses.example: Immunosenescence explains why older patients respond less well to some vaccines.
senses.exampleCN: 免疫衰老解释了为何年长患者对某些疫苗反应较弱。
senses.why: A single branch of the immune system ages on its own schedule, and the compound names it precisely.
senses.whyCN: 免疫系统中有一个分支按自己的时间表衰老，这个复合词精确地命名了它。

intro.en: The word comes from Latin senescere, to begin to grow old, built on senex, an old man. The Latin source is clear; the exact year the English noun entered use is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语中表示「开始变老」的动词，其根是表示「老人」的名词。拉丁来源清楚，英语名词进入使用的确切年份为约数。

items.en: Senex meant an old man and stands behind senior and senate as well.
items.cn: 这个词指老年男子，也是「年长的」与「元老院」等词的根源。

items.en: The verb added an inceptive ending to mean to begin to grow old, stressing the start of the process.
items.cn: 这个动词加上表示「开始」的词尾，意为「开始变老」，强调过程的起点。

items.en: The abstract noun named the process itself rather than the person who undergoes it.
items.cn: 这个抽象名词命名的是过程本身，而非经历过程的人。

items.en: English adopted the noun in the seventeenth century for the state of being old.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个名词，用来表示年老的状态。

items.en: Twentieth-century biology narrowed the word to a programmed process with measurable steps.
items.cn: 二十世纪的生物学把词义收窄为有可测步骤的程序性过程。

items.en: When cells were found to stop dividing for good, the same noun was attached to that arrest.
items.cn: 当人们发现细胞会永久停止分裂，同一个名词便被用到了这种停滞上。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root senex; the second group names ageing and decline in plainer words.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「老人」的拉丁词根；第二组是用更朴素的词表示衰老与衰退。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning growing old or having stopped dividing.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「正在变老」或「已停止分裂」的形容词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to begin to grow old.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「开始变老」的动词。

entries.definition: The state of being old, often with weakened mental powers.
entries.definitionCN: 年老的状态，常含心智衰退之意。

entries.definition: Old and showing the effects of age.
entries.definitionCN: 年老的并显出衰老影响。

entries.definition: Older or higher in rank.
entries.definitionCN: 年长的或级别较高的。

entries.definition: The process of growing older.
entries.definitionCN: 变老的过程。

entries.definition: A gradual loss of strength or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 力量或质量的逐渐下降。

entries.definition: The process of becoming worse.
entries.definitionCN: 变得更差的过程。

entries.definition: The later part of a person's life.
entries.definitionCN: 人生的后期。

entries.definition: Shrinking and drying up, as a plant does.
entries.definitionCN: 像植物那样萎缩干枯。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the leaf, the cell and the population; abstract ones treat senescence as a scheduled programme rather than a breakdown.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着叶片、细胞与人群展开；抽象联想把衰老看作被安排好的程序而非崩坏。

normal.en: A leaf yellows on schedule, and that schedule is senescence.
normal.cn: 叶子按时变黄，这个时间表就是衰老。

normal.en: A cell that stops dividing but stays alive is senescent.
normal.cn: 停止分裂却仍活着的细胞就是衰老细胞。

normal.en: The Hayflick limit is the cell's built-in countdown.
normal.cn: 海弗利克极限就是细胞自带的倒计时。

normal.en: An ageing population is senescence written at the scale of a country.
normal.cn: 人口老龄化就是把衰老写到一个国家的尺度上。

normal.en: The immune system ages too, and the compound is immunosenescence.
normal.cn: 免疫系统也会衰老，这个复合词就是免疫衰老。

abstract.en: Senescence is not damage; it is a programme that damage can accelerate.
abstract.cn: 衰老不是损伤本身，而是一套可被损伤加速的程序。

abstract.en: Every system that renews itself must also decide when to stop.
abstract.cn: 每个能自我更新的系统都必须决定何时停止。

abstract.en: Ageing is the price of having a schedule at all.
abstract.cn: 变老，是拥有时间表所付出的代价。

examples.en: Senescence is now studied as an active programme rather than simple wear.
examples.cn: 衰老如今被当作主动程序而非单纯磨损来研究。

examples.en: The forest showed clear signs of senescence after the dry decade.
examples.cn: 干旱十年之后，这片森林显出明显的衰老迹象。

examples.en: Researchers now treat senescence as a target rather than an inevitable fate.
examples.cn: 研究人员如今把衰老当作可干预的目标，而非不可改变的归宿。

dict_mnemonic.text: sen（老）+ escence（开始成为）——开始变老：衰老

root: 来自拉丁语 senescere「开始变老」，其根为 senex「老人」，与 senior、senate 同源。拉丁来源清楚，英语名词约在十七世纪进入使用，确切年份不确定；二十世纪后词义收窄为生物学的程序性衰老。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses carry one root meaning of growing old across cells, bodies, leaves, populations, institutions and the immune system.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项把「变老」这一词根含义贯穿细胞、身体、叶片、人群、机构与免疫系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a yellowing leaf with a visible vein map and a lens beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片正在变黄的叶子，叶脉清晰，旁边放着放大镜。

branches.en: THE CELLULAR CORE: a permanent exit from division, reached after a counted number of cycles.
branches.cn: 细胞内核：永久退出分裂，且发生在计数过的若干循环之后。

branches.en: THE WHOLE BODY: every organ losing reserve at once.
branches.cn: 整个身体：每个器官同时失去储备。

branches.en: THE PLANT VERSION: an ordered breakdown that recycles nutrients before shedding.
branches.cn: 植物版本：脱落前发生的有序分解并回收养分。

branches.en: THE HUMAN ARC: a population growing older and a single life reaching its late stage.
branches.cn: 人类弧线：人口整体变老，以及单条生命进入晚期。

branches.en: THE TARGETS: senescent cells in disease, institutions losing adaptability, and an ageing immune system.
branches.cn: 靶点层面：疾病中的衰老细胞、失去适应力的机构，以及衰老的免疫系统。

intro.en: One Latin root, senex, yields a verb of growing old, an abstract noun and a family of adjectives.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁词根「老人」衍生出表示变老的动词、抽象名词以及一组形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the noun of age, the inceptive verb and the adjective of old age; English adds the abstract ending and later compounds.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示年老的名称、表示开始变老的动词与老年形容词；英语加上抽象名词词尾，后来又构成复合词。

items.example: The root also stands behind words for elders and councils of elders.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也藏在表示长者与长者议事会的词背后。

items.example: The inceptive ending stresses the start of ageing.
items.exampleCN: 表示「开始」的词尾强调衰老的起点。

items.example: The abstract noun passed into English as senescence.
items.exampleCN: 这个抽象名词以「衰老」的形式进入英语。

items.example: It supplies the English adjectives for senile conditions.
items.exampleCN: 它提供了英语中表示老年性状态的形容词。

items.example: It marks a process that has started but not finished.
items.exampleCN: 它标记已经开始但尚未完成的过程。

items.example: It turns the participle into the name of a state.
items.exampleCN: 它把分词变成状态名称。

items.example: The adjective keeps the inceptive sense of starting to age.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词保留了「开始变老」的起始含义。

items.example: The verb is a back formation from the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是从名词逆构出来的。

items.example: A modern compound joins immunity to the old noun.
items.exampleCN: 一个现代复合词把免疫与这个古老名词连在一起。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加表示「正在……的」词尾构成，义为「衰老的；老化的」
去掉名词词尾得到的动词，义为「变老；开始衰老」
同一词根经另一形容词路径形成的名词，义为「衰老；老态」
同一词根的形容词，义为「年老的；老年性的」
由表示「免疫」的成分加本词构成，义为「免疫衰老」
由本词加表示「溶解、清除」的成分构成，指清除衰老细胞的药物

definition_zh: 延长；拖延；使迁延
definition_en: to make something last longer than it should, often with no gain
core_image: 一根线被慢慢往外抽，越抽越长，却始终不肯断
scene: 双方都不肯先让步，谈判一拖就是三年。 Neither side would move first, and the talks were protracted for three years.
sceneCN: 这里 protract 指把谈判拖长（第 4 个义项：拖延争端）；句意为双方都不肯先让步，谈判就被拖了三年。

pos.zh: 延长；拖延；使迁延

senses.title: Prolong length
senses.definition: to make a period longer than it would naturally be
senses.definitionCN: 把一段时间拉得比它本来更长
senses.example: One objection protracted the hearing by an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 一条反对意见把听证会拖长了一小时。
senses.why: The word measures duration, not difficulty.
senses.whyCN: 这个词衡量时长，不衡量难度。

senses.title: Drag out a meeting
senses.definition: to keep a meeting going after its purpose has been served
senses.definitionCN: 会议目的已达到之后仍让它继续
senses.example: The chair protracted the meeting with stories of his own.
senses.exampleCN: 主席用自己的往事把会议拖长。
senses.why: Here the extension has an author and usually a motive.
senses.whyCN: 这里的延长有个施加者，而且通常有动机。

senses.title: Protract an illness
senses.definition: to make a recovery slower by delay or by treatment
senses.definitionCN: 因拖延或处置不当而让康复更慢
senses.example: The infection was protracted by the wrong antibiotic.
senses.exampleCN: 用错了抗生素，感染拖得更久。
senses.why: In medicine the word often carries regret.
senses.whyCN: 在医学里这个词常带着懊悔。

senses.title: Protract a dispute
senses.definition: to keep a conflict open without resolving it
senses.definitionCN: 让冲突一直开着，不予解决
senses.example: Neither side would move first, and the talks were protracted for three years.
senses.exampleCN: 双方都不肯先让步，谈判一拖就是三年。
senses.why: Delay becomes a strategy when both sides prefer the fight.
senses.whyCN: 当双方都更喜欢打，拖延就成了一种策略。

senses.title: Protract pain
senses.definition: to make suffering last beyond its necessary time
senses.definitionCN: 让苦延长到超出必要的时间
senses.example: The appeals protracted the family's grief by a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 一轮轮上诉让这家人的悲伤延长了十年。
senses.why: The word can judge the extension as a cruelty.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以把这种延长判定为残忍。

senses.title: Protracted war
senses.definition: a conflict deliberately kept long by one side or by terrain
senses.definitionCN: 由一方或地形刻意维持很久的战争
senses.example: The marsh turned the campaign into a protracted war.
senses.exampleCN: 沼泽把这场战事变成了持久战。
senses.why: Some things are prolonged on purpose, and the word does not judge.
senses.whyCN: 有些事是被故意拉长的，而这个词并不作评判。

senses.title: Protract a departure
senses.definition: to keep putting off the moment of leaving
senses.definitionCN: 一再推迟离开的那一刻
senses.example: He protracted his departure with one more cup of tea.
senses.exampleCN: 他又添了一杯茶，把离开的时间往后拖。
senses.why: Small delays can be a way of saying something without words.
senses.whyCN: 小小的拖延，可以是一种不用说话的表述。

senses.title: Protract in law
senses.definition: to keep a case alive by procedure rather than by argument
senses.definitionCN: 靠程序而非靠论证把案子拖住
senses.example: The defence protracted the case until the witness died.
senses.exampleCN: 辩方把案子拖到证人去世。
senses.why: Law has a name for delay, and this is it.
senses.whyCN: 法律对拖延有一个称呼，就是这个。

intro.en: Protract is 'to draw forward': the picture is a line pulled out of a pocket, a little longer each time.
intro.cn: protract 就是「向前拉」：画面是一根线从口袋里被拉出来，每次长一点。

items.en: Trahere meant 'to draw or pull', the verb behind tractor, trace and contract.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、拖」，是 tractor、trace 与 contract 背后的动词。

items.en: Protrahere meant 'to draw forward or draw out', a plain physical compound.
items.cn: protrahere 意为「向前拉、拉出」，是一个朴素的物理复合词。

items.en: English borrowed protract for stretching time and for drawing lines.
items.cn: 英语借入 protract，既指拉长时间，也指画延长线。

items.en: The instrument protracts a line on paper, and gave geometry a small namesake.
items.cn: 量角器在纸上延长一条线，给几何学留下一个小同名物。

items.en: Today the verb is mostly about time, and its participle is usually an accusation.
items.cn: 今天这个动词多半关乎时间，它的分词通常是一项指责。

note.en: The look-alike group is the trahere family; the near-meaning group separates prolong, extend, drag out and draw out.
note.cn: 形近组是 trahere 词族；近义组把「延长」「延展」「拖长」与「拉长」分开。

entries.definition: drawn out over a long time.
entries.definitionCN: 被拉得很长的。

entries.definition: the act of drawing out.
entries.definitionCN: 拉长的行为。

entries.definition: an instrument for drawing angles.
entries.definitionCN: 画角用的器具。

entries.definition: draws out, third person.
entries.definitionCN: 第三人称的拉长。

entries.definition: to make longer.
entries.definitionCN: 使更长。

entries.definition: to stretch out in space or time.
entries.definitionCN: 在空间或时间上伸展。

entries.definition: to make last too long.
entries.definitionCN: 使持续过久。

entries.definition: to make something last longer than needed.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物持续超过所需。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a thread pulled slowly out of a pocket.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一根线从口袋里被慢慢拉出」的画面。

normal.en: Protract holds trahere, to pull: the word is a line being drawn out.
normal.cn: protract 里藏着 trahere（拉）：这个词就是一条被拉出来的线。

normal.en: Think of a meeting that could have ended an hour ago.
normal.cn: 想象一场本可一小时前就结束的会议。

normal.en: Pro-TRACT: the stress sits on tract, where the pulling happens.
normal.cn: pro-TRACT：重音落在 tract，正是拉扯发生处。

normal.en: Say pruh-TRAKT; the second syllable sounds like a long hallway.
normal.cn: 读成 pruh-TRAKT，第二音节听起来像一条长走廊。

normal.en: Pair it with protracted: the participle is usually the complaint.
normal.cn: 把它和 protracted 配对：分词形式通常是那句抱怨。

abstract.en: To protract is to buy time with someone else's patience.
abstract.cn: 拖延就是用别人的耐心买时间。

abstract.en: The word does not say why a thing lasts; it only says it lasts longer than it should.
abstract.cn: 这个词不说一件事为何持续，只说它持续得比该有的更久。

abstract.en: Every institution has a procedure for protracting a decision it does not want to make.
abstract.cn: 每个机构都有一套程序，用来拖住一个它不想做的决定。

examples.en: The talks were protracted for three years.
examples.cn: 谈判被拖了三年。

examples.en: One objection protracted the hearing by an hour.
examples.cn: 一条反对意见把听证会拖长了一小时。

examples.en: The defence protracted the case until the witness died.
examples.cn: 辩方把案子拖到证人去世。

dict_mnemonic.text: pro（向前）+ tract（拉）：把时间往前拉，就是「延长、拖延」。

root: 拉丁语 protrahere（向前拉出），由 pro-（向前）与 trahere（拉）构成

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses are one line pulled longer: a period, a meeting, an illness, a dispute, a grief, a war, a farewell and a lawsuit.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是同一条被拉长的线：一段时间、一场会议、一次病、一桩争端、一份悲伤、一场战争、一次告别与一宗诉讼。

core.en: A THREAD PULLED OUT OF A POCKET
core.cn: 从口袋里被拉出的线

branches.en: A period and a meeting.
branches.cn: 一段时间与一场会议。

branches.en: An illness made slower.
branches.cn: 被拖慢的病。

branches.en: A dispute and a war.
branches.cn: 争端与战争。

branches.en: A grief and a farewell.
branches.cn: 悲伤与告别。

branches.en: A case kept alive by procedure.
branches.cn: 靠程序拖着不结的案子。

intro.en: The trahere family is about pulling: contract pulls together, extract pulls out, distract pulls aside, protract pulls forward in time.
intro.cn: trahere 词族关乎拉扯：contract 拉到一起，extract 拉出来，distract 拉向旁边，protract 把时间往前拉。

latinIntro.en: Latin trahere supplies the pull, and the prefixes con-, ex-, dis- and pro- decide which way the line goes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trahere 提供那一下拉，前缀 con-、ex-、dis- 与 pro- 决定线往哪边走。

items.example: Protract the talks.
items.exampleCN: 拖长谈判。

items.example: A protracted war.
items.exampleCN: 一场持久战。

items.example: Slow protraction.
items.exampleCN: 缓慢的延长。

items.example: A plastic protractor.
items.exampleCN: 一把塑料量角器。

items.example: Muscles contract.
items.exampleCN: 肌肉收缩。

items.example: Extract a tooth.
items.exampleCN: 拔出一颗牙。

items.example: Do not distract him.
items.exampleCN: 别分散他的注意。

items.example: A faint trace.
items.exampleCN: 一道淡淡的痕迹。

definition_zh: 巨石的；用巨石建造的；巨石文化时代的；规模巨大而粗犷的
definition_en: relating to megaliths; built of large stones; belonging to a megalith-using culture; massive in style
core_image: 游客走进由巨石围成的圆形遗迹，头顶的盖石像一块压下来的天花板
scene: 游客走进由巨石围成的圆形遗迹。 The megalithic tomb was built from slabs weighing several tons.
sceneCN: 这里 megalithic 指「用巨石建造的」（第 2 个义项：以巨石为建材）；句意为这座巨石墓由数吨重的石板建成。

pos.zh: 巨石的；巨石建筑的；巨石文化时代的；粗犷巨大的

derivatives.zh: megalithic 去掉 -ic → 巨石；史前大石块
megalith + -ism（体系后缀）→ 巨石建筑传统
megalith + -ist（研究者后缀）→ 巨石文化研究者
megalithic + -ally（副词后缀）→ 以巨石方式（罕用）
否定前缀 + megalithic → 非巨石的

senses.title: Relating to megaliths
senses.definition: connected with the large rough stones used in prehistoric monuments
senses.definitionCN: 与史前纪念建筑中使用的大块粗石有关的
senses.example: The museum labels each megalithic block by its quarry source.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆按采石来源给每块巨石标注。
senses.why: the adjective simply adds -ic to megalith, so its first job is to point back at the stones.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是给 megalith 加 -ic，因此首要职能是回指那些石头。

senses.title: Built of large stones
senses.definition: constructed from massive stone slabs or blocks rather than small masonry
senses.definitionCN: 由巨大石板或石块而非小砖石建成的
senses.example: The megalithic tomb was built from slabs weighing several tons.
senses.exampleCN: 这座巨石墓由数吨重的石板建成。
senses.why: construction is the purpose of most megaliths, so the adjective naturally describes the building method.
senses.whyCN: 建造是多数巨石的用途，因此形容词自然描述营造方式。

senses.title: Of a megalith-using culture
senses.titleCN: 属于使用巨石的文化的
senses.definition: belonging to a society that raised large stone monuments as part of its ritual life
senses.definitionCN: 属于把大型石构纪念物纳入仪式生活的社会
senses.example: Megalithic communities along the coast shared burial customs.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海的巨石文化社群共享墓葬习俗。
senses.why: the stones survive while the people do not, so the adjective comes to name the culture through its monuments.
senses.whyCN: 石头留存而人已消失，因此形容词通过遗迹来命名那个文化。

senses.title: Of the Neolithic or Bronze Age
senses.definition: dated to the long period when such monuments were built, roughly the Neolithic and early Bronze Age
senses.definitionCN: 属于建造这类遗迹的漫长时期，约当新石器时代与青铜时代早期
senses.example: The megalithic layers at the site date to the late Neolithic.
senses.exampleCN: 该遗址的巨石文化层可定到新石器时代晚期。
senses.why: dating links the adjective to a period, so megalithic also works as a chronological label.
senses.whyCN: 断代把这个形容词与一个时期连起来，因此 megalithic 也作年代标签。

senses.title: Massive and rough in style
senses.definition: used for art or architecture that is deliberately blocky, heavy and rough
senses.definitionCN: 用于刻意块状、厚重、粗犷的艺术或建筑
senses.example: The sculptor's megalithic forms look quarried rather than carved.
senses.exampleCN: 这位雕塑家的巨石式造型看起来像采出来的，而非雕出来的。
senses.why: blocky, quarried-looking forms borrow the stone's heaviness for art.
senses.whyCN: 块状、像采石成果的造型，为艺术借用了石头的沉重感。

senses.title: Enormous in scale
senses.definition: figuratively very large, heavy or slow-moving
senses.definitionCN: 比喻极大、沉重或行动缓慢
senses.example: The reform was a megalithic project that took a generation.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革是一个耗掉一代人的巨大工程。
senses.why: a project on the scale of a monument takes the size sense figuratively.
senses.whyCN: 大到像纪念建筑一样的工程，以比喻方式承接了「尺寸」义。

senses.title: Cyclopean in construction
senses.definition: built of huge irregular blocks fitted without mortar, a style once attributed to giants
senses.definitionCN: 用巨大不规则石块不用灰浆砌成，这种风格曾被归为巨人所建
senses.example: The wall's megalithic masonry needs no mortar to stand.
senses.exampleCN: 这堵墙的巨石砌法不用灰浆也能立住。
senses.why: huge fitted blocks without mortar describe a distinct masonry technique.
senses.whyCN: 不用灰浆拼合的巨大石块，描述了一种独特的砌筑技术。

senses.title: Relating to megalithic monuments as a class
senses.titleCN: 与作为一类的巨石遗迹有关的
senses.definition: belonging to the archaeological category of megalithic monuments
senses.definitionCN: 属于巨石纪念建筑这一考古类别
senses.example: Every megalithic site in the region is protected by law.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的每一处巨石遗迹都受法律保护。
senses.why: heritage law turns the adjective into a category of protected monument.
senses.whyCN: 遗产法把这个形容词变成一类受保护的纪念物。

intro.en: Megalithic is megalith plus the adjective suffix -ic. It describes the stones, the buildings made from them, the cultures that raised them and, by extension, anything huge and blocky.
intro.cn: megalithic 是 megalith 加形容词后缀 -ic，描述巨石、用巨石建成的建筑、建造它们的文化，并引申描述任何巨大而块状的东西。

items.en: Megas supplied 'great' in the parent noun megalith.
items.cn: megas 在母词 megalith 中提供「巨大」。

items.en: Lithos supplied 'stone', the material the monuments are made from.
items.cn: lithos 提供「石头」，即遗迹的材料。

items.en: The nineteenth-century compound megalith named one large block.
items.cn: 十九世纪复合词 megalith 命名一块大石。

items.en: The suffix -ic turned the noun into a describing word for monuments and cultures.
items.cn: 后缀 -ic 把这个名词变成描述遗迹与文化的形容词。

items.en: The adjective now labels a whole period, a building style and a class of protected sites.
items.cn: 这个形容词如今标出一个时期、一种建筑风格与一类受保护遗址。

note.en: Group one holds adjectives and nouns of stone building easily confused with megalithic; group two holds words for great size.
note.cn: 第一组是容易与 megalithic 混淆的石构形容词与名词；第二组是表示巨大尺度的词。

entries.definition: A single large stone; megalithic is the adjective describing it or a structure made from it.
entries.definitionCN: 单块大石；megalithic 是描述它或由其建成结构的形容词。

entries.definition: Made from a single block, or figuratively rigid and uniform; it stresses unity, not prehistoric date.
entries.definitionCN: 由一整块石制成，或比喻僵化统一；强调整体性，而非史前年代。

entries.definition: Of the later Stone Age; many megalithic monuments are Neolithic, but the words answer different questions.
entries.definitionCN: 属于新石器时代；许多巨石遗迹是新石器的，但两词回答的问题不同。

entries.definition: Of the earlier Stone Age, before farming and before most megaliths.
entries.definitionCN: 属于旧石器时代，在农业与多数巨石之前。

entries.definition: Very large or serving as a memorial; megalithic specifically names stone-built prehistoric work.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大或起纪念作用；megalithic 特指史前石构作品。

entries.definition: Extremely large in size; it lacks the archaeological and stone-building reference.
entries.definitionCN: 尺寸极大；不含考古与石构指向。

entries.definition: Built of huge irregular blocks, a synonym for one kind of megalithic wall.
entries.definitionCN: 用巨大不规则石块建成，是某类巨石墙的同义说法。

entries.definition: Belonging to an early stage; it is a value judgement, while megalithic is a technical description.
entries.definitionCN: 属于早期阶段；含价值判断，而 megalithic 是技术描述。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Greek roots, the archaeological period and the real building style.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个希腊词根、考古时期与真实建筑风格。

normal.en: megalith plus -ic: the adjective of the great stone.
normal.cn: megalith 加 -ic：大石的形容词。

normal.en: Megalithic tombs, circles and walls are the three common monument types.
normal.cn: 巨石墓、石圈与石墙是三类常见遗迹。

normal.en: Megalithic masonry fits huge blocks without mortar.
normal.cn: 巨石砌法不用灰浆就能拼合大石块。

normal.en: The adjective can describe a culture, not only a building.
normal.cn: 这个形容词不只描述建筑，也能描述文化。

normal.en: Cyclopean is the old name for one style of megalithic wall.
normal.cn: cyclopean 是某类巨石墙的旧称。

abstract.en: Megalithic is the adjective of a world built by lifting, not carving.
abstract.cn: megalithic 是一个靠抬举而非雕刻建成的世界的形容词。

abstract.en: It is size turned into a style.
abstract.cn: 它是把尺寸变成风格。

abstract.en: A megalithic wall is a promise that the ground will not move.
abstract.cn: 巨石墙是一句「地面不会移动」的承诺。

examples.en: The megalithic circle is older than the nearby Roman road.
examples.cn: 这座巨石圈比附近的罗马大道更古老。

examples.en: Megalithic builders moved the slabs on rollers and levers.
examples.cn: 巨石建造者用滚木与杠杆搬运石板。

examples.en: The site is important for the study of megalithic culture.
examples.cn: 该遗址对研究巨石文化很重要。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mega（大）+ lith（石）+ ic」——像巨石一样 → 巨石的、巨大的

root: megalith（希腊 megas「巨大」+ lithos「石头」）加形容词后缀 -ic → megalithic；描述巨石、石构建筑、巨石文化，并引申为「巨大而粗犷」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses grow from the stone itself to the building method, the culture, the period, the style, the scale, the masonry and the protected site class.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从石头本身长到建造方式、文化、时期、风格、尺度、砌法与受保护遗址类别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: enormous rough slabs fitted together into a doorway that has stood for thousands of years.
core.cn: 核心意象：巨大的粗石板拼成一道已立数千年的门。

branches.en: STONE AND SITE CLASS: one block and a protected category are the same material seen as unit and as heritage.
branches.cn: 石块与遗址类别：单块石与受保护类别是同一材料在单位与遗产两面。

branches.en: BUILDING METHODS: slab-built tombs and mortarless walls are two ways of fitting great stones.
branches.cn: 建造方式：石板墓与无浆石墙是拼合巨石的两种做法。

branches.en: CULTURE AND PERIOD: the people and their age are named through the monuments they left.
branches.cn: 文化与时期：人与时代都通过他们留下的遗迹被命名。

branches.en: BLOCKY STYLE: art borrows the heaviness of stone for its own forms.
branches.cn: 块状风格：艺术为自己的造型借用石头的沉重感。

branches.en: GREAT SCALE: a huge project borrows the adjective's sense of size.
branches.cn: 巨大尺度：庞大工程借用了这个形容词的尺寸义。

intro.en: Megalithic is a Greek-rooted scientific adjective, and its endings also build abstract and adverbial forms.
intro.cn: megalithic 是希腊词根的科学形容词，其词尾还构成抽象与副词形式。

latinIntro.en: The Greek suffix -ikos became Latin -icus and English -ic; the compound itself is modern, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊后缀 -ikos 变成拉丁 -icus 与英语 -ic；复合词本身是近代产物，并非拉丁语。

items.example: The first root names size.
items.exampleCN: 第一个词根命名大小。

items.example: The second root names material.
items.exampleCN: 第二个词根命名材料。

items.example: The noun names one block.
items.exampleCN: 名词指一块大石。

items.example: The suffix makes the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成形容词。

items.example: The tomb is megalithic.
items.exampleCN: 这座墓是巨石建的。

items.example: Megalithism is studied across regions.
items.exampleCN: 巨石传统被跨地区研究。

items.example: The megalithist surveyed the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 这位巨石研究者勘察了山脊。

items.example: A monolithic column is cut from one block.
items.exampleCN: 整石柱由一块石凿成。

derivatives.zh: megalith + -ism（体系后缀）→ 巨石建筑传统
megalith + -ist（研究者后缀）→ 巨石文化研究者
megalithic + -ally（副词后缀）→ 以巨石方式（罕用）
否定前缀 + megalithic → 非巨石的

definition_zh: 连接性；连通性；网络连接
definition_en: the state or quality of being connected, especially the ability of devices, networks, or places to link and communicate
core_image: 一张网上的绳结彼此相系：哪一处断了，整张网都感觉得到
scene: 这里指「连接性」。 The technician ran a test that showed full connectivity across every node in the server room.
sceneCN: 这里 connectivity 是「连接状态」（第 1 个义项：处于连通的状态）；句意：技术员跑了一次测试，显示服务器机房里每个节点都处于完全连通状态。图中可辨识物件：服务器机柜、网线、交换机、测试笔记本。

pos.zh: 连接性；连通性；网络连接

senses.title: The state of being connected
senses.definition: the state or quality of being joined or linked to something else
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物相接或相连的状态或性质
senses.example: Engineers checked the connectivity of every cable before powering the rack.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在给机柜通电前检查了每根线缆的连接状态。
senses.why: connectere is con- 'together' plus nectere 'to bind, tie'. The suffix stack -ive + -ity turns the verb into the state of being bound, so connectivity is literally 'the condition of being tied together' before it names any technology.
senses.whyCN: connectere 是 con-“共同”加 nectere“系、绑”。后缀组合 -ive + -ity 把动词变成“被绑住的状态”，因此 connectivity 字面上就是“被系在一起的状况”，然后才指某项技术。

senses.title: Internet connectivity
senses.titleCN: 互联网连通性：能连上公网
senses.definition: the ability of a device or place to reach the internet
senses.definitionCN: 设备或地点接入互联网的能力
senses.example: Rural schools still struggle with reliable internet connectivity.
senses.exampleCN: 乡村学校仍在为稳定接入互联网而发愁。
senses.why: The 20c network sense extends the binding image to packet routes: a device is 'connected' when its packets can reach the wider network. -ity names that reachability as a property, not a single cable.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的网络义把“系在一起”的意象扩展到数据包路由：当设备的数据包能抵达更广的网络时，它就算“连着”。-ity 把这种可达性命名成一种性质，而不是某一根线。

senses.title: Network links between devices
senses.titleCN: 网络连接：节点之间的链路
senses.definition: the set or quality of links that allow devices and nodes to exchange data
senses.definitionCN: 使设备与节点能够交换数据的链路集合或质量
senses.example: The outage cut network connectivity for three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这次故障切断了网络连接三个小时。
senses.why: Here the word names a property of a whole network rather than of one device. nectere supplies the links, and -ity generalizes them into a measurable condition of the network as a system.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词指的是整个网络的属性，而不是某台设备的属性。nectere 提供一条条链路，-ity 把它们概括成网络作为一个系统的可测状态。

senses.title: Connectivity problems
senses.titleCN: 连接故障：连不上的状况
senses.definition: difficulties in establishing or keeping a connection, often called connectivity issues
senses.definitionCN: 建立或保持连接时遇到的困难，常称 connectivity issues
senses.example: The report lists connectivity as the main complaint from remote staff.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把连接问题列为远程员工的主要抱怨。
senses.why: The absence of a property is named by the property itself: people report 'connectivity' when they mean the lack of it. This is a common pattern with abstract nouns, and the binding image makes the missing link easy to picture.
senses.whyCN: 一种性质的缺失用性质本身来命名：人们说“connectivity 有问题”，其实指的是没有连接。这是抽象名词的常见用法，而“系在一起”的意象让缺失的那一环很容易被看见。

senses.title: Connectivity between regions
senses.titleCN: 地区间连通性：路把人接起来
senses.definition: the degree to which places are linked by transport, trade, or communication routes
senses.definitionCN: 各地通过交通、贸易或通信路线相互连接的程度
senses.example: The new rail line raises connectivity across the province.
senses.exampleCN: 这条新铁路提高了全省各地的连通性。
senses.why: The physical sense scales up: nectere can bind towns as easily as wires. Geography uses connectivity for the density of routes between places, so the same knot becomes a map of roads and rails.
senses.whyCN: 物理义可以放大：nectere 能把城镇系起来，就像把电线接起来一样。地理学用 connectivity 指各地之间路线的密度，于是同一个绳结变成了一张道路与铁轨的地图。

senses.title: Device-to-device interconnection
senses.titleCN: 设备互联：机器彼此搭话
senses.definition: the ability of devices or components to link directly and keep exchanging signals
senses.definitionCN: 设备或部件直接相连并持续交换信号的能力
senses.example: The protocol lets sensors maintain connectivity even after one node fails.
senses.exampleCN: 该协议让传感器在某个节点失效后仍能保持互联。
senses.why: In a mesh, each device is bound to several others, so -ity describes the mesh rather than a single pair. The resilience in the example comes from the net image: many knots mean one broken knot does not break the whole.
senses.whyCN: 在网状结构中，每台设备都与另外几台相系，因此 -ity 描述的是整张网，而不是单独一对。例句里的韧性正来自这张网的意象：结多了，断一个不等于全断。

senses.title: Social connectedness
senses.titleCN: 社会连接度：人与人之间的关系
senses.definition: the degree to which people are linked to one another through relationships and community
senses.definitionCN: 人们通过关系与社群相互联系的程度
senses.example: The survey links social connectivity to lower rates of loneliness.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查把社会连接度与较低的孤独率联系起来。
senses.why: The 21c extends the net metaphor from wires to people: relationships are the links, and -ity measures how densely a community is tied. No physical cable is needed; the binding is social.
senses.whyCN: 21 世纪把网的比喻从电线扩展到人：关系就是链路，-ity 衡量一个社群被系得有多密。这里不需要物理线缆，绑定是社会性的。

senses.title: Connectivity technology
senses.titleCN: 连接技术：提供联网能力的技术
senses.definition: the hardware or software features that provide links, as in connectivity technology or connectivity features
senses.definitionCN: 提供连接功能的硬件或软件特性，如 connectivity technology 或 connectivity features
senses.example: The chip integrates connectivity, storage and security on one die.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚芯片把连接、存储和安全功能集成在一个裸片上。
senses.why: Here the noun works attributively, modifying technology or features. The abstract state has become a product capability: what the technology supplies is the ability to be bound to other devices.
senses.whyCN: 这里名词作定语，修饰 technology 或 features。抽象状态变成了产品能力：这项技术提供的，正是“能被接到其他设备上”的能力。

senses.title: A connectivity provider
senses.titleCN: 连接服务商：把连通性当服务卖
senses.definition: a company that sells access to a network, especially satellite or broadband connectivity
senses.definitionCN: 出售网络接入服务的公司，尤指卫星或宽带连接服务商
senses.example: The airline signed a deal with a satellite connectivity provider.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司与一家卫星连接服务商签了协议。
senses.why: The commercial 21c sense turns the abstract property into a service. A provider does not sell a cable; it sells the ongoing state of being connected, which is exactly what the -ity noun names.
senses.whyCN: 21 世纪的商业义把抽象性质变成服务。服务商卖的不是一根线，而是持续“处于连接状态”这件事，而这正是 -ity 名词所命名的东西。

intro.en: Connectivity is connect plus the adjective suffix -ive and the noun suffix -ity. It began as a general word for the state of being linked and became a technical term with 20c networks. The date of its first general use is not firmly settled.
intro.cn: connectivity 是 connect 加形容词后缀 -ive 再加名词后缀 -ity。它起初泛指“被连接的状态”，20 世纪随网络技术变成术语。它作为普通词的首见年代并无定论。

items.en: The root is nectere 'to bind, tie, join'. With con- 'together', Latin formed connectere 'to bind together'. The image is physical: two things tied, not two things merely near each other.
items.cn: 词根是 nectere“系、绑、连接”。加上 con-“共同”，拉丁语构成 connectere“绑在一起”。意象是物理的：两样东西被系住，而不只是靠得近。

items.en: English connect is recorded in the 17c, coming through French from the Latin verb. It first means 'to join or fasten together', and only later covers abstract links such as ideas and people.
items.cn: 英语 connect 在 17 世纪有记录，经法语来自这个拉丁动词。它最初指“接合、系在一起”，后来才涵盖思想、人等抽象联系。

items.en: The adjective suffix -ive (Latin -ivus) adds the sense 'having the power or tendency to'. Connective therefore means 'having the power to join', and it is the intermediate step before the noun.
items.cn: 形容词后缀 -ive（拉丁 -ivus）加上“具有……的力量或倾向”之意。因此 connective 意为“具有连接力的”，它是名词形成前的中间一步。

items.en: The noun suffix -ity (Latin -itas, stem -itatem) turns that tendency into a state: connectivity is the quality of being connective or connected. The earliest general use is often placed in the 19c, but dictionary dates vary, so this is uncertain.
items.cn: 名词后缀 -ity（拉丁 -itas，词干 -itatem）把这种倾向变成状态：connectivity 就是“具有连接性、处于连接中”的性质。最早的一般用法常被放在 19 世纪，但各家词典标注不一，故此处存疑。

items.en: Telephone and computer networks give the word its modern technical sense in the 20c: the number and quality of links that allow communication. The word now measures a network, not a single join.
items.cn: 电话与计算机网络在 20 世纪赋予这个词现代技术义：允许通信的链路数量与质量。此时它衡量的是一个网络，而不是单次接合。

items.en: In the 21c the term spreads to broadband, satellites, the Internet of Things and social research. It is sold as a service and measured as a social good, so the old binding image now covers both machines and people.
items.cn: 21 世纪这个词扩展到宽带、卫星、物联网和社会研究。它既被当作服务出售，也被当作社会福祉衡量，于是古老的“系在一起”意象同时覆盖机器与人。

note.en: The first group collects words built on the same connect- stem; the second collects words for links, access and reach. Stem first, then meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个 connect- 词干上的词；第二组是表示连接、接入与覆盖范围的词。先看词干，再看词义。

entries.definition: joining things together; as a noun, a word that joins parts of a sentence. It is the -ive step before connectivity, not the state itself.
entries.definitionCN: 起连接作用的；作名词时指连接词。它是 connectivity 之前的 -ive 阶段，而不是状态本身。

entries.definition: the act of connecting, or a link between things or people. It uses -ion, while connectivity uses -ive + -ity for the measurable state.
entries.definitionCN: 连接的动作，或事物、人之间的一条联系。它用 -ion，而 connectivity 用 -ive + -ity 表示可测量的状态。

entries.definition: joined to something, or having social or business links. It describes the thing, while connectivity names the condition.
entries.definitionCN: 与某物相连的，或有社会、业务联系的。它描述事物本身，而 connectivity 命名那种状态。

entries.definition: a connection in which things are linked to one another. It stresses reciprocity, while connectivity can be one-directional reach.
entries.definitionCN: 事物彼此相连的关系。它强调相互性，而 connectivity 可以只是单向的可达。

entries.definition: a system or set of connections between parts. It is more concrete and countable than connectivity.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分之间的一组连接或连接系统。它比 connectivity 更具体、更可数。

entries.definition: the right or ability to enter, use, or reach something. It stresses permission and entry, while connectivity stresses the link itself.
entries.definitionCN: 进入、使用或抵达某物的权利或能力。它强调许可与进入，而 connectivity 强调链路本身。

entries.definition: the area or range within which a service is available. It is about extent, while connectivity is about being linked at all.
entries.definitionCN: 某项服务可用的区域或范围。它关乎范围，而 connectivity 关乎是否连上。

entries.definition: the distance or range over which something can be reached. It measures how far a link extends, a close cousin of connectivity.
entries.definitionCN: 能够触及某物的距离或范围。它衡量一条链路伸得多远，是 connectivity 的近亲。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin nectere 'bind', the real -ive and -ity suffixes, and the real connect / connection / connector family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁语 nectere“系、绑”、真实的后缀 -ive 与 -ity，以及真实的 connect / connection / connector 词族。

normal.en: nectere means 'to bind'. connect = bind together; connectivity = the state of being bound together. Every sense keeps that knot.
normal.cn: nectere 意为“系、绑”。connect = 绑在一起；connectivity = 被绑在一起的状态。每个义项都保留这个绳结。

normal.en: -ive marks the linking power (connective), and -ity turns it into a measurable state (connectivity). The two suffixes explain why the word sounds like a property, not an action.
normal.cn: -ive 标记连接的能力（connective），-ity 把它变成可测量的状态（connectivity）。这两个后缀解释了为什么这个词听起来像一种性质，而不是一个动作。

normal.en: Network connectivity is counted in links and routes: a device is connected when its packets can reach the rest of the net.
normal.cn: 网络连接靠链路与路由来计数：当设备的数据包能抵达网中其余部分时，它才算连着。

normal.en: connectivity issues name the absence by the presence: the word for being linked is used for the failure of the link.
normal.cn: connectivity issues 用“有”的词说“没有”：明明在说链路失效，却用了表示连接的那个词。

normal.en: A satellite connectivity provider sells the state of being linked, not a cable — which is why the -ity noun fits a service.
normal.cn: 卫星连接服务商卖的是“处于连接中”的状态，而不是一根线——这就是为什么 -ity 名词适合描述一项服务。

abstract.en: Picture a fishing net laid flat: each knot is tied to its neighbours, and the whole shape depends on the ties. Connectivity is the net's ability to stay one net.
abstract.cn: 想象一张摊平的渔网：每个结都与邻结相系，整张形状取决于这些系连。connectivity 就是这张网保持为一张网的能力。

abstract.en: The same net appears at every scale: a chip, a server room, a province, a community. The knots change, the binding does not.
abstract.cn: 同一张网出现在每个尺度上：芯片、机房、省份、社群。绳结变了，系绑没变。

abstract.en: Connectivity is relational, not located: no single node owns it, and one broken knot is felt across the whole net.
abstract.cn: connectivity 是关系性的，而不是位于某处的：没有哪个节点独自拥有它，断掉一个结，整张网都会感觉到。

examples.en: The new bridge improved connectivity between the two river towns.
examples.cn: 这座新桥改善了两个河畔城镇之间的连通性。

examples.en: Remote workers reported connectivity problems during the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨期间，远程办公者报告了连接问题。

examples.en: The chip's connectivity features include Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.
examples.cn: 这枚芯片的连接功能包括 Wi-Fi 和蓝牙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「康奈克提维提」：康（con）奈（ne）克（c）提（ti）维（vi）提（ty）——像把康乃馨一枝枝系成一串 → connectivity 连接性；连通性

root: connect（con- 共同 + nectere 系、绑）+ -ive（形容词后缀）+ -ity（名词后缀）；核心是“被绑在一起的状态”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of connectivity, one binding at different scales: two cables, a network, a province, a mesh of sensors, a community, a product, or a service. The knot is always the same.
sensesIntro.cn: connectivity 的九个义项，是同一个“系绑”在不同尺度上的样子：两根线缆、一张网络、一个省份、一张传感器网、一个社群、一件产品或一项服务。绳结始终是同一个。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: knots tied to one another in a net, so that every point can reach every other.
core.cn: 核心意象：网中绳结彼此相系，使每个点都能抵达其他点。

branches.en: STATE AND NETWORK: the general condition of being tied becomes a measurable property of a whole network.
branches.cn: 状态与网络：一般的“被系住”变成整个网络的可测属性。

branches.en: INTERNET AND FAILURE: reachability to the internet, and the same word used for the failure of that reachability.
branches.cn: 互联网与故障：接入公网的可达性，以及用同一个词指这种可达性的失效。

branches.en: PLACES AND DEVICES: routes bind towns, links bind sensors; the net is drawn on a map or on a circuit board.
branches.cn: 地点与设备：路线把城镇系起来，链路把传感器系起来；这张网可以画在地图上，也可以画在电路板上。

branches.en: SOCIETY: relationships replace cables, and the density of human ties is measured as social connectivity.
branches.cn: 社会：关系取代线缆，人与人之间纽带的密度被衡量为社会连接度。

branches.en: TECHNOLOGY AND SERVICE: the state becomes a feature built into hardware, and then a service sold by a provider.
branches.cn: 技术与服务：这种状态先变成硬件内置的功能，再变成服务商出售的服务。

intro.en: Connectivity shows a three-step suffix chain: connect (verb) → connective (-ive) → connectivity (-ity). Each step changes the word from an action to a tendency to a state, which is why the noun never sounds like a single event.
intro.cn: connectivity 展示了一条三步后缀链：connect（动词）→ connective（-ive）→ connectivity（-ity）。每一步都把词从动作变成倾向，再变成状态，所以这个名词从不像一次单独事件。

latinIntro.en: Latin nectere 'to bind' gives connectere 'bind together', and the suffix -ivus gives the adjective sense 'able to bind'. The -itas noun then names that ability as a condition. The same nectere appears in annex and nexus, so the root reaches beyond the connect- words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nectere“系、绑”给出 connectere“绑在一起”，后缀 -ivus 给出“能绑”的形容词义。-itas 名词再把这种能力命名为一种状况。同一个 nectere 也出现在 annex 与 nexus 中，因此这个词根超出 connect- 系列。

senses.title: Happening every two years
senses.definition: occurring once every two years
senses.definitionCN: 每两年发生一次
senses.example: The city hosts a biennial art exhibition.
senses.exampleCN: 该市每两年举办一届艺术展。
senses.why: Latin bi- means two and annus means year, so the word counts years by twos.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 bi- 指「二」，annus 指「年」，合起来即「隔两年」。

senses.title: Lasting two years
senses.definition: continuing for a period of two years
senses.definitionCN: 为期两年的
senses.example: The assembly approved a biennial budget.
senses.exampleCN: 议会批准了两年期预算。
senses.why: Not the rhythm of return but the length of span.
senses.whyCN: 不是往复的节奏，而是一段跨度。

senses.title: Of plants living two years
senses.definition: of a plant that takes two years to complete its life cycle
senses.definitionCN: 指用两个生长季完成生命周期的植物
senses.example: Carrots are biennial, flowering in their second year.
senses.exampleCN: 胡萝卜是二年生植物，第二年才开花。
senses.why: Botany borrowed the two-year count for plant lifespans.
senses.whyCN: 植物学借「两年」之数来记植物寿命。

senses.title: A biennial event
senses.definition: a large recurring event held every second year, especially in art
senses.definitionCN: 每两年举办一次的大型活动，多指艺术界
senses.example: The biennial drew curators from forty countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这届双年展吸引了四十个国家的策展人。
senses.why: The adjective hardens into the name of the event itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词凝固为活动本身的名字。

senses.title: A biennial plant
senses.definition: a plant completing its cycle in two growing seasons
senses.definitionCN: 在两个生长季内完成周期的植物
senses.example: The nursery stocks hardy biennials for autumn sowing.
senses.exampleCN: 苗圃备有耐寒二年生植物供秋播。
senses.why: The botanical sense likewise becomes a noun.
senses.whyCN: 植物义同样转为名词。

senses.title: Recurring in alternate years (of sessions)
senses.definition: of meetings or sessions held in alternate years
senses.definitionCN: 指会议、届会隔年举行
senses.example: The society's biennial congress falls in odd years.
senses.exampleCN: 该学会的大会逢单数年召开。
senses.why: Institutional rhythm adopts the two-year beat.
senses.whyCN: 机构的节拍采纳了两年一拍。

senses.title: Of terms of office or reports
senses.definition: covering or valid for a two-year term
senses.definitionCN: 任期或有效期为两年
senses.example: Her biennial term on the board ends next spring.
senses.exampleCN: 她的两年董事会任期明年春天届满。
senses.why: The two-year span applies to tenure and documents.
senses.whyCN: 两年跨度同样适用于任期与文件。

senses.title: Contrasted with annual and perennial
senses.definition: in classification, standing between one-year and many-year cycles
senses.definitionCN: 在分类上介于一年生与多年生之间
senses.example: Gardeners sort seeds into annuals, biennials, and perennials.
senses.exampleCN: 园艺师把种子分为一年生、二年生与多年生。
senses.why: The word fills the middle rung of a time ladder.
senses.whyCN: 该词补上时间阶梯的中间一档。

definition_zh: 置信区间
definition_en: a range of values calculated from sample data that is expected to contain the true parameter at a stated confidence level over repeated sampling
core_image: 一条横轴，中间一个点估计，左右各伸出一段，被一只括号围住，括号两端标着刻度
scene: 黑板上一条横轴，中间一个点，左右各伸出一段，被一只括号围住，括号两端标着刻度。 A confidence interval shows the range that repeated samples would usually bracket.
sceneCN: 这里指围绕估计值给出的参数范围（第 1 个义项：由样本算出的参数区间）；句意为置信区间显示反复抽样通常会框住的数值范围。图中可辨识物件：横轴、点估计、左右区间、括号、刻度。

pos.zh: 置信区间

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 confidere「信任」经法语而来，义为「信心；置信」
由其形容词形式而来，义为「有信心的」

senses.title: A range built around an estimate
senses.titleCN: 围绕估计值构造的范围
senses.definition: an interval computed from sample data so that it is likely to contain the unknown parameter
senses.definitionCN: 由样本数据算出、很可能包含未知参数的区间
senses.example: A confidence interval shows the range that repeated samples would usually bracket.
senses.exampleCN: 置信区间显示反复抽样通常会框住的数值范围。
senses.why: A single number hides its own uncertainty, so the interval gives the uncertainty a visible width.
senses.whyCN: 单个数字把自己的不确定性藏了起来，区间则给这份不确定性一个可见的宽度。

senses.title: The long-run coverage interpretation
senses.definition: the interpretation that, across many repeated samples, the stated proportion of such intervals will contain the true value
senses.definitionCN: 在大量重复抽样中，所述比例的区间会包含真值的解释
senses.example: A ninety-five per cent confidence interval does not mean a ninety-five per cent chance for this one interval.
senses.exampleCN: 百分之九十五的置信区间并不意味着这一个区间有百分之九十五的概率包含真值。
senses.why: The confidence belongs to the procedure that builds intervals, not to any single interval after it is built.
senses.whyCN: 信心属于构造区间的程序，而不属于建成之后的某一个区间。

senses.title: The confidence level
senses.definition: the stated proportion, usually ninety-five or ninety-nine per cent, attached to the procedure
senses.definitionCN: 附在程序上的所述比例，通常为百分之九十五或九十九
senses.example: Raising the confidence level widens the interval for the same data.
senses.exampleCN: 在数据相同的情况下，提高置信水平会使区间变宽。
senses.why: More confidence requires a wider net, and a wider net catches more but says less about where the value lies.
senses.whyCN: 更高的信心需要更宽的网，网更宽能兜住更多，却更难说清值在哪里。

senses.title: The margin around the point estimate
senses.definition: the distance from the estimate to each end of the interval, often built from a standard error and a multiplier
senses.definitionCN: 从估计值到区间两端的距离，常由标准误与倍数构成
senses.example: The confidence interval is the estimate plus and minus its margin.
senses.exampleCN: 置信区间就是估计值加减这段幅度。
senses.why: The interval is a point with two arms, and the arms carry the uncertainty the point cannot carry alone.
senses.whyCN: 区间是一个带两条臂的点，两条臂承载着点无法独自承载的不确定性。

senses.title: An interval for a difference
senses.definition: a range for the difference between two groups, used to judge whether the difference could plausibly be zero
senses.definitionCN: 两组差值所在的区间，用来判断差值是否可能为零
senses.example: The confidence interval for the difference included zero, so the effect was not established.
senses.exampleCN: 差值的置信区间包含零，因此效应尚未确立。
senses.why: A difference is itself an estimate, and its interval shows which directions and sizes remain plausible.
senses.whyCN: 差值本身也是一个估计，它的区间显示哪些方向与大小仍然可能。

senses.title: Interval versus credible interval
senses.titleCN: 置信区间与可信区间的区别
senses.definition: the contrast between a frequentist coverage interval and a Bayesian interval that carries a posterior probability
senses.definitionCN: 频率学派的覆盖率区间与带有后验概率的贝叶斯区间之间的对照
senses.example: A Bayesian credible interval answers a question that a confidence interval does not.
senses.exampleCN: 贝叶斯可信区间回答了一个置信区间不回答的问题。
senses.why: The two intervals can look alike on the page, but their probabilities are attached to different objects.
senses.whyCN: 两种区间在纸面上可能相似，但它们的概率附着在不同对象上。

senses.title: Width as a measure of precision
senses.definition: the way a narrower interval indicates a more precise estimate, usually because of a larger sample or less variation
senses.definitionCN: 区间越窄表示估计越精确，通常因为样本更大或变异更小
senses.example: The confidence interval narrowed after the second wave of data collection.
senses.exampleCN: 第二轮数据收集之后，置信区间变窄了。
senses.why: Width is the visible form of precision, and precision is bought with information.
senses.whyCN: 宽度是精确度的可见形式，而精确度是用信息换来的。

senses.title: Reading overlap between intervals
senses.definition: the practice of comparing two intervals to judge the plausibility of a difference, with care about what overlap does and does not prove
senses.definitionCN: 比较两个区间以判断差值是否可能，并注意重叠能证明什么、不能证明什么
senses.example: Overlapping confidence intervals do not by themselves prove that there is no difference.
senses.exampleCN: 置信区间重叠本身并不证明没有差异。
senses.why: Two wide intervals may overlap while the difference between their centres remains real.
senses.whyCN: 两个宽区间可以重叠，而它们中心之间的差异仍然真实存在。

intro.en: Confidence interval joins confidence, from Latin confidere, to trust fully, to interval, from Latin intervallum, the space between ramparts.
intro.cn: 这个术语把来自拉丁语 confidere「完全信任」的 confidence，与来自拉丁语 intervallum「城墙之间的空地」的 interval 组合起来。

items.en: Confidere meant to trust completely, from con- fully and fidere to trust.
items.cn: confidere 意为完全信任，由 con-「完全」与 fidere「信任」构成。

items.en: Confidentia named assurance or boldness, and English took it as confidence.
items.cn: confidentia 指确信或胆量，英语借入为 confidence。

items.en: Vallum meant a rampart or wall, and intervallum named the ground between two walls.
items.cn: vallum 指城墙或壁垒，intervallum 指两道墙之间的空地。

items.en: The noun widened from a space between walls to any gap in time or space.
items.cn: 这个名词从「墙间空地」扩展到时间或空间中的任何间隔。

items.en: English used interval for a gap and later for a set of values between two limits; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语用 interval 指间隔，后来指两个界限之间的一组取值；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Twentieth-century statistics joined the two nouns for a procedure-based range, and the exact origin of the phrase is debated.
items.cn: 二十世纪统计学把这两个名词组合成一种基于程序的区间，这个短语的确切起源仍有争议。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like confidence interval; the second group names neighbouring quantities in estimation.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 confidence interval 相近；第二组是与「估计量」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: Trust or assurance in a procedure or person.
entries.definitionCN: 指对程序或人的信任与把握。

entries.definition: Feeling sure about something.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某事感到有把握。

entries.definition: To trust someone with private information.
entries.definitionCN: 指把私密信息托付给某人。

entries.definition: A gap, or a set of values between two limits.
entries.definitionCN: 指间隔，或两界限之间的一组取值。

entries.definition: To come between; it looks close but its root is venire, to come.
entries.definitionCN: 指介入其间；形近但词根是 venire「来」。

entries.definition: The standard deviation of an estimate across repeated samples.
entries.definitionCN: 指估计量在反复抽样中的标准差。

entries.definition: A Bayesian range carrying a posterior probability.
entries.definitionCN: 指带有后验概率的贝叶斯区间。

entries.definition: The half-width of a survey interval around an estimate.
entries.definitionCN: 指调查中估计值两侧区间的半宽。

entries.definition: A single value used to estimate a parameter.
entries.definitionCN: 指用来估计参数的单个值。

entries.definition: The difference between the largest and smallest observed values.
entries.definitionCN: 指观测值中最大值与最小值之差。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations work through the real parts, word family and common phrases behind this term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依托这个术语背后真实的构词部件、同族词与常见搭配。

normal.en: Confidence is trust, and interval is the ground between two walls, so the phrase names a trusted space between two limits.
normal.cn: 「信心」是信任，「区间」是两墙之间的空地，这个短语指两条界限之间一块受信任的空间。

normal.en: Ninety-five per cent confidence means the procedure covers the truth in ninety-five per cent of repeated samples.
normal.cn: 百分之九十五置信意味着这套程序在反复抽样中百分之九十五的情况下盖住真值。

normal.en: A wider interval is more confident and less precise at the same time.
normal.cn: 更宽的区间同时更自信也更不精确。

normal.en: An interval that includes zero leaves the possibility of no difference open.
normal.cn: 包含零的区间使「没有差异」这一可能保持开放。

normal.en: A credible interval and a confidence interval can share a shape but not a meaning.
normal.cn: 可信区间与置信区间可以形状相同，含义却不同。

abstract.en: An interval is a net thrown around an unknown fish, and confidence describes the net, not the fish.
abstract.cn: 区间是撒向未知之鱼的一张网，信心描述的是网，而不是鱼。

abstract.en: The single number is a dot; the interval is the shadow the dot casts when uncertainty is the light.
abstract.cn: 单个数字是一个点，区间是当不确定性成为光源时那个点投下的影子。

abstract.en: Two intervals may overlap like two conversations in a corridor, without either speaker agreeing.
abstract.cn: 两个区间可以像走廊里的两段对话那样重叠，而两位说话者并未达成一致。

examples.en: The paper reports a confidence interval for every estimated coefficient.
examples.cn: 论文为每个估计系数报告了置信区间。

examples.en: A confidence interval that includes zero suggests the effect may be absent.
examples.cn: 包含零的置信区间提示效应可能不存在。

examples.en: The confidence interval was wide because the sample was small.
examples.cn: 由于样本小，置信区间很宽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「置信」加「区间」——一个点不够，给它左右各伸一条臂，圈出一个可能范围：置信区间。

root: 拉丁 confidere「完全信任」← con-「完全」+ fidere「信任」→ confidentia → 英语 confidence；拉丁 vallum「城墙」→ intervallum「墙间空地」→ 英语 interval；二十世纪统计学把两者组合为置信区间。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from construction to reading: the range around an estimate, long-run coverage, the confidence level, the margin, intervals for differences, the contrast with credible intervals, width as precision, and the reading of overlap.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从构造走向解读：围绕估计值的区间、长期覆盖率、置信水平、两侧幅度、差值区间、与可信区间的区别、宽度即精确度，以及区间重叠的解读。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a horizontal axis with a point in the middle, arms extending both ways, and a bracket closing around the arms.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条横轴，中间一个点，左右各伸出一条臂，一只括号把两条臂围住。

branches.en: THE BUILT RANGE: an estimate with two arms, each arm carrying uncertainty.
branches.cn: 构造的范围：一个带两条臂的估计，每条臂承载不确定性。

branches.en: THE PROCEDURE'S PROMISE: long-run coverage, and the confidence level that states it.
branches.cn: 程序的承诺：长期覆盖率，以及陈述它的置信水平。

branches.en: THE DIFFERENCE: an interval that can include zero and leave no effect established.
branches.cn: 差值：一个可以包含零、使效应无法确立的区间。

branches.en: THE ALTERNATIVE AND THE PRECISION: a Bayesian interval beside it, and width as visible precision.
branches.cn: 替代与精确：旁边的贝叶斯区间，以及作为可见精确度的宽度。

branches.en: THE COMPARISON: overlap read with care about what it does not prove.
branches.cn: 比较：谨慎解读重叠不能证明什么。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin-derived noun for trust to a Latin-derived noun for the space between walls.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁来源的「信任」名词与拉丁来源的「墙间空地」名词组合起来。

latinIntro.en: Latin con- and fidere supply confidence; inter and vallum supply interval; the statistical compound is twentieth-century.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 con- 与 fidere 提供「信心」，inter 与 vallum 提供「区间」，统计学的复合用法属二十世纪。
